Après la Conquête, des notables anglopho: After the Conquest, English-speaking notables, including James Murray and Samuel Holland, bought the estates left by the French elite. In the early 19th century, the English-speaking bourgeoisie owned large villas there, far from the sanitation problems of the city. As early as 1833, the Faubourg Guénette and its modest dwellings took shape between Avenues Bourlamaque, Crémazie and Cartier.
Après la Seconde Guerre mondiale, indust: After the Second World War, industries and homes multiplied. La Petite-Rivière became Duberger in 1964, and Québec-Ouest took the name Vanier in 1966, in honour of Governor General Georges Vanier. Between 1970 and 1973, Québec City annexed Duberger, Les Saules, Neufchâtel and Charlesbourg-Ouest.
Après la guerre de 1812, des soldats ang: After the War of 1812, English soldiers were granted land in the eastern part of Frampton Township, then called East Frampton. They resold it to Gilbert Henderson (1785-1876), who granted it to Irish immigrants. The area had a few inhabitants in 1823.
Après le Grand Dérangement de 1755, des: After the Great Upheaval of 1755, Acadians, mostly from Beaubassin and Île Saint-Jean, were welcomed on the lands of the seigneur Michel-Jean-Hugues Péan de Livaudière, in the parish of Saint-Charles-Borromée. In 1756, lands of the Première Cadie were assigned to them. French Canadians and a few British settlers joined them later.

After the Great Upheaval of 1755, Acadian families settled from 1756 on lands called the Première Cadie. Before the parish opened in 1780, this place, named Nouvelle-Cadie, brought together about sixty Acadian families.

After the Great Upheaval of 1755, Acadian families settled in Saint-Gervais, and their descendants cleared the land of the future Saint-Raphaël. In 1839, about forty landowners asked for a parish to be created. A mission was opened, served by the priest of Saint-Gervais.
Après le départ des troupes britanniques: After the British troops left in 1871, Governor General Lord Dufferin launched major projects to preserve the historic character of the city. The name "Vieux-Québec" spread with the historian Pierre-Georges Roy's book, published in 1931.
Après plus de trois semaines de retard,: After more than three weeks of delay, you can ask the TAL to terminate the lease and recover the rent. We prepare the file and submit it to you before any filing.
Armagh a le plus grand territoire de la: Armagh has the largest territory in the Bellechasse MRC. It touches Saint-Raphaël to the northwest, Saint-Damien-de-Buckland to the southwest and Saint-Philémon to the southeast. The Rivière de la Fourche joins the Rivière du Sud there, southeast of the village, and the Armagh River flows down from the Massif du Sud basin.

Attendez que la demande soit <strong>est: Wait until the application has been stamped by the TAL before serving it on the tenant[3].
Au Parc des Chutes d’Armagh, 5 km de sen: At the Parc des Chutes d’Armagh, 5 km of trails run along the river, and a 70 m viaduct spans it. The park is home to the Musée de la Gare, set in a 1916 train station, and the remains of a hydroelectric plant. It marks one end of the 74 km Cycloroute de Bellechasse.
Au Québec, le loyer est <strong>en retar: In Québec, rent is late the day after the payment date: the landlord can then claim the amounts owed from the TAL[2]. After more than three weeks of delay, the landlord can also apply to terminate the lease[1]. The tenant avoids termination by paying, before judgment, the rent owed, interest and costs[1]. The application fee is $92 since April 1, 2026[3].
Au Québec, le propriétaire ne peut exige: In Québec, a landlord can only require the first month’s rent in advance. Any other amount is prohibited: security deposit, key deposit, last month’s rent or required postdated cheques[1][2]. A lease clause providing for a deposit has no effect[1], and the tenant can ask the TAL for a refund.
Au Québec, seul le premier mois de loyer: In Québec, only the first month’s rent can be required in advance (C.C.Q., art. 1904). Security deposits, key deposits, imposed postdated cheques and application fees are prohibited; a sum collected this way is refundable with interest.
Au Québec, un logement se désigne souven: In Québec, a unit is often described by its number of rooms, with the bathroom counting as a half: a 4 ½ has four rooms and a bathroom.
Au Québec, un propriétaire peut demander: In Québec, a landlord can ask for the name, address and contact information of the applicant’s former landlords. With the applicant’s consent, the landlord can run a credit check, which requires only the name, address and date of birth[1]. The landlord cannot require the SIN, a bank account number, pay stubs, health information or copies of identity documents[1][2].
Au Québec, un propriétaire peut reprendr: In Québec, a landlord can repossess a unit for themselves or a relative by giving written notice, generally 6 months before the lease ends[1]. The tenant has one month to respond and silence counts as refusal; the landlord must then apply to the TAL within the month[1][3]. Evictions to enlarge, subdivide or change the use of a dwelling are suspended until June 6, 2027[2].
Au XIXe siècle, la chute Montmorency fou: In the 19th century, the Montmorency Falls supplied power to several businesses, including the Patterson sawmill, a Dominion Textile mill and a hydroelectric plant. In the early 20th century, the Montmorency-Charlevoix railway linked the industries of Sault-Montmorency to Québec City.
Au XIXe siècle, la compagnie John Breake: In the 19th century, the company John Breakey Reg’d, founded by Hans Denaston Breakey (1811-1860), handled the cutting, log driving and sawing of timber in the Chaudière basin. In 1908, the parish was canonically erected after being split from Saint-Jean-Chrysostome. It took the name Sainte-Hélène-de-Breakeyville, in honour of Helen Henderson and her husband, the lumber merchant John Breakey (1846-1911).
Au XIXe siècle, le commerce du bois fait: In the 19th century, the timber trade sustained the area. Saint-Romuald separated from Saint-Jean-Chrysostome in 1855, and its Chaudière-Bassin district became known for timber and shipbuilding. In 1859, Hans Denaston Breakey built a sawmill just upstream of the Chaudière Falls, on a site then called Chaudière Mills.
Au XIXe siècle, les anses de Sillery viv: In the 19th century, the coves of Sillery lived off the timber trade and shipbuilding, and notables built villas there. Sainte-Foy (1855), Saint-Colomb de Sillery (1856) and Saint-Félix-du-Cap-Rouge (1872) became municipalities. The Cap-Rouge trestle was completed in 1908, and the Québec Bridge connected Sainte-Foy to the South Shore in 1917.
Au XIXe siècle, sa population en faisait: In the 19th century, its population made it the capital of the island. The Manoir Mauvide-Genest, built in 1734, has been a classified heritage site since 1971 and a National Historic Site of Canada since 1993. It houses an interpretation centre on the seigneurial regime. The church, built between 1734 and 1737 on the riverbank, has been classified since 1957.
Au XIXe siècle, seuls quelques agriculte: In the 19th century, only a few Irish farmers lived around the lake. In 1833, about thirty Irish families, who had arrived from Connecticut in 1817, occupied the southeastern area of the lake. The town’s name pays tribute to Jacques Nau de La Boissière et de Fossambault, King’s counsellor and treasurer of finances in Berry.
Au XXe siècle, Saint-Sauveur reste un qu: In the 20th century, Saint-Sauveur remained a working-class neighbourhood. In 1914, the Laiterie de Québec, the future Laiterie Arctic, was the first in the city to pasteurize its milk. More recently, the railway that cut the neighbourhood off from Parc Victoria was removed in 1974, Boulevard Charest was redeveloped from 2006 to 2008 and the banks of the Saint-Charles River were renaturalized in 2007.
Au besoin, il vous oriente vers le TAL,: When needed, it directs you to the TAL, Éducaloi, a housing committee, an owners’ association, a lawyer or a notary.
Au centre de Lévis, entre la rivière Cha: In central Lévis, between the Rivière Chaudière and the Rivière Etchemin. Saint-Romuald borders the St. Lawrence River at the foot of the Pont de Québec, and Avenue Taniata (Route 275) leads to Saint-Jean-Chrysostome.
Au centre de la MRC de Bellechasse, en C: In the centre of the MRC de Bellechasse, in Chaudière-Appalaches, 23 km south of Saint-Vallier. The municipality lies between Saint-Raphaël to the north and Saint-Damien-de-Buckland to the southeast.
In the centre of the MRC de Bellechasse, in Chaudière-Appalaches, about thirty minutes from Lévis. The municipality is the seat of the MRC.
Au centre de la MRC de Portneuf, dans la: In the centre of the MRC de Portneuf, in the Capitale-Nationale region, 25 km north of Donnacona. It is sometimes called Saint-Raymond-de-Portneuf.
In the centre of the MRC de Portneuf, in the Sainte-Anne River valley, 25 km north of Donnacona. Routes 354, 365 and 367 cross its territory.
Au centre géographique de la ville de Qu: At the geographic centre of Québec City, on both sides of the Rivière Saint-Charles. Boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel crosses it from east to west, and several highways intersect there, including Félix-Leclerc, Laurentienne and Robert-Bourassa.
Au centre-nord de la ville, près des aut: In the north-central part of the city, near the Laurentienne and Félix-Leclerc highways. The Galeries de la Capitale are located here.
Au cimetière de Saint-Pierre-de-l’Île-d’: In the Saint-Pierre-de-l’Île-d’Orléans cemetery, where he lived his last years. The Espace Félix-Leclerc, at the entrance to the village, presents his work and gives access to hiking trails.
Au cours de l’hiver 1923-1924, Eugène Pr: During the winter of 1923-1924, Eugène Prévost built a first bus in his workshop in the village. His company employed more than 200 people in 1951, took the name Prevost Car in 1957 and is now owned by Volvo. Sainte-Claire and Louis-Joliette merged in 1977 to form the current municipality.
Au cœur de la MRC de Bellechasse, en Cha: In the heart of the Bellechasse RCM, in Chaudière-Appalaches, about 9 km northeast of Saint-Anselme. The municipality is bordered by Saint-Gervais, Saint-Lazare-de-Bellechasse and Sainte-Claire.
Au cœur de la MRC de Portneuf, à quelque: In the heart of the Portneuf MRC, a few kilometres south of Saint-Raymond, between Pont-Rouge and Portneuf. The town is less than 35 minutes from Québec City.
In the heart of the Portneuf MRC, a few kilometres south of Saint-Raymond. The Portneuf River crosses the territory, and Route 365 passes through it between Pont-Rouge and Saint-Raymond.
Au début des années 1920, le Sault compt: In the early 1920s, Le Sault had about 550 residents, a third of the population of L’Ange-Gardien, of which it was part. On April 3, 1920, it became the municipality of Saint-Jean-de-Boischatel, named in honour of Jean-François de Beauchatel, first aide-de-camp to General Montcalm.
Au début des années 1920, le moulin de s: In the early 1920s, the Breakey family sawmill employed many workers, and log driving supported several families during the Depression of the 1930s. The mill closed as log driving declined and transportation modernized. On January 1, 2002, Breakeyville was merged into Lévis and became a sector of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough.
Au début des années 1960, quelques domai: In the early 1960s, a few estates were subdivided to build houses, and Boulevard Champlain led to the destruction of several houses in the former working-class villages. The Sillery historic district was created in 1964. The city became the Ville de Sillery on May 31, 1980, then was integrated into Québec City on January 1, 2002.
Au début des années 1960, une école cent: In the early 1960s, a centralized school was built near the church and welcomed students from 1963. Issoudun has been twinned with the French town of Issoudun since 1977. The Nature-Environnement committee developed the La Tourbière trail in 2010, and the steam mill, more than a century old, still operates on occasion.
Au début des années 1970, l’autoroute Du: In the early 1970s, Autoroute Dufferin-Montmorency was built on the mudflats and cut the area off from the river. On January 1, 1976, Courville, Villeneuve and Montmorency were merged into Beauport; the cotton mill closed in the 1980s. In 2002, when Beauport was annexed to Québec City, these former villages were grouped together to form the Chutes-Montmorency neighbourhood.
Au début des années 1990, la ville conna: In the early 1990s, the city grew strongly under the slogan "Val-Bélair, ville de la nature." Its population rose from 11,000 in 1971 to more than 22,000 in 2002. On January 1, 2002, Val-Bélair was merged with Québec City; first part of the Laurentien borough, it has been part of La Haute-Saint-Charles since 2009. In 2004, remaining in Québec City won narrowly in a referendum, with 50.24% of the vote.
Au début des années 1990, une associatio: In the early 1990s, a lake protection association began working to protect the Marais du Nord, whose first trails opened in 1995. Lac-Saint-Charles became a town in 1997, then was merged with Québec City in 2002 and made part of the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough. That same year, part of the marshes became one of the first three private nature reserves in Québec.
Au début des années 2000, l’étalement ur: In the early 2000s, Québec City's urban sprawl reached Sainte-Brigitte-de-Laval, which bet on residential development. Dozens of streets were opened to welcome new homes. The municipality obtained town status on December 8, 2012.
Au début du Régime français, les basses: At the start of the French Regime, the lowlands bordering the Saint-Charles River formed the common lands. In 1618, Champlain proposed founding a town there named “Ludovica,” a project abandoned around 1638. In 1653, Jean Le Sueur, the first secular priest of New France, nicknamed “Monsieur de Saint-Sauveur,” received land between today's Rue Durocher and Rue Montmagny: the neighbourhood owes him its name.
Au début du XIXe siècle, des colons s’ét: In the early 19th century, settlers established themselves on the banks of the Rivière Jaune, where it crossed the road to Stoneham Township; the locality took the name Rivière-Jaune. The notable George Muir, who spent his summers there, acquired a lot in 1869. He funded a convent for the Sœurs du Bon-Pasteur in 1871, then a chapel in 1875, still standing.
Au début du XIXe siècle, le blocus conti: In the early 19th century, Napoleon's Continental Blockade pushed Great Britain to seek timber in its colonies. Henry Caldwell, who acquired the seigneury in 1801, and then his son John had wharves, basins and sawmills built on the Etchemin islets. The first bridge over the Etchemin was built in 1818, and shipbuilding became the main employer until the 1930s.
Au début du XIXe siècle, une poterie, un: In the early 19th century, a pottery, a forge, a brickyard and the timber trade fostered growth. In 1859, the residents obtained a chapel, named Saint-Félix in honour of Vicar General Charles-Félix Cazeau. The parish was established in 1862, and the church was completed in 1864. In 1872, the municipality of the parish of Saint-Félix-du-Cap-Rouge was created, with Joseph Bell Forsyth as its first mayor.
Au début du XVIIe siècle, les peuples de: In the early 17th century, the peoples of the Wendat confederacy lived in Huronia, southeast of Lake Huron, in present-day Ontario. They grew corn, squash and beans, and hunted and fished. Their trading network extended around Lakes Huron, Ontario and Erie.
Au début du XXe siècle, le village se sé: In the early 20th century, the village separated from the parish. Electricity arrived on October 23, 1923, and the arena was built in 1980 thanks to subscriptions and the work of many volunteers. In 1993, the village and the parish were reunited to form the municipality of Saint-Charles-de-Bellechasse.
Au début du XXe siècle, une quarantaine: At the start of the 20th century, about forty families lived off subsistence farming. In the 1930s, alpine skiing changed everything: a first chairlift was installed in 1938 at Mont Saint-Castin. The village became a leisure destination for Québec City residents, and the population grew quickly from the 1970s on.
Au fil du temps, le secteur reste boisé: Over time, the area remained wooded in the north and agricultural in the south. In 1917, the municipality of Saint-Charles-de-Charlesbourg-Est split from Saint-Charles-de-Charlesbourg; it took the name Charlesbourg-Est in 1927. The current neighbourhood follows the boundaries of this former municipality, which joined the new city of Charlesbourg on January 1, 1976. Maurice Légacé, from 1953 to 1966, then Marcel Paradis, until 1975, were its last mayors.
Au milieu du XIXe siècle, le territoire: In the mid-19th century, the Saint-Sacrement area was occupied by farms and country estates, mostly owned by the bourgeoisie of British origin. The mayor of Québec City, George O'Kill Stuart, lived at Holland House, a large property bordering the future Avenue Holland. Not far away, the Congregation of Notre Dame opened a convent on the Bellevue estate in 1874. Chemin Sainte-Foy, laid out in the 17th century, already crossed the area.

In the mid-19th century, the territory was organized as a parish municipality under the name Saint-Ambroise-de-la-Jeune-Lorette. Over time, several village centres split off from it, including Loretteville in 1913. The remaining lands, mostly agricultural, kept the name Saint-Ambroise. Urban expansion began to reach the area in the 1950s.
Au milieu du XVIIIe siècle, un premier f: In the mid-18th century, a first faubourg, the future Saint-Roch, housed artisans and workers outside the walls. The Faubourg Saint-Jean was urbanized starting in the 1780s, and both were integrated into the city in 1792. In the 19th century, fires, including those of 1845 and 1866, levelled faubourgs that were then rebuilt.
Au milieu du XXe siècle, le territoire e: In the mid-20th century, the territory was carved up by the creation of Lac-Saint-Charles in 1946, Charlesbourg-Ouest in 1952 and Orsainville in 1953. In 1965, Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides obtained city status. The area has kept a low-density settlement pattern, mostly on flat land in the south and in the valleys between the hills.

Au nord de Québec, au pied des Laurentid: North of Québec City, at the foot of the Laurentians, in the Jacques-Cartier River valley. Homes are concentrated along the river and Route 371.
Au nord de Québec, dans la MRC de La Jac: North of Québec City, in the La Jacques-Cartier RCM. The municipality borders the Charlesbourg and Beauport boroughs to the south, Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury to the north and Sainte-Brigitte-de-Laval to the east.
North of Québec City, in the La Jacques-Cartier MRC. The town borders the Lac-Saint-Charles sector of Québec City to the south and Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury to the northeast.
Au nord de Québec, dans les Laurentides,: North of Québec City, in the Laurentians, just above the Charlesbourg and Beauport boroughs. Lac Beauport, in the south of the territory, gives it its name.
North of Québec City, in the Laurentians, along Route 175 to Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean. The Station touristique Stoneham and part of the Parc national de la Jacques-Cartier are in its territory.
Au nord de Québec, entre le secteur de L: North of Québec City, between the Lac-Saint-Charles sector and Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury. The town surrounds Lac Delage, in wooded terrain with sometimes steep slopes.
Au nord de Québec, à environ 25 km du ce: North of Québec City, about 25 km from downtown, in the La Jacques-Cartier MRC. The municipality borders the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough of Québec City to the south.
Au nord de la rivière Saint-Charles. La: North of the Rivière Saint-Charles. 3e Avenue is its commercial artery.
Au nord de la ville. Son cœur historique: In the north of the city. Its historic heart, the Trait-Carré, preserves the 17th-century star-shaped layout.
Au nord de l’arrondissement de Beauport,: In the north of the Beauport borough, between Boulevard Louis-XIV and Lac-Beauport, as far as the Montmorency River. Avenue Sainte-Thérèse and Boulevard Raymond are the main routes; the Centre de plein air de Beauport borders the river.
Au nord de l’arrondissement de Charlesbo: In the north of the Charlesbourg borough, at the foot of the Laurentians. The Laurentienne highway, Boulevard Henri-Bourassa and Boulevard du Lac run through it from south to north; the Rivière Jaune and wooded hills mark the area.
Au nord de l’arrondissement de La Cité-L: In the north of the La Cité-Limoilou borough, in the southeast quadrant formed by the Félix-Leclerc and Laurentienne highways. 1re Avenue is its commercial artery; the ExpoCité site, with the Centre Vidéotron and the Grand Marché de Québec, occupies its southwest corner.
Au nord-est de Québec, dans la vallée de: Northeast of Québec City, in the Montmorency River valley. Avenue Sainte-Brigitte runs through it from north to south and forms its only direct access to Québec City.
Au nord-est de l’arrondissement de Charl: In the northeast of the Charlesbourg borough, between the farming zone and Mont Reine-Malouin. Avenue du Bourg-Royal crosses it from north to south; its star-shaped streets converge on the Carré de Tracy.
Au nord-ouest de Québec, autour de la pa: Northwest of Québec City, around the southern part of Lac Saint-Joseph. Route de Fossambault runs along the lake and through the town.
Au nord-ouest de Québec, dans la MRC de: Northwest of Québec City, in the La Jacques-Cartier RCM, around the southern part of Lac Saint-Joseph. The town borders Sainte-Catherine-de-la-Jacques-Cartier, Shannon and Lac-Saint-Joseph.
Northwest of Québec City, in the La Jacques-Cartier MRC. The town borders Lac Saint-Joseph to the west, north and east, while Fossambault-sur-le-Lac occupies the southeast part.
Au nord-ouest de Québec, sur les rives o: Northwest of Québec City, on the west, north and east shores of Lac Saint-Joseph. Chemin Thomas-Maher goes around the lake within the town’s territory.
Au nord-ouest de la ville de Québec, dan: In the northwest of Québec City, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough, around Jean-Lesage International Airport. It borders the town of L’Ancienne-Lorette.
Au nord-ouest de la ville, autour de l’a: In the northwest of the city, around Jean-Lesage International Airport. Boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel and Boulevard Chauveau-Ouest serve its residential areas; the Sainte-Foy outdoor base and vast farmland are found here.
Au nord-ouest du centre-ville de Québec,: Northwest of downtown Québec City, in the upper part of the Saint-Charles River basin. The borough includes Loretteville, Val-Bélair, Lac-Saint-Charles, Saint-Émile and Des Châtels.
Au parc des Chutes-de-la-Chaudière, acce: At Parc des Chutes-de-la-Chaudière, accessible from exit 130 of Autoroute 73. A 113-metre suspension footbridge, 23 metres above the river, offers a view of the 35-metre-high falls.
No later than the 15th of each month.
Au printemps, la Beaurivage sort souvent: In spring, the Beaurivage often overflows its banks. Check where the unit is in relation to the river before you sign.
Au recensement de 2006, Charny comptait: In the 2006 census, Charny had 10,367 residents over about 8 km². City-wide, 34.1% of Lévis households were tenants in 2021. The area is home to the Paul-Gilbert hospital centre, the école secondaire les Etchemins and the Honco stadium, as well as Parc Maréchal-Joffre and Parc de la Rivière.
Au recensement de 2006, Pintendre compta: At the 2006 census, Pintendre had 6,334 residents; across Lévis, 34.1% of households were tenants in 2021. The area has two elementary schools, the école des Moussaillons and the école du Boisé. Parc du Lac-Baie-d’Or and the Site des Pins, at the end of Route Monseigneur-Lagueux, are among its green spaces.
Au recensement de 2006, Saint-Nicolas co: At the 2006 census, Saint-Nicolas had 18,437 residents over about 95 km². City-wide, 34.1% of Lévis households were tenants in 2021. The area has five elementary schools and the école secondaire de l’Envol. The heritage site preserves the Maison Pâquet, built around 1760, and the Chapelle Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, from 1867-1868.
Au recensement de 2006, Saint-Romuald co: At the 2006 census, Saint-Romuald had 11,633 residents over about 17 km². City-wide, 34.1% of Lévis households were tenants in 2021. The area is home to Lévis city hall, at 2175 Chemin du Fleuve, a marina and the start of Lévis’s main cycling trail, which runs along the river for about fifteen kilometres to Lauzon.
Au recensement de 2006, le secteur compt: At the 2006 census, the area had 1,141 residents; across Lévis, 34.1% of households were tenants in 2021. It is home to Lac Bargoné and its park, as well as Parc André-Guay. Since 2010, the Saint-Joseph-de-Lévis parish has grouped seven churches and one chapel in the Desjardins borough.
Au recensement de 2011, Saint-Rédempteur: At the 2011 census, Saint-Rédempteur had 7,700 residents. City-wide, 34.1% of Lévis households were tenants in 2021. The area has three elementary schools, du Tournesol, Dominique-Savio and de la Ruche, as well as a Catholic church in the centre of the village, across from the école du Tournesol.
Au recensement de 2011, le secteur compt: In the 2011 census, the sector had 9,990 residents. City-wide, 34.1% of Lévis households were tenants in 2021. It is home to the Plein-Soleil, La Chanterelle and La Clé-du-Boisé schools, the Centre Bruno-Verret arena, the Albert-Rousseau library and several parks, including Grandes-Pointes and Jean-de-Lauzon. The Maison des aînés et alternative de Lévis opened there in 2023.
Au recensement de 2016, 10,8 % des habit: At the 2016 census, 10.8% of residents were tenants, out of a population of 10,095. Lac Saint-Charles, with a surface area of 3.6 km², is one of the region’s most important sources of drinking water. The neighbourhood also has the Marais-du-Nord nature reserve, the start of the linear park along the Saint-Charles and du Berger rivers, Parc Paul-Émile-Beaulieu and the Le Tournesol library.
Au recensement de 2016, 13,2 % des habit: At the 2016 census, 13.2% of residents were tenants, and the neighbourhood had 17,885 residents, 29.8% of whom were under 25. A few farms remain active on Avenue Joseph-Giffard and Boulevard Louis-XIV. It is also home to the Club de golf Beauport and the parks la Ribambelle, Chevalier, Saint-Joseph, Armand-Paris and Montpellier.
Au recensement de 2016, 17,7 % des habit: In the 2016 census, 17.7% of residents were tenants and the average age was 36.1, compared with 43.2 for the city as a whole. The neighbourhood has many parks, including Grande-Oasis, Réal-Cloutier and du Millénaire. It is also home to the Centre communautaire Saint-Émile and Saint-Émile church, built in 1926–1927.
Au recensement de 2016, 23,2 % des habit: In the 2016 census, 23.2% of residents were tenants, out of a population of 28,665 and an average age of 35.1. The Base de plein air de Val-Bélair offers 55 km of cross-country ski and snowshoe trails in winter. The neighbourhood also has Parc La Chanterelle, Parc de détente Belle-Eau, the Félix-Leclerc library and the Georges-Dor cultural centre.
Au recensement de 2016, 23,8 % des habit: In the 2016 census, 23.8% of residents were tenants; the population reached 14,450 in 2021. The neighbourhood has several parks, including Parc Chauveau, Parc Montchâtel and Parc de la Chaumière, as well as the linear park of the Saint-Charles and Du Berger rivers. It is home to the Neufchâtel library, the Michel-Labadie community centre and the École secondaire de Neufchâtel.
Au recensement de 2016, 36,8 % des habit: At the 2016 census, 36.8% of residents were tenants, out of a population of 15,655. The neighbourhood is home to Parc de la chute Kabir Kouba, whose falls are 28 metres high, the linear park along the Saint-Charles and du Berger rivers and the Cheminots bike path. It also has the Hôpital Chauveau, the Chrystine-Brouillet library and the École du cinéma et de la télévision du Québec.
Au recensement de 2016, 44,7 % des habit: In the 2016 census, 44.7% of residents were tenants, out of a population of 16,090. Parc de la Chute-Montmorency, where the falls reach 83 metres, includes the Montmorency manor and its interpretation centre. The neighbourhood also has the Le Montmorency golf club, the Gilles-Tremblay arena, the école secondaire La Courvilloise and the Théâtre de la Dame Blanche.
Au recensement de 2016, 45,8 % des habit: In the 2016 census, 45.8% of residents were tenants, out of a population of 15,460. The neighbourhood is home to the Beauport borough office, the Marcel-Bédard sports centre, Parc de la Rivière-Beauport and several schools, including Académie Sainte-Marie and École secondaire de la Seigneurie. The Maison Girardin and the Terrasse Joseph-Abraham-Gagnon, known as "Les maisons victoriennes," are among its notable buildings.
Au recensement de 2016, 61,4 % des habit: In the 2016 census, 61.4% of residents were tenants, out of a population of 14,985. The neighbourhood is home to the Institut universitaire en santé mentale de Québec, formerly the Centre hospitalier Robert-Giffard, and the Étienne-Parent library. Parc des Cascades, the Alexis-Bérubé sports centre and the Pavillon Royal recreation centre are its main recreation spots.
Au recensement de 2016, 65,3 % des ménag: In the 2016 census, 65.3% of households were tenants. Parc Saint-Sacrement offers a pool, a skatepark and a curling rink, and Parc Holland and Parc des Saints-Martyrs-Canadiens round out the green spaces. The neighbourhood also has the Hôpital du Saint-Sacrement, the Jeffery Hale Hospital, Cégep Garneau and several elementary and high schools.
Au recensement de 2016, 70,6 % des ménag: In the 2016 census, 70.6% of households were tenants. The Saint-Charles and du Berger rivers linear park runs along the neighbourhood, which also has Parc Victorin-Beaucage, the Laurence-Perron recreation centre and the Patrick-Poulin arena. It is home to the Aliette-Marchand library, the Institut de réadaptation en déficience physique de Québec and Vanier secondary school.
Au recensement de 2016, 77,1 % des ménag: In the 2016 census, 77.1% of households were tenants, and 61.4% of dwellings dated from 1960 or earlier. The neighbourhood is home to the Grand Théâtre de Québec, the Théâtre Périscope, the Québec City Convention Centre and the Claire-Martin library, housed in the former St. Matthew church. Its green spaces are small parks, such as Berthelot, Richelieu and de l’Amérique-Française parks, or St-Matthew park, a former Protestant cemetery.
Au recensement de 2016, 78,2 % des ménag: At the 2016 census, 78.2% of households were tenants. The Domaine de Maizerets, a 27-hectare park with 11 km of trails and an arboretum, is its main green space, along with Parc Bardy. The neighbourhood is also home to the Hôpital de l’Enfant-Jésus, the Institut universitaire en santé mentale de Québec and the Centre Monseigneur-Marcoux.
Au recensement de 2016, 81,2 % des ménag: At the 2016 census, 81.2% of households were tenants, and the neighbourhood had 15,865 residents. It has Parc Lairet and, at ExpoCité, the Centre Vidéotron, the Guy-Lafleur pavilion, the Centre de foires and the Grand Marché de Québec. The neighbourhood also has the Saint-Albert-le-Grand, Sainte-Odile and Saint-Paul-Apôtre elementary schools, as well as the Centre de formation professionnelle de Limoilou.
Au recensement de 2021, Beaupré comptait: In the 2021 census, Beaupré had 4,117 residents. Besides the ski resort, the town has an industrial park and a marina at the mouth of the Sainte-Anne River.
Au recensement de 2021, Boischatel compt: In the 2021 census, Boischatel had 8,231 residents. The Montmorency Falls are partly on its territory, and the Boischatel caves, explored over about 3,000 m, are the longest in Canada east of the Rockies.
Au recensement de 2021, Cap-Santé compta: In the 2021 census, Cap-Santé had 3,594 residents. The Sainte-Famille heritage site, classified in 1986, includes the church, the rectory, the cemetery and a section of the old road leading to the wharf.
Au recensement de 2021, Honfleur comptai: In the 2021 census, Honfleur had 881 residents. Agriculture and forestry work long supported the population, and Maurice Laliberté’s farm received the Mérite agricole gold medal in 1962. The Fleur de Lys hall, owned by the municipality, can hold up to 290 people.
Au recensement de 2021, Lac-Sergent comp: At the 2021 census, Lac-Sergent had 541 residents. The lake normally freezes from November to April, and its shores are lined with many homes and cottages.
Au recensement de 2021, Neuville comptai: At the 2021 census, Neuville had 4,475 residents. Rue des Érables and the former village core form a historic ensemble of regional interest, with many well-preserved old buildings.
Au recensement de 2021, Saint-Basile com: In the 2021 census, Saint-Basile had 2,709 residents. The Ciment Québec cement plant, founded by the Papillon family, is the town’s main economic player.
Au recensement de 2021, Saint-Henri comp: In the 2021 census, Saint-Henri had 5,813 residents. The village has a recreation centre with an arena, a library, a bike path and cross-country ski trails. Its industrial park, on Rue de la Gare, is home to an Olymel plant, among others.
Au recensement de 2021, Saint-Joachim co: At the 2021 census, Saint-Joachim had 1,427 residents. The Cap-Tourmente National Wildlife Area, created in 1978, protects the marshes where the greater snow goose stops. Since 1981, it has been recognized as a site of international importance under the Ramsar Convention.
Au recensement de 2021, Wendake comptait: In the 2021 census, Wendake had 2,200 residents. The Nation Council, led by a Grand Chief and chiefs, handles education, health, recreation and housing, among other things. French is the language of use, and the Wendat language is the subject of a revitalization project.
Au recensement de 2021, elle comptait 7: In the 2021 census, it had 7,968 residents, 30% more than in 2016. That was the largest increase in Québec among municipalities of more than 5,000 residents. There are two elementary schools, a medical clinic and a pharmacy.
Au recensement de 2021, la municipalité: In the 2021 census, the municipality had 1,504 residents. In summer, its population increases by about 1,000 people thanks to its vacation areas.

In the 2021 census, the municipality had 3,806 residents. The Sept-Chutes power station, put back into service by Hydro-Québec in 1999, produces 22 MW, and part of the Seigneurie de Beaupré wind farms is in its territory.

At the 2021 census, the municipality had 6,817 residents. On Rue du Pont, the Centre de loisirs and Parc Alexis-Blanchet group together baseball, tennis and pickleball courts, skating rinks and a skatepark.
At the 2021 census, the municipality had 8,164 residents. The Le Relais ski centre has 27 runs, and the Sentiers du Moulin offer about 50 km of cross-country skiing and 30 km of mountain biking.

In the 2021 census, the municipality had 9,682 residents, compared with 5,266 in 2001. The Station touristique Stoneham, the golf club and the parks make recreational tourism its main economic activity. Cottages in summer and ski-resort condos in winter add about 2,000 seasonal residents.
Au recensement de 2021, la ville comptai: In the 2021 census, the town had 10,121 residents, up from 9,240 in 2016. Its territory covers 123.4 km². Its residents are called Pont-Rougeois (men) and Pont-Rougeoises (women).

At the 2021 census, the town had 11,108 residents over 693.6 km². The Centre multifonctionnel Rolland-Dion, with its six halls, hosts shows and artists. Every July, the Festival forestier de Saint-Raymond brings the town to life.

In the 2021 census, the town had 13,134 residents, making it the second-largest town in Beauce after Saint-Georges. Its two industrial parks, along Highway 73, account for about 60% of the RCM's industrial jobs. It also has a comprehensive high school, a college campus, an arena, a library and indoor and outdoor pools.

At the 2021 census, the city had 149,683 residents. Nearly half of its 444 km² territory is cultivated, and forest covers more than a third. The Mouvement Desjardins, founded in Lévis in 1900, is among the region’s major employers, and the Davie shipyard, in Lauzon, has been active since 1832.

In the 2021 census, the town had 16,970 residents. Its French-language public schools come under the Centre de services scolaire des Découvreurs, and the town publishes its municipal newspaper, Le Lorettain, four times a year.
In the 2021 census, the city had 19,907 residents. The François-Leclerc industrial park is home to the head offices of Biscuits Leclerc and Louis Garneau Sports.
In the 2021 census, the town had 2,327 residents. Lac Saint-Joseph covers 11.31 km² and is 8.1 km long from north to south. The Duchesnay resort surrounds it to the west, north and east.
In the 2021 census, the town had 2,888 residents. Its basilica is one of the main pilgrimage sites in North America and receives several hundred thousand visitors a year.

In the 2021 census, the town had 7,436 residents over 37.3 km². Several regional organizations have offices there, including the Centre local d’emploi and the Carrefour jeunesse emploi de Portneuf. An industrial park extends along Autoroute 40.
Au recensement de 2021, le quartier comp: At the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 12,000 residents, and 78.8% of households were tenants. Units here are smaller than the city average: 70.7% have fewer than five rooms. It is home to Parc Henri-Casault, Parc Maurice-Lortie, the École de l’Envol and the École de la Fourmilière.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 13,375 residents, and 17.4% of households were tenants. It is home to the Sainte-Foy outdoor base, the Parc des Sentiers-de-la-Rivière-du-Cap-Rouge and the Saint-Ange and Saint-Denis farming rangs. The neighbourhood also has the Collège de Champigny, the Chauveau industrial park and part of the Colbert industrial park.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 13,820 residents, up 37.8% since 2001, and 27.7% of households were tenants. It is home to the Parc de la Montagne-des-Roches, the Parc du Bourg-Royal and the Parc des Émeraudes. The Externat Saint-Jean-Eudes, the École secondaire des Sentiers and the École primaire du Bourg-Royal are located here.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 14,105 residents, and 47.5% of households were tenants. It includes the Marly, Compagnons-de-Cartier and Neilson woods, as well as Campanile and Saint-Benoît parks. The neighbourhood is also home to the head office of Revenu Québec, Saint-Benoît-Abbé church and the Collège des Compagnons.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 14,610 residents and 27.7% of households were tenants. It is home to Parc du Bois-de-Coulonge, the Cataraqui estate, the villa Bagatelle, the Maison des Jésuites de Sillery and part of the Promenade Samuel-De Champlain. The neighbourhood borders the Saint-Michel-de-Sillery cemetery, where René Lévesque rests.

At the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 14,815 residents and 64.0% of households were tenants; the average age was 38.9, compared with 43.8 for the city. Parcs Sainte-Geneviève and Saint-Mathieu are its main green spaces. It also has the Sainte-Geneviève and Saint-Mathieu churches, the Quatre-Bourgeois shopping centre and the Hôtel Château Bonne-Entente.

At the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 14,825 residents, and 17.8% of households were tenants. The Rivière Jaune, the Rivière des Sept Ponts and several lakes, including Lacs Clément, Jaune and Bégon, run through it. It has Parc Notre-Dame, Parc Bon-Pasteur, the Royal-Charbourg golf club, the Bon-Pasteur convent and the Le Sommet secondary school.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 15,975 residents, and 42.7% of households were tenants. It is home to the Patro de Charlesbourg, the Arpidrome, a sports complex adjoining the École polyvalente de Charlesbourg, and Parc Guillaume-Mathieu. The Charlesbourg campus of Cégep Limoilou and the École Joseph-Paquin are also located there.

At the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 16,535 residents and 55.1% of households were tenants. It is home to the Aquarium du Québec, the Centre de glaces de Québec, the Centre sportif de Sainte-Foy and several parks, including Saint-Louis-de-France and Roland-Beaudin. The CHUL, the Andrée-P.-Boucher building, the Sainte-Foy public market and the Monique-Corriveau library are also located there.

At the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 16,575 residents, and 30.7% of households were tenants. The Golf de la Faune and Parc des Moulins occupy much of the west, and the du Berger, des Commissaires and des Roches rivers run through it. It also has the Rivière-des-Roches linear park, Parcs Saint-Pierre, Chabot and des Verveines, and the Église Saint-Pierre-aux-Liens.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 17,030 residents, and 13.5% of households were tenants. The south is residential and low-density, while the north is wooded. It is home to the Centre de plein air de Beauport, the La Sablière recreation centre and Parc de la Rivière-Beauport.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 17,290 residents, and 14.1% of households were tenants. Parc de la Plage-Jacques-Cartier, Parc nautique de Cap-Rouge and Parc Cartier-Roberval give access to the river, where a large marsh is home to waterfowl. Old Cap-Rouge has 75 heritage buildings, and the neighbourhood is home to the Léon-Provancher house and the Roger-Lemelin library.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 20,565 residents and 74.5% of households were tenants. The Université Laval campus holds most of the green spaces and sports facilities, including the PEPS and Stade TELUS-Université Laval. The neighbourhood is also home to the Roger-Van den Hende botanical garden, the Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec and the Laurier Québec and Place Sainte-Foy shopping centres.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 26,780 residents and 54.4% of households were tenants. It combines residential, commercial and industrial uses, including part of the Parc technologique du Québec métropolitain. It has the linear park of the Saint-Charles and Du Berger rivers, Parc de Duberger and the Jean-Baptiste-Duberger and Romain-Langlois libraries.

In the 2021 census, the neighbourhood had 9,680 residents, and 38.0% of households were tenants. The Charlesbourg heritage site covers 24 ha and has 138 buildings around a central square of 8.5 ha. The neighbourhood also has Parc Maurice-Dorion, Parc de la Commune and the Bibliothèque Paul-Aimé-Paiement.
Au recensement de 2021, le secteur compt: At the 2021 census, the area had 16,826 residents; across Lévis, 34.1% of households were tenants. It has five elementary schools and the école secondaire l’Horizon. Parc Champigny, a sports park, hosts Festivent shows, and the Saint-Jean-Chrysostome airport is on Rue de l’Aéroport.
Au recensement de 2021, l’arrondissement: In the 2021 census, the borough had 88,460 residents over about 148 km². Its green spaces include Parc de la Falaise et de la chute Kabir Kouba, the Marais-du-Nord nature reserve, the Saint-Charles River linear park and the Mont-Bélair nature park.
Au sud de Saint-Nicolas, de part et d’au: South of Saint-Nicolas, on both sides of the Beaurivage River, in the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough. The route des Rivières runs through the area and several businesses line Route Lagueux; the Chaudière River borders it to the east.
South of Saint-Nicolas, on both sides of the Beaurivage River, west of the Chaudière River. It is one of the three sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough, in Lévis.
Au sud de la ville, dans le quadrant sud: In the south of the city, in the southeast quadrant formed by Autoroutes Henri-IV and Charest, around Université Laval’s main campus. Chemin Sainte-Foy and Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois run through it; the Laurier Québec and Place Sainte-Foy shopping centres line Boulevard Laurier.
Au sud de la ville, en bordure du fleuve: South of the city, along the St. Lawrence River, at the foot and on top of the cliff. Chemin Saint-Louis and Boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest run through it; it is home to Parc du Bois-de-Coulonge and the Cataraqui estate.
Au sud de la ville, en grande partie ent: In the south of the city, largely between the Duplessis and Henri-IV highways, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough. Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois and Chemin Sainte-Foy cross it; Parcs Sainte-Geneviève and Saint-Mathieu are its main green spaces.
Au sud de la ville, à la tête des ponts: In the south of the city, at the head of the Québec and Pierre-Laporte bridges, partly along the St. Lawrence River. Boulevard Laurier concentrates hotels and shops there; Chemin Saint-Louis and Route de l’Église run through it.
Au sud de l’arrondissement de Charlesbou: In the south of the Charlesbourg borough, alongside Autoroutes Laurentienne and Félix-Leclerc. 1re Avenue is its main artery; the Saint-Rodrigue church stands there.
Au sud-est de la ville de Québec, le lon: In the southeast of Québec City, along the St. Lawrence River and the Saint-Charles River. The borough brings together Upper Town, Lower Town and Limoilou, north of the river.
Au sud-est de l’arrondissement de Charle: In the southeast of the Charlesbourg borough, between Boulevard Henri-Bourassa and Boulevard du Loiret, south of Boulevard Jean-Talon. The Moulin des Jésuites and the Carrefour Charlesbourg shopping centre are landmarks.
Au sud-ouest de la ville de Québec, sur: Southwest of Québec City, on the Québec City hill and along the river. The Québec and Pierre-Laporte bridges end here, and Boulevard Laurier connects the borough to downtown.
Au sud-ouest de l’arrondissement de Char: In the southwest of the Charlesbourg borough, between Autoroute Laurentienne and Boulevard Henri-Bourassa. The 1re Avenue and Boulevard Louis-XIV cross it; the Église Saint-Charles-Borromée marks the centre of the historic village.

Autour de Lac-Saint-Charles et de Saint-: Around Lac-Saint-Charles and Saint-Émile, the poor soil limited agriculture. The parish of Saint-Ambroise-de-la-Jeune-Lorette became the town of Loretteville, the area’s commercial and institutional centre. Leatherworking, influenced by the proximity of Wendake, and the power of the Kabir Kouba falls gave rise to a small industry.
Autour du lac Sergent, dans Portneuf, à: Around Lac Sergent, in Portneuf, about 40 km from Québec City and 10 km from Saint-Raymond. Chemin du Tour-du-Lac circles the lake, and Route 367 runs along its northern part.
Aux Saules, la paroisse Sainte-Monique-d: In Les Saules, the parish of Sainte-Monique-des-Saules was created in 1945. From the 1940s, housing cooperatives backed by the Ligue ouvrière catholique, then by the Catholic unions, built homes there for working-class families; the cooperative’s 150th home was blessed on November 18, 1956. The municipality of Sainte-Monique-des-Saules was born in 1953 and became Ville Les Saules in 1960. Its church was completed in 1958.
Aux XVIIe et XVIIIe siècles, après leur: In the 17th and 18th centuries, after their defeat by the Iroquois, the Wendat settled in the seigneury of Bourg-Louis and the neighbouring townships. They hunted, fished and gathered berries there.
Avant 1903, le secteur est partagé entre: Before 1903, the area was split among five parishes: Saint-Édouard, Sainte-Croix, Saint-Antoine-de-Tilly, Saint-Apollinaire and Saint-Flavien. In 1885, Honoré Ferland was already operating a water-powered sawmill there, on the riverbank, in the 6e rang.
Avant l’ouverture de la paroisse, en 178: Before the parish opened in 1780, about sixty Acadian families lived in what was called the Nouvelle-Cadie. The rangs de la Première Cadie and de la Deuxième Cadie keep their memory. The village preserves a procession chapel built around 1817, classified in 1981, and a former rectory from 1873, designated in 2022.
Avec environ 12 km², Laurier-Station est: At about 12 km², Laurier-Station is the smallest municipality in the Lotbinière MRC by area and the most densely populated. It developed on both sides of Autoroute 20, where the railway crosses Route 271. The village combines a commercial and industrial zone along the highway with residential areas, surrounded by farmland.
Avec environ 181 km², Saint-Gilles est l: At about 181 km², Saint-Gilles is the largest municipality in the Lotbinière MRC, about 11% of its territory. It lies at the foot of the Appalachians, and several waterways cross it, including the Beaurivage River, the rivière aux Pins and the Bras d’Henri. You have to travel about 20 km to reach Highway 20 at Saint-Apollinaire or Saint-Étienne-de-Lauzon.
Avec la création de la MRC de La Jacques: With the creation of the La Jacques-Cartier RCM, the municipality took the name Sainte-Catherine-de-la-Jacques-Cartier in 1984. It became a town in 2000. Since the early 2000s, its population has grown rapidly.

Charlesbourg devient un lieu de villégia: Charlesbourg became a resort area in the first half of the 20th century, then urbanized. In 1959, the church was classified and the area officially received the name Trait-Carré. The Charlesbourg heritage site was declared in 1965. The city of Charlesbourg, formed in 1976, was merged with Québec City in 2002. The Sainte-Maria-Goretti church, opened in 1966, closed in 2007 and was demolished in the early 2010s.
Charlesbourg se trouve au nord de La Cit: Charlesbourg is north of La Cité-Limoilou, west of Beauport and east of Les Rivières and La Haute-Saint-Charles. Boulevard Henri-Bourassa and Autoroute Laurentienne connect it to downtown Québec City.
Charlesbourg s’urbanise dans la seconde: Charlesbourg urbanized in the second half of the 20th century. The parish of Saint-Jérôme was erected in 1956; its church, opened in 1960, was completed in 1967. The City of Charlesbourg acquired the mill in 1982 and restored it in 1990–1992; it now houses a children’s history museum. The neighbourhood’s name was adopted shortly after the election of its first council, on February 19, 2008.

Charny est l’un des quatre secteurs de l: Charny is one of the four sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough. It is on the east bank of the Chaudière, not far from the Québec Bridge, and the rail network plays an important role there, with Canadian National’s Joffre rail yard. De la paroisse Saint-Gervais-et-Saint-Pr: From the parish of Saint-Gervais-et-Saint-Protais, opened in 1780 and dedicated to Saints Gervase and Protase by Father Louis-Pascal Sarault. The shortened name Saint-Gervais became the municipality’s official name in 1991.

De la paroisse fondée en 1679 sous le pa: From the parish founded in 1679 under the patronage of Saint Joseph, and from the pointe de Lévy, named after Henri de Lévis, Duke of Ventadour. The spelling “De Lévy” reflects the noble particle.

Depuis le 1er janvier 2026, le calcul su: Since January 1, 2026, the calculation follows a new method. The base is the three-year average of the Québec consumer price index, published by the TAL. Added to it, where applicable, are an adjustment for municipal and school taxes and for insurance, when their increase exceeds that base percentage; major work expenses, at the rate of 5%; and the addition of a service, accessory or dependency. Government assistance received is taken into account. A notice given before January 1, 2026 follows the old method. The result is a reference: the parties can agree on a different amount[3].
Depuis le 21 février 2024 (Loi 31), le p: Since February 21, 2024 (Bill 31), a landlord who receives an assignment notice has 15 days to respond[1][2]. With no response within 15 days, the landlord is deemed to have accepted[1].

Des années 1940 à 1960, le quai sert de: From the 1940s to the 1960s, the wharf served as home port to the schooners carrying pulpwood to Québec City. In 1971, the municipality adopted the name Berthier-sur-Mer to distinguish itself from Berthierville. The word mer (sea) evokes the width of the river, its salt water and its strong tides. Former Premier Jean Lesage spent his summers there, and a park bears his name.
Des appartements dans des immeubles de m: Apartments in buildings of fewer than five storeys, single-family homes and a notable share of recent construction.
Des bungalows des années 1950 et suivant: Bungalows from the 1950s onward, older houses along the first roads and a denser fabric in Loretteville, with mansard-roofed and Boomtown-style houses.
Des chalets de montagne, des maisons bif: Mountain chalets, duplexes and New France–style houses northeast of the lake. To the west, larger, heavily wooded lots developed starting in 1990.
Des colons venus de L’Ancienne-Lorette s: Settlers from L’Ancienne-Lorette established themselves on the territory as early as 1830. The Catholic parish of Saint-Raymond-Nonnat was founded around 1842. Its name honours Raymond Nonnatus, a Catalan cardinal. The civil parish was erected in 1845.
Des colons venus des paroisses voisines: Settlers from neighbouring parishes moved in the late 1840s into the townships of Buckland and Mailloux. The united townships municipality of Buckland-et-Mailloux was created in 1859. The township of Buckland, proclaimed in 1806, is named after a locality in England.
Des condos et des lofts dans d’anciens b: Condos and lofts in converted former industrial buildings, and units above shops.
Des croisières guidées partent de la mar: Guided cruises leave from the Berthier-sur-Mer marina, at 100 Rue de la Marina, from May to October. Grosse-Île served as a quarantine station from 1832 to 1937, and the visit is led by Parks Canada guides.
Des difficultés d’alimentation en eau po: Problems with the drinking water supply led to the annexation of Neufchâtel to Québec City on January 1, 1971. During the 2002 mergers, its territory was divided among several neighbourhoods. Its western part became the Des Châtels neighbourhood, in the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough, whose name is derived from that of Neufchâtel.
Des duplex, des maisons individuelles et: Duplexes, single-family homes and apartment buildings from different eras, along wide, tree-lined streets.

In 1932, Dr. Paul Gilbert had the 12-bed Notre-Dame-de-Charny hospital built, transferred in 1948 to the Sisters of Saint Paul of Chartres. Charny gained town status in 1965, with 4,564 residents.

Du chef iroquoien Donnacona, qui vivait: From the Iroquoian chief Donnacona, who lived in the village of Stadacona, on the banks of the Saint-Charles River, when Jacques Cartier passed through in 1535. The residents are called Donnaconiens and Donnaconiennes.
Du chemin Saint-Louis et de la paroisse: From Chemin Saint-Louis and the Saint-Louis-de-France parish, founded in 1956 and named in honour of Louis IX, King of France from 1226 to 1270.
Du comté d’Orsainville, un fief situé à: From the county of Orsainville, a fief located nearby in the days of New France. The municipality of Saint-Charles-de-Charlesbourg took this name in 1953.
Du lac Saint-Charles, qui doit son nom à: From Lac Saint-Charles, which is named after the Rivière Saint-Charles that flows out of it. The name recalls Charles Desboues, a benefactor of the Récollets who arrived in Québec City in 1615.

Duberger–Les Saules est l’un des cinq qu: Duberger–Les Saules is one of the five neighbourhoods of the Les Rivières borough. It is roughly bounded by Autoroute Félix-Leclerc, the Saint-Charles River and Boulevard de l’Auvergne to the north, Autoroute Henri-IV to the west, Autoroute Charest to the south and the line of Avenue Saint-Sacrement to the east. Boulevards Wilfrid-Hamel and Père-Lelièvre run through it from east to west; the Saint-Charles, Du Berger and Lorette rivers flow through it.
Durant la première moitié du XXe siècle,: During the first half of the 20th century, Rue Saint-Joseph was Québec City’s great shopping centre, with the Paquet, Pollack, Syndicat de Québec and Laliberté department stores. Two-thirds of the city’s population then lived in Saint-Roch or Saint-Sauveur. From the 1950s, the suburbs drew families away, and the neighbourhood’s population fell from about 20,000 to 5,000. In 1974, part of Rue Saint-Joseph was covered with a roof: this was the Mail Saint-Roch.

Dès 1651, Eustache Lambert organise un é: As early as 1651, Eustache Lambert set up a fishing station at this spot in the seigneury of Lauzon, then known as Etchemin. Under the French Regime, agriculture, fishing and early logging dominated the economy. After 1738, a road ran along the river from Pointe-Lévy to the lands of Lambert's heirs. The area was first settled by a small group of Irish, soon followed by French Canadians.
Dès 1702, le seigneur fait bâtir une cha: As early as 1702, the seigneur had a wooden chapel built under the patronage of Saint Anthony of Padua, and the parish registers were opened. The first stone of a church was laid in 1712. During the siege of Québec in 1759, English soldiers landed at Saint-Antoine and entrenched themselves in the church.
Dès 1939, la Seconde Guerre mondiale fai: From 1939, the Second World War caused the population to grow, as many residents worked at the nearby military base and munitions factories. In 1965, Saint-Gérard-Majella became a city and took the name Bélair, recalling the former seigneury. On January 1, 1974, Bélair and Val-Saint-Michel merged to form Val-Bélair, which was briefly placed under trusteeship in 1977.
Dès la fin du XVIIIe siècle, le lac atti: From the end of the 18th century, the lake attracted travellers and artists, mostly English-speaking, on a circuit that also included Montmorency Falls and the village of Lorette. They stayed at the inn, in boarding houses or at the Hôtel Verret, built between 1850 and 1883. Built around 1850, the Campbell-Gale cottage is the oldest resort cottage still standing. At the end of the 19th century, cottage stays replaced passing tourism.
Dès la fin du XVIIe siècle, des Hurons-W: From the end of the 17th century, Huron-Wendat settled in the region after leaving their settlement at Lorette, today’s L’Ancienne-Lorette; their Wendake reserve is a little east of the neighbourhood. Boulevard de l’Ormière follows a road dating from the French regime. The founding of the parish of Saint-Ambroise-de-la-Jeune-Lorette, in the late 18th century, marked the start of settlement in the territory.
Dès le lendemain de l’échéance pour récl: From the day after the due date to claim the rent. After more than three weeks of delay, you can also apply to terminate the lease (s. 1971 CCQ).
Dès le milieu du XIXe siècle, des centai: From the mid-19th century, hundreds of Sunday strollers came by ferry. Wealthy Québec City families, including the Boswells, brewers, had summer residences built along Chemin Royal. The painter Horatio Walker worked in his studio here until his death in 1938.
Dès les années 1660, le bailliage de Bea: From the 1660s, the bailiwick of Beaupré, a seigneurial court, sat in Château-Richer. In 1694, Bishop de Laval had a first convent built for the education of young girls, entrusted to the Congrégation de Notre-Dame. The Petit-Pré water mill, built in the late 17th century for the Séminaire de Québec, is one of the oldest commercial flour mills in North America.
Dès les années 1820, les scieries implan: From the 1820s, the sawmills set up near the falls were among the largest in North America. Their workers settled at Bas-du-Sault, along today’s Avenue Saint-Grégoire; in 1871, nearly 650 people worked there. On October 7, 1885, a hydroelectric plant was inaugurated near the falls. The mills ceased operations in 1892, by which time a cotton mill was already running.
