D’une banlieue agricole à un quartier de: From an agricultural suburb to an Upper Town neighbourhood, in five dates and four chapters.
D’une chapelle que les Récollets dédient: From a chapel that the Récollets dedicated to Saint Roch in 1692, when an epidemic struck the colony. The name then passed to the street, the suburb, the parish and the neighbourhood.
D’une statue de Notre-Dame de Lourdes ac: From a statue of Notre-Dame de Lourdes bought by the notable George Muir, who also funded the Sœurs du Bon-Pasteur convent in 1871 and a chapel in 1875.
En 1535, Jacques Cartier accoste sur les: In 1535, Jacques Cartier landed on the banks of the Rivière Saint-Charles, very close to present-day Limoilou. In 1626, the Notre-Dame-des-Anges seigneury was granted to the Jesuits, and the lands north of the river’s mouth became farms. This agricultural character lasted until the early 20th century.
En 1535, Jacques Cartier appelle l’île «: In 1535, Jacques Cartier called the island “isle de Bacchus” because of the wild vines, which were plentiful in the Saint-François area. He soon renamed it Île d’Orléans. The territory is part of the seigneury of Île d’Orléans, granted on January 15, 1636.
En 1541, Jacques Cartier s’installe à Ca: In 1541, Jacques Cartier settled at Cap-Rouge with 375 colonists and founded the colony of Charlesbourg-Royal. Roberval took over the following year, but the site was abandoned in 1543. The name Cap-Rouge comes from the reddish shale of the cliffs, at the mouth of the rivière du Cap Rouge.
En 1541, Jacques Cartier, mandaté par Fr: In 1541, Jacques Cartier, commissioned by Francis I, established the colony of Charlesbourg-Royal at the mouth of the Cap Rouge River. The settlers built two forts there, but winter, scurvy and tensions with the Indigenous peoples weakened them. Roberval took over in 1542 and named the colony France-Roy, but the site was abandoned in 1543. Archaeological digs begun in 2006 confirmed the existence of these forts.
En 1620, Champlain choisit la Haute-Vill: In 1620, Champlain chose Upper Town as the site for Fort Saint-Louis. From then on it took on a military and administrative character, home to soldiers, officials and clergy, while Lower Town was settled by merchants and artisans.
En 1626, le territoire fait partie de la: In 1626, the territory was part of the seigneury of Notre-Dame-des-Anges, granted to the Jesuits. In 1667, Intendant Jean Talon, backed by Minister Colbert, expropriated part of their lands between Charlesbourg and Beauport. He had a star-shaped village laid out there, inspired by the Trait-Carré of Charlesbourg, with an annex to the north, the Bourg-la-Reine. This plan is rare in New France, where lands mostly form long strips perpendicular to the river.
En 1629, Champlain nomme l’endroit cap d: In 1629, Champlain named the place Cap de Lévy, in tribute to Henri de Lévis, Viceroy of New France. The Lauzon seigneury was created in 1636. In 1647, Guillaume Couture, a carpenter and interpreter to the Indigenous nations, received land there and became the first settler of Pointe-Lévy.

In 1629, Champlain named the place Cap de Lévy, in honour of Henri de Lévis, viceroy of New France. The seigneury of Lauzon was created in 1636, and Guillaume Couture settled at Pointe-Lévy in 1647. The Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-de-Lévy mission, from which Lauzon and Saint-Joseph arose, was founded in 1679.
En 1634, le territoire fait partie de la: In 1634, the territory was part of the Beauport seigneury, granted to Robert Giffard. The first settlement appeared around 1820 under the name Waterloo Settlement. Many of the settlers were Irish Catholics.
En 1636, la Compagnie des Cent-Associés: In 1636, the Compagnie des Cent-Associés promised Jacques Le Neuf de la Poterie a concession on the heights of Cap-Santé and Portneuf. The first settlers arrived in 1675, and the parish’s first register was opened in 1679, the date used for the founding.
En 1637, les Jésuites établissent une mi: In 1637, the Jesuits established a mission at Sillery, with the support of Noël Brûlart de Sillery. The Notre-Dame-de-Foy mission served the settlers on the west of the hill as of 1638, and the seigneury of Sillery was created in 1651. On April 28, 1760, the Chevalier de Lévis defeated James Murray's troops at Sainte-Foy.
En 1638, les Jésuites fondent la mission: In 1638, the Jesuits founded the Notre-Dame-de-Foy mission to serve the settlers on the west of the Québec City hill. In 1667, about twenty families lived on the Côte Saint-Michel, which the current Chemin Sainte-Foy crosses, and a wooden chapel was built near the current Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois. The parish was created in 1698, and a first stone church was built in 1719, on the current site of Parc de la Visitation.
En 1647, la seigneurie de Maur est concé: In 1647, the seigneury of Maur was granted to the brothers Jean Juchereau de Maur and Noël Juchereau Deschatelets. Settlement was slow: in 1663, only three lots had been granted. A banal mill was built in 1672 at the outlet of Lac Saint-Augustin, and the Catholic parish was founded in 1691.
En 1653, Jean de Lauson concède la seign: In 1653, Jean de Lauson granted the seigneury to Jean Bourdon for his son Jean-François Bourdon de Dombourg, hence its first name, Dombourg. The first settlers arrived from 1667, and a seigneurial mill was built in 1668.
En 1658, Étienne de Lessard donne un ter: In 1658, Étienne de Lessard donated a piece of land to build a chapel dedicated to Saint Anne. According to tradition, Breton sailors saved from a shipwreck had wanted this shrine. The healing of a worker, Louis Guimont, during construction drew the first pilgrims, and a stone church was built in 1676.
En 1662, une route appelée Saint-Romain: In 1662, a road called Saint-Romain was opened and a village of the same name formed, attached to the parish of Charlesbourg. In 1794, the parish of Saint-Ambroise was founded at Jeune-Lorette, now Loretteville. Saint-Romain was part of it, as was the village of Saint-Ignace, located on what is now Rue de la Faune.
En 1664, Mgr de Laval érige la paroisse: In 1664, Bishop de Laval erected the parish of Saints-Anges-Gardiens. The chapel, baptized in 1670, took the name in the singular, and the municipality inherited it.
En 1665, l’intendant Jean Talon y trace: In 1665, Intendant Jean Talon laid out a village there around a central square, the Trait-Carré, from which the settlers’ lands radiate like a star. It is the only village of its kind in Canada.
En 1671, le territoire est rattaché à la: In 1671, the territory was attached to the seigneury of Les Islets, Talon’s personal property. In 1674, Bourg-Royal had 29 lots, against 6 for Bourg-la-Reine. Farther north, the Château Bigot, also called Beaumanoir, was built in 1718 as the summer residence of the intendant of New France. Abandoned around 1850, it inspired two novels in the 1870s; its last wall was dismantled in 1909.
En 1672, Olivier Morel de La Durantaye,: In 1672, Olivier Morel de La Durantaye, captain in the Carignan-Salières regiment, received the seigneury that bears his name. A mission was opened there the same year, then the Saint-Michel parish was established in 1678. It is among the first ten parishes in Québec territory.
En 1672, le capitaine Alexandre Berthier: In 1672, Captain Alexandre Berthier, of the Carignan regiment, received a seigneury split off from that of Bellechasse. As he also named a second seigneury upstream Berthier, today’s Berthierville, the first became Berthier-en-Bas. The seigneury then passed to the Bergères de Rigauville family.
En 1672, l’intendant Jean Talon concède: In 1672, Intendant Jean Talon granted the seigneury of Beaumont to Charles Couillard, grandson of Louis Hébert, and the neighbouring seigneury of Vincennes to François Bissot. The lands have been inhabited since about 1680, and the parish of Saint-Étienne was founded in 1692. A first wooden church was built in 1694.

In 1672, Intendant Jean Talon granted the seigneury of Pointe-aux-Écureuils to Toussaint Toupin and his son Jean. The town today bears the name of Donnacona, an Iroquoian chief whose village of Stadacona Jacques Cartier described in 1535, near present-day Québec City.
En 1674, le jésuite Pierre Chaumonot fai: In 1674, the Jesuit Pierre Chaumonot had a chapel built where the present cemetery stands. It served the Huron-Wendat who had taken refuge near Québec City after the war against the Iroquois. Healed after a pilgrimage to the Italian shrine of Loreto, Father Chaumonot placed the mission under the patronage of Notre-Dame de l’Annonciation, and the place took the name Lorette.
En 1675, on entreprend la construction d: In 1675, construction began on the parish church, the first built on the South Shore. Officially founded in 1679, the parish of Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-de-Lévy was canonically erected in 1694, then civilly in 1722. Its territory then covered a large part of the seigneury of Lauzon. Some documents also refer to it as Saint-Joseph-de-Lauzon.
En 1680, Nicolas Dupont de Neuville achè: In 1680, Nicolas Dupont de Neuville bought the seigneury and gave it his name. It already had 372 residents in 1683. The parish of Saint-François-de-Sales was established in 1684, with Jean Basset as its first parish priest, and the place was also called Pointe-aux-Trembles, after a point once covered in aspens.
En 1693, l’abbé Louis Soumande explore l: In 1693, Abbé Louis Soumande explored the heights north of Saint-Joachim on a hunting expedition and spotted arable land there. These lands were part of the seigneury of Beaupré, owned by the Séminaire de Québec. The first families settled there around 1730, most of them from Île d’Orléans.
En 1697, le territoire fait partie d’une: In 1697, the territory was part of a seigneury granted to the Jesuits for the use of the Abenaki, along the Chaudière. In 1737, it was granted to François-Étienne Cugnet under the name Saint-Étienne seigneury, developed from 1742.
En 1697, les Hurons-Wendats s’installent: In 1697, the Huron-Wendat settled farther away, at Jeune-Lorette. Their former village became Vieille-Lorette, or Ancienne-Lorette, and continued to develop with French settlers. Over time, the parish lost part of its territory to Saint-Félix-de-Cap-Rouge in 1872, then to Saint-Gérard-Majella in 1909.
En 1698, à la demande de François Berthe: In 1698, at the request of François Berthelot, Count of Saint-Laurent, the parish took the name Saint-Laurent, in memory of the Roman deacon. A stone church was built there at the end of the 17th century. In 1759, General Wolfe set up his quarters in the parish, and the priest obtained from him that the church be spared.
En 1713, Charles Couillard fils obtient: In 1713, Charles Couillard the younger obtained an extension of a league and a half in depth, at the back of the seigneury of Beaumont. The first settlers, who arrived from 1717, then depended on the parish of Beaumont. Settlement accelerated from 1723, because the land there was good.
En 1714, l’évêque divise la paroisse de: In 1714, the bishop divided the seigneury's parish in two, on either side of the Boyer River. The eastern part became the parish of Saint-Philippe-et-Saint-Jacques, where a first stone church had been started in 1712. In 1720, the nuns of the Hôpital général de Québec took possession of this part of the seigneury, acquired through Bishop de Saint-Vallier, whose name it took.
En 1721, les limites de la paroisse sont: In 1721, the parish boundaries were set from the Rivière du Petit Pré to the Montmorency falls. Two stone procession chapels were built in 1753. The parish municipality was created in 1845, abolished in 1847, then re-established in 1855. On April 3, 1920, Saint-Jean-de-Boischatel split off from L’Ange-Gardien.
En 1732, l’évêque coadjuteur Pierre-Herm: In 1732, the coadjutor bishop Pierre-Herman Dosquet had the first villa built there, called Samos. In the 19th century, the anse au Foulon became a centre of the timber trade and shipbuilding. Starting in 1850, Edward Stavely built the Cataraqui estate for the merchant Henry Burstall. In 1860, four small working-class villages stood alongside the large properties of the timber merchants, several of which would later pass to religious communities.
En 1734, le chirurgien Jean Mauvide et s: In 1734, surgeon Jean Mauvide and his wife, Marie-Anne Genest, had a stone house built, which they later expanded into a manor. Enriched by maritime trade, Mauvide bought the southwest half of the seigneury in 1752. Construction of the church also began in 1734 and was completed in 1737. In 1759, the manor was one of the few dwellings spared by Wolfe’s troops.
En 1738, Angélique Le Gardeur, fille du: In 1738, Angélique Le Gardeur, daughter of the seigneur of Tilly, received a seigneury south of Tilly’s. She named it the seigneury of Gaspé, after her late husband. In 1806, a road opened between Saint-Nicolas and Saint-Gilles helped develop the territory.
En 1742, les Jésuites construisent un mo: In 1742, the Jesuits built a stone water mill, one of a series of six on their seigneury. The Rivière des Commissaires, which flowed 1.5 km to the north, was diverted by hand to feed it, hence the expression “bringing water to the mill”. Until 1854, the miller was only a tenant of the mill, where he lived with his family.
En 1748, le seigneur Charles Couillard d: In 1748, the seigneur Charles Couillard donated a lot to build a church. The following year, Bishop de Pontbriand established the parish of Saint-Charles-Borromée, separated from Beaumont. In the 1750s, Acadian families settled in the area, notably on the rang de l’Hêtrière.
En 1754, les Ursulines font bâtir un mou: In 1754, the Ursulines had a flour mill built at the foot of the chute du Petit Saut. In 1846, Pierre-Gustave Joly, seigneur de Lotbinière, bought land at Pointe-Platon and had a summer manor, Maple House, built there in 1851. The parish municipality came into being in 1855.
En 1759, le corps du général Wolfe est t: In 1759, General Wolfe’s body was taken to the parish church to be embalmed. In 1763, the corpse of Marie-Josephte Corriveau was displayed there in an iron cage, an episode taken up by legend and literature. The parish municipality was created in 1845, folded into the county municipality in 1847, then reinstated in 1855.
En 1759, les matériaux de l’église serve: In 1759, the church’s materials were used to build Fort Jacques-Cartier, at the mouth of the river. After the defeat on the Plains of Abraham, the French army spent the winter there, and Lévis left from there in the spring of 1760 for the Battle of Sainte-Foy. The residents then recovered the materials and finished the church in 1767.
En 1759, pendant l’invasion britannique,: In 1759, during the British invasion, Father Charles d’Youville Dufrost took refuge in Saint-Henri with 287 parishioners from Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-Lévy.
En 1764, Kenelm Chandler, originaire de: In 1764, Kenelm Chandler, originally from Tewkesbury in England, obtained land in the region, which he would never occupy. In 1790, the Anglican pastor Philip Toosey received a large tract of land at Stoneham and built the first farm there in 1794. Irish, English and Scottish families settled in the township between 1815 and 1825. In 1855, the municipality took the name united townships of Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury.
En 1779, un presbytère-chapelle est bâti: In 1779, a rectory-chapel was built on land donated by Augustin Roberge and Marie-Anne Pouliot. The parish opened in 1780, and Father Louis-Pascal Sarault dedicated it to Saints Gervase and Protase. Construction of a church began in 1795.
En 1786, le seigneur fait construire le: In 1786, the seigneur had the Tilly manor built, which later became a hotel. The present church was blessed on September 24, 1788, and its interior décor includes woodwork designed in part by Thomas Baillairgé. It was classified as a historic monument in 1963.
En 1804, le blocus continental de Napolé: In 1804, Napoleon’s Continental Blockade pushed England to look for timber in its colonies, and logging began on the lands of the future parish. The parish was established canonically in 1858, from territories of Saint-Nicolas and Saint-Lambert, then civilly in 1860. Its name recalls Étienne Baillargeon, parish priest of Saint-Nicolas from 1838 to 1870; the post office opened in 1862 was in fact named Baillargeon.
En 1811, le grand voyer décide d’ouvrir: In 1811, the grand voyer decided to open a road between Sainte-Marie and the township. The following year, Desbarats and George Pyke hired Robert Gibson to build a sawmill. The first permanent residents settled between 1810 and 1815, and the 1825 census, the first in the territory, counted 194 residents.
En 1812, les premiers colons tracent une: In 1812, the first settlers laid out a road between the Jacques-Cartier River and Loretteville. In 1815, four Québec City businessmen, including John Neilson, bought a large part of the Jesuit lands. After Neilson’s call for settlement in 1816, Scottish, Irish, English and French settlers moved in and built houses, sawmills and flour mills.
En 1825, Mgr Plessis visite Frampton et: In 1825, Bishop Plessis visited Frampton and accepted a plot offered by Desbarats on which to build a chapel. An Irish Anglican community also settled in the north of the township, where Christ Church of Springbrook and its cemetery now form a designated heritage site. The Catholic mission of Saint-Édouard was canonically erected in 1858, and Église Saint-Édouard was built from 1859 to 1863.
En 1827, Mgr Panet, évêque de Québec, a: In 1827, Bishop Panet of Québec placed the new parish under the patronage of Saint Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury, a saint he held in particular veneration.
En 1830, Marguerite Marcoux, veuve de La: In 1830, Marguerite Marcoux, widow of Lazare Buteau, a former militia major of Saint-Gervais, donated land to the church council. The deed specified that the parish would be placed under the name Sainte-Marguerite. Bishop Bernard-Claude Panet canonically erected it on November 8, 1831, under the patronage of Saint Margaret of Scotland.
En 1847, le marchand de bois William Hed: In 1847, lumber merchant William Hedley Anderson divided his land into lots to attract workers: this was the birth of the village of Hedleyville. Three other working-class villages followed: Stadacona, Parkville and New Waterford. Overcrowding in Québec City, cholera epidemics and the fires of 1845 pushed many families toward these villages. The Lavigueur bridge, in 1867, and the arrival of the railway, in 1890, helped them grow.
En 1855, la municipalité de paroisse de: In 1855, the parish municipality of Sainte-Foy was established. Its boundaries were reduced in 1872 with the creation of the municipality of Saint-Félix-du-Cap-Rouge to the west. During the 19th century, notables and businessmen acquired estates and ran farms in the territory of Sainte-Foy, which kept a rural character until the 1940s.
En 1855, le territoire forme la municipa: In 1855, the territory formed the parish municipality of Ancienne-Lorette. It lost part of its territory in 1872 with the creation of Saint-Félix-du-Cap-Rouge, then in 1909 with that of Saint-Gérard-Majella. In 1947, the village separated from the parish to form the village municipality of Notre-Dame-de-Lorette, and the parish remained mostly agricultural.
En 1857, les habitants obtiennent la per: In 1857, the residents obtained permission to build a wooden chapel, and a first missionary opened the registers. A first church followed, then the parish of Saint-Cajetan-d’Armagh was canonically erected in 1882. Its patron, Saint Cajetan, or Gaetano of Thiene, founded the Theatine order in the 16th century.
En 1858, la paroisse de Saint-Étienne-de: In 1858, the parish of Saint-Étienne-de-Lauzon was separated from those of Saint-Nicolas and Saint-Lambert. Its name honours Étienne Baillargeon, parish priest of Saint-Nicolas from 1838 to 1870. Sawmills set up along the Beaurivage, and a bridge linked the two banks of the village in 1917.
En 1863, la paroisse est érigée sous le: In 1863, the parish was erected under the patronage of Saint Brigid of Ireland, in memory of the origin of the first settlers. The name Laval recalls the seigneury of Beaupré, whose first owner was François de Montmorency-Laval, bishop of Québec. French Canadians, who arrived after the Irish, became the majority around 1871.
En 1867, le village de Lauzon, le long d: In 1867, the village of Lauzon, along the river, broke away from the territory. Residents of the south, notably farmers in the rangs d’Harlaka, remained in the municipality, often called Saint-Joseph-de-Lévis. On January 1, 2002, it was merged into the new city of Lévis. The sector took the name Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-De Lévy, a spelling that reflects the noble particle.
En 1868, on y aménage le premier club de: In 1868, the first golf club in North America was laid out here, a three-hole course. The Église Sainte-Pétronille, built in 1871 on a promontory, has a simple interior by David Ouellet. The village also has St Mary's Chapel, a wooden Anglican chapel lit by stained-glass windows installed in 1904.
En 1870, le secteur est détaché de Saint: In 1870, the area was detached from Saint-Pierre and erected as a parish under the name Sainte-Pétronille de Beaulieu. A village municipality was created there in 1874 under the name Beaulieu, in honour of Jacques Gourdeau de Beaulieu. It officially adopted the name Sainte-Pétronille in 1980.
En 1889, après un référendum tenu les 26: In 1889, after a referendum held on September 26 and 27, following a fire that had destroyed about 500 houses.
En 1892, le curé Brousseau et Virginie F: In 1892, Father Brousseau and Virginie Fournier founded the congregation of the Sisters of Notre-Dame du Perpétuel Secours. In 1905, a fire destroyed most of their buildings, and the motherhouse was rebuilt from 1906 to 1910. The Sainte-Anne-des-Montagnes chapel, destroyed by the same fire, was rebuilt and became a place of pilgrimage.
En 1893, après un incendie qui ravage un: In 1893, after a fire ravaged part of Hedleyville, the villages joined together to form the municipality of Limoilou, named in honour of Jacques Cartier, sieur de Limoëlou. Since the territory was still mostly agricultural, developers drew inspiration from New York’s grid: streets running east to west, avenues north to south and brick residential buildings, often more than three storeys.
En 1898, Arthur Saint-Jacques fait const: In 1898, Arthur Saint-Jacques had his first cottage built at Baie de l’Écho, which became a major resort area. In 1934, a dam was built at the lake outlet, serving as a drinking-water reservoir for Québec City; replaced in 1948, it raised the lake level by about 2 metres. The municipality of Lac-Saint-Charles was founded in 1946, and the Sainte-Françoise-Cabrini church was built the following year.

Il honore Mgr Pierre-Flavien Turgeon (17: It honours Bishop Pierre-Flavien Turgeon (1787–1867), the fourth Archbishop of Québec. Its residents are called Saint-Flaviennois (men) and Saint-Flaviennoises (women).
Il honore Mgr Pierre-Herman Dosquet (169: It honours Bishop Pierre-Herman Dosquet (1691–1777), Bishop of Québec from 1734 to 1739. The municipality was called Saint-Octave-de-Dosquet until 1996. Its residents are called Dosquetois and Dosquetoises.
Il honore Noël Brûlart de Sillery (1557-: It honours Noël Brûlart de Sillery (1557-1640), Knight of Malta and commander of Troyes, whose gift enabled the Jesuits to found their mission in 1637.
Il honore Pierre Lambert, arpenteur qui: It honours Pierre Lambert, the surveyor who drew up the plans of the seigneury of Lauzon in 1828. Lauzon recalls that seigneury, which belonged to Jean de Lauzon.
Il honore le pape Sylvestre Ier, fêté le: It honours Pope Sylvester I, whose feast day is December 31. According to tradition, the last saint of the year was chosen because these lands then seemed to be at the end of the world. Its residents are called Sylvestois and Sylvestoises.
Il honore l’abbé Joseph-Nérée Gingras (1: It honours Abbé Joseph-Nérée Gingras (1825-1893), considered the founder of the parish. The patron, Saint Nereus, is a martyr of the early centuries, celebrated with Saint Achilleus.
Il honore saint Basile le Grand, évêque: It honours Saint Basil the Great, bishop of Caesarea and a 4th-century Greek theologian. The name comes from the religious parish, whose registers opened in 1847.
Il honore saint Isidore de Séville, évêq: It honours Saint Isidore of Seville, a Spanish bishop who died in 636, and not Isidore the Farmer. The parish was first called Saint-Isidore-de-Lauzon, after the seigneury of Lauzon.
Il honore saint Malachie (1094-1148), ar: It honours Saint Malachy (1094-1148), Archbishop of Armagh, in Ireland, where most of the first settlers came from. Before the parish was created, the place was called East Frampton.

Il rappelle Charles Couillard (1647-1715: It recalls Charles Couillard (1647-1715), Sieur des Islets and de Beaumont, to whom Jean Talon granted the seigneury in 1672. Until 1998, the municipality’s official name was Saint-Étienne-de-Beaumont.
Il rappelle Charles de Lauson, sieur de: It recalls Charles de Lauson, sieur de Charny, who arrived in New France in 1652. He held the title from his grandmother, the daughter of Guillaume Lottin, lord of Charny, in France.
Il rappelle François Berthelot, seigneur: It recalls François Berthelot, seigneur of Île d’Orléans when the parish was created, and Saint Francis de Sales. The parish was established in 1714 under the name Saint-François-de-Sales.
Il rappelle Georges P. Vanier, militaire: It recalls Georges P. Vanier, soldier, diplomat and Governor General of Canada. The city of Québec-Ouest adopted this name in June 1966, for its golden jubilee.
Il rappelle Honfleur, port de Normandie: It recalls Honfleur, the Normandy port from which Champlain sailed in 1603. According to the Commission de toponymie, it also evokes Saint-Léonard-de-Honfleur, the place of origin of the ancestor of Cardinal Louis-Nazaire Bégin.
Il rappelle Jean de Lauson, premier conc: It recalls Jean de Lauson, first grantee of the Lauzon seigneury in 1636 and governor of New France. The name was chosen in 1867 to avoid confusion with the neighbouring town of Lévis.

Il rappelle Olivier Morel de La Durantay: It recalls Olivier Morel de La Durantaye (1640–1716), captain in the Carignan-Salières regiment, who received the seigneury of La Durantaye in 1672. The parish and the municipality were first called Saint-Gabriel-Archange.
Il rappelle la Jeune-Lorette, l’établiss: It recalls La Jeune-Lorette, the settlement of the Huron-Wendat who arrived at the end of the 17th century from their site at Lorette, now L’Ancienne-Lorette. The village of Saint-Ambroise adopted the name Loretteville in 1913.
Il rappelle la fête de l’Exaltation de l: It recalls the feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, September 14, the day Father Jérôme Lalemant took possession of the seigneury in 1647. Its residents are called San-cruciens and San-cruciennes.
Il rappelle le marchand de bois John Bre: It recalls the lumber merchant John Breakey (1846-1911) and his wife, Helen Henderson, hence the official name Sainte-Hélène-de-Breakeyville, chosen when the parish was established in 1908.
Il rappelle le pape Agapit, ou Agapet Ie: It recalls Pope Agapetus, or Agapetus I, who reigned from 535 to 536. The parish was first called Saint-Agapit-de-Beaurivage, in memory of the seigneury of Beaurivage. Its residents are called Agapitois (men) and Agapitoises (women).
Il rappelle le pont Rouge, un pont gratu: It recalls the Red Bridge, a free bridge built next to the Royal Bridge, now the Pont Déry, which charged a toll. Rue Dupont, for its part, honours Father Charles-François Dupont, parish priest from 1917 to 1933.
Il rappelle l’abbé Étienne Baillargeon,: It recalls Abbé Étienne Baillargeon, parish priest of Saint-Nicolas from 1838 to 1870, who worked on the creation of the parish. “Lauzon” marks the territory’s membership in the former seigneury of Lauzon.

In 1917, a log jam formed near the village and caused what was probably the worst flood in the history of the Chaudière.
La municipalité doit son nom à saint Tit: The municipality owes its name to Saint Titus, a disciple of Saint Paul. In Québec, the word caps refers to more or less bare rock faces, and the Caps region extends between Cap Tourmente and Baie-Saint-Paul.
La municipalité du canton est créée en 1: The township municipality was created in 1845, abolished in 1847 and re-established in 1855. In 1892, it gave way to the parish municipality of Saint-Édouard-de-Frampton. At the end of the 19th century, French Canadians gradually replaced the Irish, who left for industrial centres. In 1997, the municipality adopted the short name Frampton, already common in everyday use.
La municipalité est créée en 1845, aboli: The municipality was created in 1845, abolished in 1847 then reinstated in 1855, and the parish was canonically erected in 1848. The post office, opened in 1852, bore the name Saint-Pierre-Montmagny. The cemetery, laid out from 1908 in terraces on a rock outcrop, is now a designated heritage site. In 2013, the parish celebrated its 300th anniversary.
La municipalité est créée le 14 décembre: The municipality was created on December 14, 1946, from part of the territory of Sainte-Catherine de Portneuf. It became a town on May 20, 2017.
La municipalité est érigée civilement le: The municipality was civilly incorporated on July 11, 1835, and its first mayor was elected in 1845. A church replaced the first chapel in 1862. Saint-Patrice separated from Saint-Sylvestre in 1871, followed by Saint-Séverin in 1872.
La municipalité est érigée le 23 avril 1: The municipality was established on April 23, 1928 under the name Notre-Dame-du-Rosaire. As several parishes already bore that name, it became Beaupré the same year. It obtained town status in 1962.
La municipalité honore Apollinaire de Ra: The municipality honours Apollinaris of Ravenna, a martyred bishop of the 2nd century and a disciple of Saint Peter. Its residents are called Apollinairois (men) and Apollinairoises (women).
La municipalité porte le nom du lac Beau: The municipality takes its name from Lac Beauport, in the south of its territory. It was called Saint-Dunstan-du-Lac-Beauport until 1989.
La municipalité possède de grandes terre: The municipality has large farmland and manufacturing businesses, and is one of the main industrial employment hubs of the Montmagny MRC. In the centre of the village, the heritage site classified in 1988 brings together the former rectory, the church, the former convent of 1883 and the rectory of 1887.
La municipalité prend le nom de Beaumont: The municipality takes the name Beaumont
La municipalité prend le nom de Saints-G: The municipality took the name Saints-Gervais-et-Protais in 1969. It joined the Bellechasse MRC on January 1, 1982. Since November 23, 1991, it has been called Saint-Gervais.
La municipalité se trouve à environ 25 k: The municipality is about 25 km from downtown Québec City. Its economy rests mainly on poultry farming and Village Vacances Valcartier, a water park in summer and a slide centre in winter. The presence of the Canadian Forces Base Valcartier, located in its territory, also strongly influences economic activity.

La paroisse Saint-Louis-de-Pintendre est: The parish of Saint-Louis-de-Pintendre was founded in 1900, and the municipality was born the same year under the name Saint-Louis-de-Gonzague-de-Pintendre. The first name Louis recalls the devotion to this saint of Cardinal Louis-Nazaire Bégin, Archbishop of Québec and a native of Lévis. The name was shortened to Saint-Louis-de-Pintendre in 1951, then to Pintendre in 1986.
La paroisse catholique de Saint-Lambert: The Catholic parish of Saint-Lambert was canonically erected on May 30, 1851. The parish municipality of Saint-Lambert de Lauzon came into being on July 1, 1855.
La paroisse de Saint-François-de-Sales-d: The parish of Saint-François-de-Sales-de-la-Rivière-du-Sud was established canonically in 1842. The parish municipality was created in 1845, abolished in 1847 and reinstated in 1855. The present church was built in the 1860s, followed by the convent in 1883 and the rectory in 1887.
La paroisse de Saint-Gérard-Majella est: The parish of Saint-Gérard-Majella was founded in 1906 and canonically erected in 1909; a parish municipality of the same name was created the same year. Residents then made their living from the timber industry and hunting. In 1914, the first cottages appeared on the road that would become Boulevard Pie-XI, and the resort municipality of Val-Saint-Michel was created in 1933.
La paroisse de Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe: The parish of Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-Lévy was canonically established on September 18, 1694; the 1675 chapel became the Saint-Joseph church in 1721. In 1759, the church served as a military hospital for the British, and General Wolfe’s body was laid there after the Battle of the Plains of Abraham. In 1763, the body of La Corriveau was displayed in a cage in the village.
La paroisse de Saint-Nicolas est fondée: The parish of Saint-Nicolas was founded in 1694, making it one of the oldest in Canada. A first church was built there in 1721. On September 12, 1759, General Wolfe embarked at Saint-Nicolas with part of his troops to go to the Plains of Abraham.
La paroisse de Saint-Romuald-d’Etchemin: The parish of Saint-Romuald-d'Etchemin was separated from Saint-Jean-Chrysostome in 1853, then civilly incorporated in 1854; its church was built in 1855-1856. The population grew from 1,650 in 1856 to 3,993 in 1911, two-thirds French-speaking and about one-third Irish. In 1902, Cistercian nuns from France founded the Notre-Dame-du-Bon-Conseil abbey, where they made chocolate.
La paroisse est reconnue canoniquement e: The parish was canonically recognized in 1909, the year the municipality was incorporated, and the first council met at the home of Mayor Xavier Fortier. On August 4, 1910, lightning destroyed the barely finished church, and parishioners regained a rebuilt church on September 10, 1911. Also in 1910, Herménégilde Ferland moved the family mill to the centre of the village and converted it to steam.
La paroisse est érigée canoniquement en: The parish was canonically erected in 1835, then the municipality of Sainte-Marie-de-Beauce came into being on July 1, 1845. In 1913, the most urbanized part, the village, separated from the parish.

The parish was canonically erected in 1872, from lands of Saint-Gilles, Saint-Patrice-de-Beaurivage, Saint-Lambert-de-Lauzon and Saint-Bernard. The parish municipality was constituted in 1874, the year the post office opened under the name Newbois. A first church, built in 1872, burned down seven years later, and the current church, designed by Siroy Lafleur, was built in 1879 and 1880.
La paroisse est érigée canoniquement le: The parish was established canonically on December 1, 1834 and named in honour of Bishop Pierre-Flavien Turgeon, the future Archbishop of Québec. It was established civilly on September 28, 1843. Even so, it took about fifteen years for the first chapel, and more than 20 years for a resident priest to arrive.

The parish was canonically erected on October 2, 1871, and Arthur Davidson Ross became the first mayor. The first council meeting took place on February 11, 1873, and the minutes were then written in English. On September 14, 1921, Saint-Patrice split into two municipalities, the village and the parish.
La paroisse est érigée civilement en 183: The parish was civilly erected in 1837. A first municipality, Sainte-Marguerite-de-Joliette, was created in 1845 and disappeared in 1847. The current parish municipality came into being on July 1, 1855. The name Joliette recalled Louis Jolliet, to whom the neighbouring seigneury had been granted in 1697.
La paroisse est érigée en 1721, après so: The parish was established in 1721, after breaking away from Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré. In 1759, during the siege of Québec, British troops burned the church and several houses. The current church, one of the oldest preserved in Québec, was blessed on July 8, 1779.
La paroisse et la municipalité de Saint-: The parish and municipality of Saint-Gabriel-Archange were created on August 4, 1910. The first Mass was celebrated in the CN station on June 1, 1910, and a wooden church was erected the same year. The post office opened in 1911 under the name La Durantaye.
La paroisse honore saint Antoine de Pado: The parish honours Saint Anthony of Padua. The name Tilly recalls Pierre-Noël Le Gardeur, sieur de Tilly, who bought the seigneury in 1700. Its residents are called Antoniens (men) and Antoniennes (women).
La paroisse honore saint Joachim, époux: The parish honours Saint Joachim, husband of Saint Anne according to tradition. The name was chosen because the parish broke away from Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré.
La paroisse s’appelait Saint-Paul jusqu’: The parish was called Saint-Paul until 1698. It took the name of Saint Lawrence, deacon of Rome, at the request of François Berthelot, Count of Saint-Laurent, then owner of the island.
La paroisse, dont les limites sont fixée: The parish, whose boundaries were set in 1722, was placed under the protection of Saint Peter in honour of Pierre Blanchet. First served by priests from Saint-Thomas, it received a resident priest in 1751. On March 25, 1776, during the siege of Québec by the Continental Army, the Battle of Saint-Pierre took place near the village between two groups made up mostly of Canadian militiamen.
La paroisse, fondée en 1749, est placée: The parish, founded in 1749, was placed under the patronage of Saint Charles Borromeo, in honour of the seigneur Charles Couillard. Because the Boyer River crosses the territory, it was also once called Saint-Charles-de-la-Rivière-Boyer.
La paroisse, érigée en 1678, porte le no: The parish, established in 1678, bears the name of the Archangel Saint Michael. Until 1842, it was called Saint-Michel-de-la-Durantaye. The word Bellechasse was added in 1992 to distinguish the municipality from Saint-Michel, in Montérégie.
La partie la plus ancienne et la plus de: The oldest and densest part of Québec City. Upper Town concentrates the political and cultural institutions, while Lower Town and Limoilou are mostly residential, with a few industrial areas.

La plage s’étend sur plus d’un kilomètre: The beach stretches over more than a kilometre of sand, and the marina hosts 65 seasonal members. Nicknamed “Sailing Capital” since 1992, the municipality gains nearly 1,000 residents in summer. Cruises to Grosse-Île, a former quarantine station, and to the L’Isle-aux-Grues archipelago leave from its marina.
La population est passée de 4 681 habita: The population grew from 4,681 residents in 2001 to 8,442 in 2021. The town has two elementary schools, a high school that takes students up to Secondary II and a youth centre. In winter, the Grand-Héron sliding park maintains a 2.7 km ice trail through the forest.
La population passe de 5 543 habitants e: The population rose from 5,543 in 1991 to 6,209 in 2001, notably with the arrival of residents northeast of Route 173. On January 1, 2002, Pintendre was merged with Lévis and became an area of the Desjardins borough. In 2006, Lac Baie d’Or was rehabilitated to improve its aquatic ecosystem.
La population vit surtout au village et: The population lives mostly in the village and in the hamlet of Springbrook. Sainte-Marie is about 10 km to the west, and Routes 112, 216 and 275 link Frampton to neighbouring municipalities.
La première gare est construite en 1874: The first station was built in 1874 and was also named Méthot’s Mill. On May 16, 1880, Louis Méthot’s widow transferred her Méthot’s Mill lands to her son Wenceslas. François-Xavier Caron, son-in-law of the pioneer Octave Ratté, was stationmaster from 1885 to 1937, and a second station was built in 1910.
La première gare est détruite lors d’un: The first station was destroyed in a derailment in July 1918, then rebuilt. The furniture industry gradually took hold, and the first furniture factory, Meubles Laurier, was built in 1945. Businesses and services followed.

La route 228 traverse la municipalité et: Route 228 runs through the municipality and reaches Montmagny and Autoroute 20. The astronomical observation park is in the forest, about ten kilometres from the village.
La route 275 relie le village à Saint-Is: Route 275 connects the village to Saint-Isidore, where the Autoroute Robert-Cliche (A-73) passes. A public transit service is available to residents.
La route 277 traverse la municipalité, e: Route 277 runs through the municipality, and an intercity RCM bus service runs Monday to Friday to Lévis. Cyclists on the Cycloroute de Bellechasse have a parking lot and rest area on Rue de la Station.

La route 281 relie le village à Saint-Mi: Route 281 links the village to Saint-Michel-de-Bellechasse and to Route 132, to the north. The municipality has a municipal daycare service.
La route 367 rejoint l’autoroute 40 une: Route 367 reaches Highway 40 about ten kilometres to the south, and Route 369 leads to Shannon. By bike, the Jacques-Cartier/Portneuf trail connects to the Corridor des Cheminots toward Québec City.
La rue Seigneuriale est l’ancienne route: Rue Seigneuriale is the old road that linked these rangs to the heart of the seigneury. In 1725, Beauport had about a hundred families spread over its various rangs. Avenues Saint-Michel and Joseph-Giffard, the former Rang Saint-Joseph, preserve the trace of these roads. The house at 94 Avenue Saint-Michel, built between 1830 and 1860, is among the oldest in the area.

La réserve nationale de faune du Cap-Tou: The Cap-Tourmente National Wildlife Area protects the marshes where greater snow geese stop in spring and fall. It has hiking trails, an interpretation centre and the remains of Champlain’s farm.
La seigneurie de Portneuf devient une ba: The seigneury of Portneuf became a barony in 1681. A chapel-rectory was built in 1709, then a first stone church from 1716 to 1718. Construction of the present church began in 1754.
La seigneurie de Sainte-Croix est concéd: The seigneury of Sainte-Croix was granted in 1637 and reserved for the nuns who would come to settle in Québec City, the Ursulines. On September 14, 1647, the day of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, Father Jérôme Lalemant took possession of it on their behalf, hence the name of the place. The first lands were granted to settlers starting in 1680, including that of Louis Houde in 1682.
La seigneurie de Sainte-Marie est concéd: The seigneury of Sainte-Marie was granted in 1736 to Thomas-Jacques Taschereau. Its name honours his wife, Marie-Claire Fleury de La Gorgendière. The parish was founded the following year, in 1737. Most of the first settlers came from Île d'Orléans and the Côte-de-Beaupré.
La seigneurie devient en 1845 la municip: In 1845, the seigneury became the parish municipality of Notre-Dame-de-Miséricorde-de-Beauport. Toward the end of the 19th century, the village became denser, and lawyers and doctors joined the farmers and craftspeople.
La seigneurie est démantelée en 1836, ap: The seigneury was dismantled in 1836, after the bankruptcy of John Caldwell, and several villages sprang up on the South Shore. The town of Lévis was founded on May 18, 1861, on the initiative of parish priest Joseph-David Déziel. Its name honours François Gaston de Lévis, hero of the Battle of Sainte-Foy in 1760. In the 1860s, the British built three forts there to protect Québec City and its harbour.

La station de ski alpin est sur le terri: The alpine ski resort is in the territory of Beaupré. Saint-Ferréol-les-Neiges occupies the eastern slope of the mountain, and cross-country skiing is done at the Centre national d’entraînement Pierre-Harvey.

La traverse Québec-Lévis part du quai Pa: The Québec–Lévis ferry leaves from Quai Paquet, in Vieux-Lévis. By car, you can reach the Québec and Pierre-Laporte bridges, west of the city, via Autoroute 20. The Société de transport de Lévis also has routes to the North Shore.

La ville comptait 8 468 habitants au rec: The town had 8,468 residents in the 2021 census, more than double the 3,790 counted in 2006. Between 2011 and 2016, its population grew by 29%, the biggest increase in Québec among municipalities of comparable size.
La ville de Lévis est fondée le 18 mai 1: The City of Lévis was founded on May 18, 1861, on the initiative of Father Joseph-David Déziel. In 1867, the village of Lauzon split off from Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-de-Lévy, and the Davie shipyard expanded there in the 1880s. Between 1865 and 1872, the British built three forts on the heights to protect Québec City and its port. Farther south, Église Saint-Louis de Pintendre was built in 1899, and the municipality of Pintendre was born in 1901.
La ville est constituée le 10 juin 1936,: The town was incorporated on June 10, 1936, separating from Sainte-Catherine-de-la-Jacques-Cartier. Thomas Maher was elected alderman on September 30 of that year, and the road around the lake bears his name today.
La ville mesure 11 km d’est en ouest. Da: The town is 11 km from east to west. In the backcountry, the Concessions have about 300 permanent residents, and up to 600 in summer. The Place-de-l’Église heritage site includes Église de La Visitation-de-Notre-Dame, the 1833 rectory and a 17th-century cemetery.
La ville n’a pratiquement pas de commerc: The town has practically no businesses: plan to do your shopping elsewhere. Most properties are secondary residences, and the permanent population is small.
La ville porte le nom de François Gaston: The city is named after François Gaston de Lévis, hero of the Battle of Sainte-Foy in 1760. Long before that, in 1629, Champlain had named the cape Cap de Lévy in honour of Henri de Lévis, Viceroy of New France.
La ville porte le nom du lac qu’elle bor: The town takes its name from the lake it borders. The name appears on maps as early as the 17th century, and the lake has also been called Ontaritzi and Grand lac des Vents.
La ville prend un caractère de banlieue: The city took on a suburban character from the 1960s, and the Bocages neighbourhood developed around 1975. La voie ferrée est inaugurée le 1er mars: The railway line was inaugurated on March 1, 1898, and a station was built there. In 1906, Mrs. Théophile Daigle, born Octavie Lemay, and her family built a sawmill near the railway.

Lac-Sergent fait partie de la MRC de Por: Lac-Sergent is part of the Portneuf MRC, in the Capitale-Nationale region. Lairet est le secteur le plus au nord de: Lairet is the northernmost sector of the La Cité-Limoilou borough, immediately south of Charlesbourg. Lauzon s’étend au bord du fleuve Saint-L: Lauzon stretches along the St. Lawrence River, northeast of Vieux-Lévis, facing Île d’Orléans. On January 15, 1634, the Compagnie des Cent-Associés granted the seigneury of Beauport to Robert Giffard. That same year, he settled two tradesmen there, Jean Guyon and Zacharie Cloutier, joined by the first families from 1636. Around 1654, the Bourg du Fargy, whose name reverses the two syllables of Giffard, became the first embryo of a village in Québec.
Le 15 janvier 1634, la seigneurie de Bea: On January 15, 1634, the seigneury of Beauport was granted to Robert Giffard, a surgeon and apothecary from Normandy. It extends between the Beauport and Montmorency rivers and the St. Lawrence. A first village, Fargy, was created there, and the seigneurial manor was built between 1637 and 1642. Avenue Royale, Avenue des Cascades and Avenue Seigneuriale are its historic roads.
Le 15 mars 1969, la municipalité de paro: On March 15, 1969, the parish municipality took the name Saint-Lambert-de-Lauzon. On June 22, 2013, it changed status and became a municipality.
Le 15 mars 1969, la paroisse prend le no: On March 15, 1969, the parish took the name L’Ancienne-Lorette, then was annexed to Sainte-Foy on December 26, 1970 and became the Laurentien neighbourhood. In 1993, the airport was renamed in honour of Jean Lesage. After the 2002 merger, the Laurentien neighbourhood became the Aéroport neighbourhood, attached since November 1, 2009 to the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.
Le 15 septembre 1845, l’Asile provisoire: On September 15, 1845, the Asile provisoire de Beauport opened its doors: it was the first psychiatric institution in Québec. Entrusted in 1893 to the Sœurs de la Charité de Québec, it formed the municipality of Saint-Michel-Archange from 1897. In 1912, the municipality of Giffard was created west of the Beauport River and named in honour of the first seigneur. Its church, Saint-Ignace-de-Loyola, was blessed on June 6, 1934.

Le 18 octobre 1664, une première messe e: On October 18, 1664, a first Mass was celebrated in Jean Trudelle’s house, and the territory split off from Château-Richer. The same year, Bishop de Laval erected the parish of Saints-Anges-Gardiens, which had about 125 residents. A stone church was built near the river in 1675, then a new church in 1717, on the site of the present church.
Le 1er avril 1738, la seigneurie Saint-G: On April 1, 1738, the Saint-Gilles seigneury was granted to Gilles Rageot de Beaurivage, an important Québec City merchant. It was sold in 1782 to Alexander Fraser. Around 1791, Arthur Davidson, who administered the seigneury on behalf of his young son Walter, had a sawmill and flour mill built on the banks of the Beaurivage River, in the territory of Saint-Gilles.

On April 1, 1738, the Saint-Gilles seigneury, also called the seigneury of Beaurivage, was granted to Gilles Rageot de Beaurivage, a Québec City merchant. The Rivière Noire area was opened to settlement around 1830 by people from Saint-Nicolas, Montmagny and Sainte-Croix.
Le 1er janvier 1867, le village de Lauzo: On January 1, 1867, the village of Lauzon separated from the parish; the name avoids confusion with the neighbouring town of Lévis, founded in 1861. Between 1865 and 1872, the Royal Engineers built Fort Numéro-Un. In 1882, George Taylor Davie bought the Anse aux Sauvages, where the shipyard was born, and the Lorne dry dock was completed in 1886.
Le 1er janvier 1976, Giffard et Saint-Mi: On January 1, 1976, Giffard and Saint-Michel-Archange were merged with Beauport, and the hospital took the name Centre hospitalier Robert-Giffard. Beauport was in turn merged with Québec City in 2002. The neighbourhood holds the largest enclaved farmland in the city, acquired in 2014 by the Dallaire real estate group, which plans to build some 6,500 housing units there.
Le 1er janvier 1976, Sainte-Thérèse-de-L: On January 1, 1976, Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux was annexed to Beauport and became a neighbourhood of it. In 2002, Beauport was merged into Québec City and the neighbourhood was given the number 5-1. On October 2, 2023, residents voted to create a neighbourhood council, authorized by the City on October 24. An organizational meeting was held on December 11, 2023.
Le 1er janvier 2002, Saint-Rédempteur es: On January 1, 2002, Saint-Rédempteur was grouped with eight other municipalities to form the new city of Lévis. Its name now designates a sector that corresponds to the territory of the former city. In 2007, the école de la Ruche hosted the first structure of the Les Aidants scolaires movement, which encourages citizens to volunteer in neighbourhood schools.
Le 1er janvier 2002, Vanier est regroupé: On January 1, 2002, Vanier was amalgamated with Québec City, like several other municipalities. In the June 20, 2004 referendum, 61.3% of voters supported demerger, but that result represented only 23.1% of registered voters, below the required threshold of 35%. Vanier therefore remains a Québec City neighbourhood. In 2008, the Saint-Charles River linear park was inaugurated along its southern boundary.
Le 1er janvier 2002, la ville est fusion: On January 1, 2002, the town was merged into Québec City. In the June 20, 2004 referendum, 61.7% of voters chose to reconstitute it. L’Ancienne-Lorette became a full-fledged town again on January 1, 2006, within the Québec City agglomeration.
Le 1er octobre 1910, la foudre incendie: On October 1, 1910, lightning set fire to the first church, while the new one was already under construction. The current Romanesque church was blessed in 1912. Electricity arrived in the village in 1925, and a bus line connected the parish to Lévis and Québec City by Route 275 starting in 1933.
Le 20 février 1693, le gouverneur Fronte: On February 20, 1693, Governor Frontenac granted the seigneury of Fossambault to Alexandre Peuvret, named in honour of his mother, Marie-Catherine Nau de Fossambault. The seigneury then passed to the Juchereau Duchesnay family. It only truly developed under Michel-Louis Juchereau Duchesnay, hero of the Battle of Châteauguay.
Le 20 janvier 1945, la partie restante d: On January 20, 1945, the remaining part of the municipality, northeast of the original territory, took the name Sainte-Thérèse-de-Lisieux. Joseph-F. Paquet was its mayor from 1944 to 1952. The hyphens were added to the name on March 15, 1969. Boulevard Raymond was named in 1971 in honour of Mayor Raymond-Marie Côté, in office from 1968 to 1972.
Le 20 mai 2017, la municipalité de Shann: On May 20, 2017, the municipality of Shannon changed its status to that of a town. In the 2021 census, it had 6,432 residents, on a territory neighbouring Canadian Forces Base Valcartier.
Le 21 septembre 1963, la municipalité pr: On September 21, 1963, the municipality took the name Neufchâtel, in tribute to residents who fought at Neufchâtel-en-Bray, in Normandy, during the Second World War. It gained town status on July 11, 1964. Inaugurated in 1970, the building at 9150 Boulevard de l’Ormière then served as fire station and town hall.
Le 24 décembre 1912, le lieutenant-gouve: On December 24, 1912, the lieutenant governor proclaimed the municipality of Saint-Octave-de-Dosquet, named in honour of Bishop Pierre-Herman Dosquet, Bishop of Québec. Because of a procedural defect in the council election, the Gazette officielle did not announce it until February 9, 1918. Work on the rectory began in 1915, and the church was blessed on July 16, 1922, by Cardinal Louis-Nazaire Bégin.
Le 25 mars 1776, pendant le siège de Qué: On March 25, 1776, during the siege of Québec by the Continental Army, pro-American forces routed Loyalist militiamen near the village. Both sides were made up largely of Canadian militiamen.
Le 26 juillet. C’est le principal rassem: July 26. It is the main gathering of the year at the shrine and the high point of a novena.
Le 26 mars 1902, la municipalité de La P: On March 26, 1902, the municipality of La Petite-Rivière was created; its territory roughly corresponds to the present-day neighbourhoods of Duberger and Vanier. In 1916, its eastern part split off to form Québec-Ouest, the future city of Vanier. In the early 1950s, western La Petite-Rivière still had about twenty farms, linked to Québec City and L’Ancienne-Lorette by Chemin Saint-Charles Nord, today’s Boulevard Père-Lelièvre.
Le 27 mai 1914, un incendie détruit l’ég: On May 27, 1914, a fire destroyed the church, which was rebuilt the following year using some of the original stones. A covered bridge was built over the Filkars River in 1927. In the 1950s, at the height of the Cold War, the Royal Canadian Air Force installed a radar base at the top of Mont Sainte-Marguerite, in service until 1964.
Le 27 mars 1650, Étienne Racine reçoit l: On March 27, 1650, Étienne Racine received the first land granted and farmed at this location. The 1658 land register names about thirty early settlers, including Étienne de Lessard, Claude Poulin and Noël Racine.
Le 28 avril 1760, le chevalier de Lévis: On April 28, 1760, the Chevalier de Lévis defeated General Murray's British troops at Sainte-Foy, without being able to retake Québec City. In the 19th century, notables built villas there and ran farms; four of them, built between 1849 and 1856, gave Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois its name.
Le 29 mars 1995, le village et la parois: On March 29, 1995, the village and the parish came together to form the town of Saint-Raymond. The former railway that led to Rivière-à-Pierre and Lac-Saint-Jean has become a cycling trail. Wood and leather remain at the heart of the local economy.
Le 29 octobre 1672, l’intendant Jean Tal: On October 29, 1672, Intendant Jean Talon granted the territory to Claude-Sébastien de Villieu, a lieutenant in the Carignan regiment. The 1681 census names five early settlers there. In 1700, the Villieu family sold the seigneury to Pierre-Noël Le Gardeur, sieur de Tilly, and it has been called Tilly ever since.
Le 3 décembre 1655, Pierre Maheut et Jea: On December 3, 1655, Pierre Maheut and Jean Trudelle committed by contract to clear five arpents of land east of the Montmorency Falls, in present-day Boischatel. On September 29, 1657, they became the first two permanent settlers. Most settlers came from Normandy.
Le 3,5 % du TAL n’est pas un tarif: The TAL’s 3.5% is not a fee schedule
Le 31 janvier 2008, la papetière, devenu: On January 31, 2008, the paper mill, by then Abitibi-Bowater, stopped production, and the closure became permanent. Demolition of the mill began in late March 2011. The town remains a service centre for the Portneuf region.
Le 8 février 1856, le territoire devient: On February 8, 1856, the territory became the civil parish of Saint-Colomb-de-Sillery, detached from Sainte-Foy and Québec City. The chemin Cap-Rouge, which served the large estates, took the name Chemin Saint-Louis in 1929. In the 1930s, the architect Robert Blatter built the first International Style residences in Québec there, including the maison Kerhulu. On May 10, 1947, the municipality became the Cité de Sillery.
Le 9 mars 1916, Québec-Ouest se détache: On March 9, 1916, Québec-Ouest separated from La Petite-Rivière. Land companies wanted to build a residential area there for Québec City workers. During the Depression, low-priced houses attracted families, and the population rose from 600 to 2,132 between 1928 and 1933.
Le Boisé du Cap, avec ses sentiers et sa: The Boisé du Cap, with its trails and observation tower, the Sentier du Moulin along the rivière des Îles Brûlées, and the Halte de la Chaudière, open in summer with access to the river. The village also has several parks, including Parc du Faubourg and the Récré-O-Parc.
Le Centre Nature est fondé en 1976 par d: The Centre Nature was founded in 1976 by citizens who loved cross-country skiing. In 2000, the parish municipality of Saint-Basile and the village of Saint-Basile-Sud amalgamated to form the town of Saint-Basile. In 2005, the community centre was named after Ernest-J. Papillon.
Le Centre Nature offre une trentaine de: The Centre Nature offers about thirty kilometres of trails for walking, snowshoeing, mountain biking and fat biking, as well as inner-tube sliding in winter. Its trails run along the Chaude River and through maple groves and forests.
Le Centre Vidéotron, le Centre de foires: The Centre Vidéotron, the Centre de foires, the Guy-Lafleur pavilion, the Grand Marché de Québec and the former Colisée de Québec, which opened in 1949 and closed in 2015. The site hosts trade shows, concerts and sporting events.
Le Centre de plein air de Beauport, en b: The Centre de plein air de Beauport, along the Montmorency River, Parc de la Rivière-Beauport, Parc Jean-Guyon and, to the north, Mont Saint-Louis and Mont Saint-André.
Le Code civil interdit aussi de refuser: The Civil Code also prohibits refusing to lease to a woman because she is pregnant or to a person because they have children, unless the size of the dwelling justifies it; punitive damages are possible[4].
Le Code civil permet au locataire d’agir: The Civil Code allows the tenant to act themselves when a repair is urgent and necessary to preserve the unit or its enjoyment[1]. The TAL gives examples[2]:
Le Demolition fest, le principal festiva: The Demolition fest, the municipality's main festival, is held on the last weekend of May.
Le Domaine Joly-De Lotbinière, avec son: The Domaine Joly-De Lotbinière, with its 1851 manor house and gardens, the church completed in 1915 and the chute du Petit Saut. In spring and fall, thousands of snow geese stop on the river flats.
Le Domaine Taschereau, un parc écologiqu: The Domaine Taschereau, an ecological park laid out on the former seigneurial estate, with wetlands and a bird-watching site. You can also visit the Maison J.-A. Vachon, the Musée de l'aviation and the Le Forgeron d'or économusée.
Le Domaine devient un parc public: The Domaine becomes a public park
Le Festival de la Gargouille est fondé e: The Festival de la Gargouille was founded in 1983. In the early 2000s, the municipality modernized its water and sewer systems, which supported the expansion of residential and industrial areas. The recreation complex, with its covered rink, was inaugurated in 2010, and the parish celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2022.
Le Grand incendie de Québec rase Saint-S: The Great Fire of Québec razed Saint-Sauveur in 1866. In 1889, another fire destroyed about 500 houses and left four to five thousand people homeless. The same year, citizens approved annexation to Québec City by referendum, which brought running water, sewers, sidewalks, paved streets and electric lighting in less than three years.
Le Guide Local de l’Immobilier <em>à Mon: The Local Real Estate Guide in Montréal and Québec City.

Le Manoir du Lac Delage accueille les vi: The Manoir du Lac Delage welcomes visitors, and the Empire 47 centre is dedicated to mountain biking. Annual cycling events are held there, such as XTerra and Popcycle47, a fatbike event.
Le Musée maritime de l’île d’Orléans, av: The Musée maritime de l’île d’Orléans, with the 1837 Godbout boatworks, and the 1860 church. The wharf and marina give access to the river.
Le Musée maritime de l’île d’Orléans, pr: The Musée maritime de l’île d’Orléans, owned by the municipality, receives about 15,000 visitors a year. It includes the Godbout boatworks, built in 1837, and an interpretation centre on shipbuilding. The current church dates from 1860, and its interior decoration, completed in 1863 by Charles Baillairgé, uses moulded plaster ornaments rather than wood.
Le Métrobus 802 dessert la station Fleur: Métrobus 802 serves the Fleur-de-Lys station, and Autoroutes Laurentienne and Félix-Leclerc border the neighbourhood. Handy for getting downtown or to Charlesbourg.
Le Plateau, aussi appelé plateau de Sain: Plateau, also called the Sainte-Foy plateau, is one of the seven neighbourhoods of the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough. It stretches largely between the Duplessis and Henri-IV highways. Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois, Chemin Sainte-Foy, Boulevard du Versant-Nord, Boulevard Hochelaga and Avenue Duchesneau are its main arteries.
Le Relevé 31 vous est remis au plus tard: Your Relevé 31 is provided to you no later than the last day of February, for the previous year. It is used to claim the solidarity tax credit.
Le Séminaire y produit nourriture et boi: The Séminaire produced food and firewood there. After the American troops passed through in 1775–1776, it had the estate house rebuilt in 1777, and it became a country retreat for its priests and students. The estate took the name Maizerets in the mid-19th century, in honour of Louis Ango de Maizerets, superior of the Séminaire. In 1889, the Québec, Montmorency and Charlevoix railway ran along the tidal flats with a stop at Maizerets.
Le TAL donne précisément l’exemple des c: The TAL specifically gives the example of keys: the lessor cannot require an additional sum “to guarantee the return of the keys.” Postdated cheques cannot be imposed, but the parties can choose this method of payment by mutual agreement[2].
Le TAL ne publie plus une grille de pour: The TAL no longer publishes a grid of percentages by type of unit. A single method, simpler and more predictable, applies to all renewed leases. The calculator above uses its official rules; only the annual rate will change in January.
Le TAL publie chaque année le pourcentag: Each year the TAL publishes the base percentage and an online calculation tool: use the version that matches the year covered by the notice[3].
The TAL publishes the annual rate in January. The calculator switches to the 2027 rate as soon as it is published; until then, it uses the 2026 rate.
Le TAL qualifie ce recours de mesure d’e: The TAL describes this remedy as an exceptional measure, to be used with caution and in good faith. The repair must be limited to the essentials, on a temporary basis[2].
Le TAL utilise un pourcentage de « frais: The TAL uses a “management fees” percentage in its rent calculation parameters. It is a regulatory parameter, not a market rate: it says nothing about what a manager charges.
Le Trait-Carré est délimité par le boule: The Trait-Carré is bounded by Boulevard Jean-Talon to the north, Autoroute Laurentienne to the west, Boulevard Henri-Bourassa to the east and the Corridor des Cheminots to the south. The 1re Avenue crosses it from north to south and Boulevard Louis-XIV from west to east. Residential, it is also the institutional heart of the borough; most businesses line Boulevard Henri-Bourassa.
Le Tribunal administratif du logement (T: The Tribunal administratif du logement (TAL) replaced the Régie du logement on August 31, 2020. It decides disputes between tenants and landlords of residential units in Québec, and publishes the rent increase calculation method each year.
Le Vieux-Bourg est délimité par le fleuv: Vieux-Bourg is bounded by the St. Lawrence River to the south, Autoroute Félix-Leclerc to the north, the Beauport River to the west and Rue Francheville to the east. Autoroute Dufferin-Montmorency, Boulevard Sainte-Anne and Avenue Royale cross it from west to east; Rue Seigneuriale, Rue Labelle and Boulevard des Chutes, from north to south. Its terrain gradually rises toward the north, from about twenty metres to nearly a hundred.
Le Vieux-Bourg, le plus ancien, conserve: Vieux-Bourg, the oldest, preserves the Église de la Nativité-de-Notre-Dame and many historic houses on Avenue Royale, which are part of the historic district of Beauport. The Saint-Michel neighbourhood, along Autoroute Félix-Leclerc, has a 16-screen cinema, big-box stores and car dealerships.
Le Vieux-Limoilou est délimité par la ri: Vieux-Limoilou is bounded by the Rivière Saint-Charles to the south, Boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, Avenue Eugène-Lamontagne and 18e Rue to the north, and the Laurentienne highway to the west. Its grid plan is crossed from north to south by 1re Avenue; 3e Avenue is its commercial artery, with its cafés, restaurants and boutiques.
Le Vieux-Moulin est limité à l’est par l: Vieux-Moulin is bounded on the east by the Beauport River, on the south by the St. Lawrence River, and on the north and west by the borough's boundaries. It is crossed by Autoroutes Félix-Leclerc and Dufferin-Montmorency, Avenue Royale, Boulevard Sainte-Anne and Avenues Saint-David, Clemenceau, D'Estimauville and du Bourg-Royal. North of Autoroute Félix-Leclerc, the Promenades Beauport has nearly 120 shops.
Le Vieux-Québec est-il dans La Cité-Limo: Is Old Québec in La Cité-Limoilou?
Le Vieux-Québec fait partie du quartier: Vieux-Québec is part of the Vieux-Québec–Cap-Blanc–Colline parlementaire neighbourhood, in La Cité-Limoilou. Rue Saint-Jean, Terrasse Dufferin, Place Royale and the Petit-Champlain district are emblematic spots.
Le Zoo Miller, où l’on voit une centaine: The Zoo Miller, where you can see about a hundred animals along trails, the Frampton Brasse microbrewery and the Dorchester golf club, an 18-hole course. The former water mill, built in 1862, was moved to Route 275.
Le bail continue; le locataire peut cont: The lease continues; the tenant can contest the refusal before the TAL
Le bail est reconduit, et c’est au propr: The lease is renewed, and it is up to the landlord to ask the TAL to set the rent, within the month following the refusal. Keep the tax bills, the insurance policy and the work invoices: the tribunal asks for them.
Le bail est résilié à la date de cession: The lease is terminated on the assignment date stated in the notice
Le boisé de Marly, le boisé des Compagno: The Boisé de Marly, the Boisé des Compagnons-de-Cartier, the Boisé Neilson, Parc du Campanile and Parc Saint-Benoît. Parc de la Plage-Jacques-Cartier, on the riverfront, is very close.
Le bon moment</strong> : au Québec, beau: The right timing: in Québec, many leases end on June 30; planning the re-rental as early as winter avoids missing the season.
Le boulevard Champigny, ouvert en 1958,: Boulevard Champigny, opened in 1958, became Boulevard Maurice-Duplessis in 1961, then Autoroute Duplessis in 1981. The Sainte-Geneviève and Saint-Mathieu-Apôtre parishes were created in 1960 and 1964. The Sainte-Geneviève church, on Avenue D’Amours, was built in 1965–1966 to plans by the architects Laroche, Ritchot and Déry, with a cedar-shingle roof and white stucco walls.
Le boulevard Henri-Bourassa et l’autorou: Boulevard Henri-Bourassa and Autoroute Félix-Leclerc quickly link the neighbourhood to Charlesbourg and Beauport. Access to the Domaine de Maizerets is free in every season.
Le boulevard Henri-Bourassa relie le qua: Boulevard Henri-Bourassa connects the neighbourhood to Limoilou; Autoroute Félix-Leclerc runs through it to the south.
Le boulevard Henri-Bourassa, le boulevar: Boulevard Henri-Bourassa, Boulevard Louis-XIV (Route 369), Boulevard du Loiret and Autoroute Félix-Leclerc (Autoroute 40).
Le boulevard Louis-XIV traverse le quart: Boulevard Louis-XIV crosses the neighbourhood from east to west and connects it to Beauport and the centre of Charlesbourg.
Le boulevard Louis-XIV, au sud du quarti: Boulevard Louis-XIV, in the south of the neighbourhood, connects Beauport to Charlesbourg; Boulevard Raymond and Boulevard Lloyd-Welch cross it from north to south.
Le boulevard Sainte-Anne (route 138) et: Boulevard Sainte-Anne (Route 138) and Avenue Royale (Route 360) connect Beaupré to Québec City, about 40 km to the west. Route 360 also leads to the Mont Sainte-Anne resort.
Le boulevard Sainte-Anne (route 138) mèn: Boulevard Sainte-Anne (Route 138) leads to Québec City in about thirty minutes. Pilgrims are numerous near the basilica in summer, especially around July 26.
Le boulevard de l’Ormière, l’autoroute H: Boulevard de l’Ormière, Autoroute Henri-IV, Avenue Chauveau, Boulevard Bastien, Boulevard des Cimes, Boulevard Saint-Claude and Rue Monseigneur-Cooke.
Le bureau de poste prend le nom de Saint: The post office took the name Saint-Rédempteur-de-Lévis in 1966. The Pierre-Laporte Bridge, opened in 1970 less than 5 km away, accelerated the village’s development. From the late 1970s, residential developments occupied the former farmland, then the woodlots at the far end of those lands. In 1981, Saint-Rédempteur obtained city status.
Le bureau de poste prend son nom actuel: Post office takes its present name
Le calcul jour par jour avec les chiffre: The day-by-day calculation using CMHC figures for the Québec City region, and the levers that shorten the rental period.
Le calcul repose sur des pièces : compte: The calculation relies on supporting documents: municipal and school tax bills, insurance premiums, invoices for major work and invoices for added services or accessories. Gather them before sending the notice. An increase backed by verifiable figures is easier to discuss and easier to defend before the TAL.
Le calculateur applique la méthode du TA: The calculator applies the TAL method in force since January 2026: base rate, taxes, insurance and work.
Le campus de l’Université Laval et le CH: The Université Laval campus and the CHUL make it a major hub for studies and health care. Many residents still identify with the former parish neighbourhoods, each organized around a church, a park and an elementary school.
Le campus de l’Université Laval, le CHUL: The Université Laval campus, the CHUL and the shopping centres of Boulevard Laurier, including Place Sainte-Foy and Place Laurier.
Le campus principal de l’Université Lava: Université Laval’s main campus, Cégep Garneau, Cégep de Sainte-Foy and Champlain Regional College St. Lawrence.
Le candidat qui refuse l’enquête peut fo: An applicant who refuses the credit check can provide their own credit report, a bank statement of account, a reference letter or proof of payment of bills, for example electricity or telecommunications[1]. The landlord cannot refuse an applicant for not providing their health insurance or driver’s licence numbers[1].
Le candidat retenu est avisé par écrit;: The selected applicant is notified in writing; the others receive a reply.
Le canton de Frampton est proclamé le 10: The township of Frampton was proclaimed on July 10, 1806. The same day, the Crown granted 59 lots, or 11,029 acres, to Pierre-Édouard Desbarats and his associates. A translator at the Québec Gazette and the Legislative Assembly of Lower Canada, Desbarats then sold lots to Irish settlers.
Le canton d’Armagh est créé en 1799 et p: Armagh Township was created in 1799 and bears the name of a county in Ulster, Northern Ireland. Despite the name, the first residents were not Irish. Charles Turgeon, originally from Saint-Vallier, settled there around 1838, and other settlers arrived from Saint-Vallier, Saint-Michel and Saint-Raphaël.
Le centre de Québec est à une trentaine: Downtown Québec City is about thirty kilometres away via Avenue Sainte-Brigitte. The Traverse de Laval offers a second road link, to Lac-Beauport to the west.
Le centre hospitalier Paul-Gilbert ouvre: The Paul-Gilbert hospital centre opened in 1987, and new neighbourhoods were built in the late 1980s and early 1990s. In 1992, the Joffre roundhouse was designated a National Historic Site of Canada. In 1998, Parc des Chutes-de-la-Chaudière was transferred to the towns of Charny and Saint-Nicolas. On January 1, 2002, Charny was merged with eight other municipalities to form the new City of Lévis.
Le centre-ville de Québec est à environ: Downtown Québec City is about 20 minutes away. PLUmobile public transit serves L’Ange-Gardien from Monday to Friday, with connections to Québec City and Sainte-Foy.
Downtown Québec City is about 25 km away. Route 371 runs through the municipality and connects it to the La Haute-Saint-Charles borough of Québec City to the south.
Le centre-ville de la basse-ville : rest: The downtown of the Lower Town: restaurants, offices, tech companies and an active cultural life.
Le centre-ville longe la rivière Chaudiè: Downtown runs along the Chaudière River, which overflowed in 2019. Before signing a lease, ask whether the unit is in a flood zone.
Le cessionnaire reprend le bail tel quel: The assignee takes over the lease as is. They are not a new tenant: they cannot have their rent set by the TAL on the ground that the rent is higher than the lowest rent paid in the last 12 months[2].
Le changement s’est fait en un mois. Les: The change took a month. Tenants received the notice and Cléo took over the same day.
Le chef-lieu de la Nation huronne-wendat: The capital of the Huron-Wendat Nation, where Wendat culture is alive and well. Vieux-Wendake brings together old houses, craft shops and restaurants.
Le chemin Ross devient route de Valleau: Chemin Ross becomes Route de Valleau
Le chemin de fer Lévis and Kennebec, con: The Lévis and Kennebec railway, built by Charles Armstrong Scott and Louis-Napoléon Larochelle, reached Scott Jonction on June 20, 1875. After the line was bought by the Quebec Central in 1881, a bridge was built over the Chaudière to connect it to the network coming from Sherbrooke. The Scott-Jonction station gave the village its name.
Le chemin de fer Lévis et Kennebec trave: The Lévis and Kennebec railway crossed the parish in the 1870s, and the station stayed open until about 1965. In 1893, Joseph Mercier built a first waterworks with wooden pipes, which served the village until 1967.
Le chemin de fer arrive dans la région e: The railway reached the region in 1869 and encouraged the opening of sawmills. In 1888, the Lac Saint-Joseph railway station was at Duchesnay. Notary Cyprien Labrecque, in 1896, was one of the lake’s first summer residents.

The railway reached the region in 1869, and cottage life began in 1896, when the notary Cyprien Labrecque had a residence built. Notaries, doctors and merchants from Québec City followed. The Saint-Joseph-du-Lac chapel, built entirely of wood, was built in 1902.
Le chemin de fer arrive en 1897 et fait: The railway arrived in 1897 and made the village a stopping place for travellers and goods. The telephone followed in 1905. In 1919, the village of Francoeur separated from the parish.
Le chemin de la Liseuse, une piste cycla: The chemin de la Liseuse, a bike path along the Jacques-Cartier River, the Duchesnay tourist resort and the Grand-Héron sliding park, with its 2.7 km ice trail through the forest.
Le chemin du Roy traverse la seigneurie: The Chemin du Roy crossed the seigneury from 1716. In 1734, the Augustinian Hospitallers of Québec became the seigneurs of Saint-Augustin. They remained so until the seigneurial system was abolished, and the revenues went toward the upkeep of the Hôtel-Dieu de Québec.
