Le compte où sont déposés les loyers : s: The account where rent is deposited: separate or in trust?
Le consentement d’une personne de moins: The consent of a person under 14 is given by the person with parental authority.
Le constructeur d’autocars Prevost, fond: The bus manufacturer Prevost, founded by Eugène Prévost, a native of Sainte-Claire. The company, owned by Volvo, operates an assembly plant in the municipality.
Le contrat de gestion dure 12 mois et se: The management contract lasts 12 months and renews. To not renew it, send written notice at least 30 days before its end; you can also end it at any time in writing. We then hand over leases, files and keys to the person you designate.
Le corridor des Cheminots, une piste cyc: The Corridor des Cheminots, a bike path that runs along the south of the neighbourhood, leads to the Domaine de Maizerets.
Le coût d’un logement vide: The cost of an empty unit
Le coût net de la gestion est donc plus: The net cost of management is therefore lower than the advertised percentage. Check your situation with your accountant.
Le curé Joseph Élie dit Breton arrive à: Priest Joseph Élie dit Breton arrived at the end of 1883 and directed the construction of a fieldstone church, from plans by Georges-Émile Tanguay. He also had a sawmill built near the church in 1884. The parish was canonically erected in 1886, and the municipality was constituted in 1887.
Le cœur urbain de Lévis, avec le Vieux-L: The urban heart of Lévis, with Vieux-Lévis and Vieux-Lauzon near the river, residential neighbourhoods on the plateau and a more rural landscape toward Pintendre.
Le dossier de chaque locataire était inc: Each tenant’s file was incomplete. Everything was taken over, filed and scanned before the first report.
Le délai de 15 jours et les trois répons: The 15-day period and the three possible responses
Le délai de réponse aux urgences, la nui: The response time for emergencies, at night and on weekends.
Le délai dont le locataire dispose pour: The time the tenant has to refuse, which is one month after receipt.
Le développement reprend en 1940 avec l’: Development resumed in 1940 with the opening of new streets. Founded in 1943, the L'Habitation familiale cooperative had Rue Eymard and several others opened to make home ownership accessible to families. The new Jeffery Hale Hospital was inaugurated in 1956, when the population was close to 8,000. In 1988, the area, until then part of the Montcalm neighbourhood, became the Saint-Sacrement neighbourhood.
Le développement résidentiel de Lairet s: Residential development in Lairet took place mostly in the 1940s and 1950s, north of the Exposition provinciale grounds. Several churches were built there, including Sainte-Claire-d’Assise (1951), Saint-Albert-le-Grand (1952) and Saint-Paul-Apôtre (1960). Having become an open sewer in its urbanized section, the Rivière Lairet was channelled in three phases, in 1960, 1965 and 1967, and almost entirely disappeared underground.
Le développement résidentiel explose dan: Residential development exploded in the 1950s: the parish had 2,500 families in 1955. In the 1960s, the shoreline south of the neighbourhood was filled in for Autoroute Dufferin-Montmorency and the Port of Québec facilities. The City acquired the Domaine de Maizerets in 1979 to make it a public park, and the neighbourhood was officially created in 1988, when Limoilou was divided into three.
Le faubourg Saint-Jean existe depuis le: The Saint-Jean suburb dates back to the French Regime, west of the fortified Upper Town. Today’s Rue Saint-Jean was laid out as a road in 1667, on land largely held by the Ursulines and the Hospitalières de l’Hôtel-Dieu. A hamlet of craftsmen began to be subdivided there in 1722 and had about thirty houses by 1740. In 1775, during the American invasion, the British army had the suburb razed to clear the fortifications.
Le faubourg se reconstruit après 1780. E: The suburb was rebuilt after 1780. In 1783, the nuns of the Hôtel-Dieu entrusted the subdivision of their lands to surveyor Vondenvelden, who laid out streets at right angles. The Berthelot market, opened in 1825, gave the suburb greater independence, and the population exceeded 9,000 residents by 1840. From the 1830s, families of Irish origin settled in the neighbouring Saint-Louis suburb, around Rues Saint-Patrick, O’Connell and Scott.
Le fil complet transmis au gestionnaire: The full thread passed on to the manager
Le hameau du Lac-Vert, au bord d’un lac: The hamlet of Lac-Vert, on the shore of a lake of about 33 ha, has been home since 1974 to the Alphonse-Tardif observatory of the Collège de Lévis. The local economy relies on agriculture, maple production and forestry work.
Le lac Delage couvre 0,49 km² et atteint: Lac Delage covers 0.49 km² and reaches a depth of 26 m. It drains into Lac Saint-Charles through the Rivière Delage, and the Rivière des Hurons touches the town’s southern boundary.
Le lac Larron rattaché au canton de Ston: Lac Larron attached to Stoneham Township
Le lac Saint-Joseph couvre 11,31 km² et: Lac Saint-Joseph covers 11.31 km² and measures 22.4 km around. The Duchesnay tourist resort, operated by Sépaq, occupies most of the municipal territory.
Le lac Saint-Joseph, où la Corporation n: Lac Saint-Joseph, where the Corporation nautique de Fossambault runs summer sailing, kayaking and swimming activities for young people. Nearby, the Duchesnay resort has hiking, cross-country skiing and snowshoeing trails.
Le lac apparaît sous le nom de lac Saint: The lake appears as Lac Saint-Joseph on a map by Nicolas Sanson in 1656. In the early 19th century, it was also known by the Indigenous name Ontaritzi, and it was called Grand lac des Vents. The name Lac Saint-Joseph became official in 1912.
Le lac figure sur une carte de Sanson: The lake appears on a Sanson map
Le lac, alors appelé lac Larron, est rat: The lake, then called Lac Larron, was attached to Stoneham Township when it was created in 1790. In the 19th century, the English-speaking bourgeoisie frequented it, and the painter Cornelius Krieghoff came to paint there. Around 1900, the Gails family established Rockland Farm there, and then the Webster family, owners in 1939, had a ski slope built there in the 1940s.
Le locataire a 1 mois pour accepter, ref: The tenant has 1 month to accept, refuse and stay, or leave; silence counts as acceptance. If the tenant refuses and stays, the landlord has 1 month to ask the TAL to set the rent.
Le locataire a <strong>un mois</strong>: The tenant has one month after receiving the notice to respond. If they do not respond, they are deemed to have refused to leave the unit[1].
Le locataire a un mois pour répondre: The tenant has one month to respond
Le locataire avise par écrit, avec le no: The tenant gives written notice, with the name and address of the proposed person. The landlord has 15 days to respond; silence counts as consent (Civil Code of Québec, arts. 1870 and 1871).
Le locataire doit aviser le propriétaire: The tenant must notify the landlord in writing and give the name and address of the person to whom they want to assign the lease. Since Bill 31, the notice must also state the planned assignment date[1]. The TAL offers a notice form[4].
Le locataire est en défaut dès le lendem: The tenant is in default as of the day after the due date. The landlord is not required to accept a partial payment[2].
Le locataire peut demander au TAL de se: The tenant can ask the TAL to rule on the reasons for the refusal. According to the decision summaries published by the TAL, the tribunal can, among other things, declare the assignment valid or award damages[5].
Le locataire peut refuser l’accès avant: The tenant can refuse access before 7 a.m. and after 7 p.m., except for urgent work[1].
Le locataire évite la résiliation s’il p: The tenant avoids termination by paying, before judgment, the rent owed, interest and costs[1]. On the day of the hearing, bring an up-to-date statement of the amounts owed and the payments received.
Le logement relève du Conseil de la Nati: Housing falls under the Conseil de la Nation huronne-wendat, and some rental units are intended primarily for Wendat people. Check with the Council before starting your search.
Le loyer actuel est multiplié par le tau: The current rent is multiplied by the annual rate published by the TAL.
Le loyer inscrit au bail, sans les servi: The rent stated in the lease, excluding services.
Le manoir seigneurial disparaît à la fin: The seigneurial manor disappeared in the late 1870s, and the 1849 church, designed by Charles Baillargé, was destroyed by fire on January 24, 1890. Its replacement burned in turn on February 21, 1916, taking with it the registers kept since 1673; the current church reuses its plans. In the meantime, on February 19, 1913, the urbanized core became the village of Beauport, which obtained city status in 1924.
Le marché locatif de Québec en chiffres: The Québec City rental market in numbers
Le modèle officiel du TAL, validé par un: The TAL’s official template, validated by a person.
Le moratoire peut prendre fin plus tôt s: The moratorium can end earlier if the vacancy rate published by CMHC reaches 3%, after a notice published in the Gazette officielle; the government can also exempt territories from the moratorium[2]. Check the status of the moratorium with the TAL before sending a notice.
Le motif sérieux concerne en général le: The serious reason generally concerns the assignee, for example their ability to pay the rent. The landlord must give their reasons within 15 days, otherwise they are deemed to have consented[1]. The TAL publishes a response form for notices sent since February 21, 2024[3].
Le même courriel vous indique comment ac: The same email tells you how to activate your access.
Le nom Beaupré est attesté en 1636, anné: The name Beaupré is documented in 1636, the year seven partners formed the Compagnie de Beaupré. Their seigneury extended from the Montmorency River to Baie-Saint-Paul and included Île d’Orléans. According to a popular explanation, Breton sailors admired the coastal meadow and cried out “Oh! le beau pré”.
Le nom Château-Richer apparaît sur une c: The name Château-Richer appears on a map by the surveyor Jean Bourdon in the early 1640s. It then referred to the promontory where the church stands, and its origin remains obscure. The first resident priest arrived in 1661, and the parish of La Visitation-de-Notre-Dame was canonically erected on October 30, 1678.
Le nom LeaseLane, son logo, son slogan,: The LeaseLane name, its logo, its slogan, the Cléo character, the texts, the images and the site’s code belong to Solutions locatives LeaseLane inc. or its licensors. You may view and print the content for personal, non-commercial use. Any other reproduction requires our written authorization.
Le nom Lebourgneuf réunit la fin de « Ch: The name Lebourgneuf combines the end of “Charlesbourg” and the start of “Neufchâtel,” the two sectors that frame it. The neighbourhood corresponds to the former municipality of Charlesbourg-Ouest, separated from Charlesbourg in 1952, annexed to Québec City in 1973 and renamed in 1988. Boulevard Lebourgneuf has carried this name since 1977.
Le nom apparaît en 1904 avec le bureau d: The name appeared in 1904 with the Saint-Émile-de-Québec post office. The parish, established in 1925, was placed under the patronage of Saint Emilian, a 3rd-century martyr of Carthage.
Le nom de Saint-Émile apparaît en 1904,: The name Saint-Émile appeared in 1904, with the opening of the Saint-Émile-de-Québec post office. The parish was established on August 14, 1925, and the church, designed by architect Émile-Georges Rousseau, was built in 1926–1927. The municipality of Saint-Émile was founded in 1929 and celebrated the 50th anniversary of its founding in 1975.
Le nom de la municipalité rappelle Pierr: The municipality’s name recalls Pierre Lambert, the surveyor who drew up the plans of the seigneury of Lauzon in 1828, then those of the town of Aubigny, now part of Lévis, in 1848. Lauzon refers to the seigneury of Jean de Lauzon.
Le nom de lac Saint-Joseph est officiali: The name Lac Saint-Joseph becomes official
Le nom du lac est en usage avant 1829. S: The lake’s name was in use before 1829. According to the most widely held explanation, it recalls an old soldier who held the rank of sergeant and lived on its shores. Another theory sees it as a corruption of serre-joint (clamp), a carpenter’s tool whose shape the lake resembles.
Le nom est attribué en 1694 à la demande: The name was assigned in 1694 at the request of Claude de Bermen de La Martinière, who wanted to recall his home parish, Saint-Nicolas-de-la-Ferté, in France. It also evokes Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop.
Le nom est une variante de Limoëlou, le: The name is a variant of Limoëlou, Jacques Cartier’s manor in Saint-Malo, Brittany. The working-class villages north of the Saint-Charles River adopted it in 1893.
Le nom honore Henri II, empereur du Sain: The name honours Henry II, Holy Roman Emperor. The municipality is also known as Saint-Henri-de-Lévis.
Le nom honore Henri-Elzéar Juchereau Duc: The name honours Henri-Elzéar Juchereau Duchesnay (1809–1871), seigneur of Sainte-Marie at the time, a lawyer and later a senator. A municipality of Saint-Elzéar was created in 1845 and abolished two years later. The post office opened in 1853, and the parish municipality came into being in 1855.
Le nom honore l’abbé François-Raphaël Pa: The name honours Abbé François-Raphaël Paquet, priest of Saint-Gervais and first priest to serve the mission. The post office opened in 1852. In 1874, the church was enlarged and received a new façade designed by architect Joseph-Ferdinand Peachy.
Le nom honore saint Jean Chrysostome, ma: The name honours Saint John Chrysostom, but mostly recalls Sir John Caldwell (1775-1842), Seigneur of Lauzon, who helped build the church. The parish briefly bore the name Saint-Jérôme, in honour of Abbé Jérôme Demers. Around 1840-1850, logging, notably by the Breakey family, was the main activity. The neoclassical church was built between 1848 and 1850 from plans by Thomas Baillairgé.
Le nom rappelle Jean de Lauson, qui obti: The name recalls Jean de Lauson, who obtained the Lauzon seigneury in 1636 and governed New France in the 1650s. The first settler, Guillaume Couture, settled at Pointe-Lévy on May 15, 1647. In 1690, he commanded the local militia that repelled Admiral William Phips’s troops near the shore, on the present site of the Davie shipyard.
Le nom rappelle la rivière Saint-Charles: The name recalls the Rivière Saint-Charles, which crosses the borough, and two of its tributaries, the Rivière du Berger and the Rivière Lorette.
Le nom rappelle le sanctuaire de Lorette: The name recalls the shrine of Loreto, in Italy. When the Huron-Wendat left the mission in 1697 for Jeune-Lorette, the old village became Vieille-Lorette, then L’Ancienne-Lorette.
Le nom rappelle l’origine irlandaise d’u: The name recalls the Irish origin of a large part of its population, which arrived in the 19th century.
Le nom rappelle que l’arrondissement occ: The name recalls that the borough occupies the upper part of the Saint-Charles River watershed, where Lac Saint-Charles is located.
Le nom rend hommage à Jean-François de B: The name honours Jean-François de Beauchatel, first aide-de-camp to General Montcalm. The municipality was called Saint-Jean-de-Boischatel before becoming Boischatel in 1991.
Le nouveau loyer, en dollars, ou l’augme: The new rent, in dollars, or the increase, in dollars or as a percentage.
Le noyau villageois et ses maisons de bo: The village core and its wooden houses, the parish complex with its 1740 presbytery and 1872 church, the Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes shrine on the riverbank and the marina.
Le noyau villageois prend forme dans la: The village core took shape in the first half of the 19th century, with craftsmen, merchants and notables. The parish was established canonically in 1832 and civilly in 1835, then the municipality was created in 1845. Teaching nuns settled there in 1859, and a new church was built after the fire of 1872.
The RBQ number has the format 1234-5678-90.
Le parc Saint-Sacrement, avec sa piscine: Parc Saint-Sacrement, with its pool, skatepark and curling rink, Parc Holland, Parc des Saints-Martyrs-Canadiens and Parc Notre-Dame-de-Bellevue.
Le parc Victoria, le parc Durocher, le p: Parc Victoria, Parc Durocher, Parc Dollard-des-Ormeaux, Parc Alys-Robi and the linear park along the Saint-Charles and du Berger rivers, among others.
Le parc de la Falaise et de la chute Kab: Parc de la Falaise et de la chute Kabir Kouba, the Marais-du-Nord nature reserve, the Saint-Charles River linear park and the Mont-Bélair nature park, in Val-Bélair.
Le parc de la Montagne-des-Roches, le pa: Parc de la Montagne-des-Roches, Parc des Moulins, Domaine Notre-Dame-des-Bois, Parc Henri-Casault and Parc des Verveines, among others.
The Parc de la Montagne-des-Roches, the Parc du Bourg-Royal, the Parc Saint-Viateur and the Parc des Émeraudes.
Le parc de la falaise et de la chute Kab: Parc de la falaise et de la chute Kabir Kouba, the linear park along the Saint-Charles and du Berger rivers, Parc Johnny-Parent, Parc Gaby-Pleau and Parc Jean-Roger-Durand, as well as the Cheminots bike path.
Le parc des Moulins, créé en 2006 sur un: Parc des Moulins, created in 2006 on part of the former Jardin zoologique du Québec, the Rivière-des-Roches linear park and Parcs Saint-Pierre, Chabot, des Verveines, du Périgord and du Lyonnais.
Le parc du Bois-de-Coulonge, le domaine: Parc du Bois-de-Coulonge, the Cataraqui estate, the villa Bagatelle, the Promenade Samuel-De Champlain and Parc Ross, Parc des Voiliers and Parc de la Falaise.
Le parc du Lac-Baie-d’Or, le Site des Pi: Parc du Lac-Baie-d’Or, the Site des Pins, at the end of Route Monseigneur-Lagueux, Parc Olympique and Parc des Petits-Jardins.
Le peuplement commence en 1647 sur les s: Settlement began in 1647 on the seigneuries of Saint-Ignace, to the east, and Saint-Gabriel, to the west. Hills and waterways dictated the placement of farms, served by roads that would become Rue Racine, Boulevard Bastien, Boulevard de l’Ormière and Avenue du Lac-Saint-Charles.
Le plan d’urbanisme de l’architecte Isaa: Architect Isaac Miron’s urban plan called for five neighbourhoods of about a hundred houses each, every one built around an inn. The first appeared between 1962 and 1964, with the Manoir du Lac Delage, but the formula was abandoned in 1970. Starting in 1990, the west shore was developed with large wooded lots.
Le plan est une recommandation : chaque: The plan is a recommendation: every rent increase, every project and every recourse is submitted to you.
Le pont Pierre-Laporte, par l’autoroute: The Pont Pierre-Laporte, via Autoroute 73, leads directly to Québec City. Routes 116 and 132 are the main routes, and the Société de transport de Lévis serves all three areas.
Le pont de Québec relie Sainte-Foy à la: The Québec Bridge connected Sainte-Foy to the South Shore in 1917. The parish remained rural until the 1940s, then became a town on March 10, 1949. The same year, Boulevard Laurier opened and the Université Laval campus was begun. The Sainte-Foy hospital, opened in 1954, became the Centre hospitalier de l'Université Laval (CHUL) in 1968.
Le pont de l’Île-d’Orléans arrive à Sain: The Île d'Orléans bridge arrives at Saint-Pierre, the neighbouring municipality to the southwest. PLUmobile offers public transit Monday to Friday, with connections to Québec City.
Le pont de l’Île-d’Orléans, à Saint-Pier: The Île d'Orléans bridge, at Saint-Pierre, connects the island to Beauport. PLUmobile public transit serves the island Monday to Friday, with connections to Québec City.
The Île-d’Orléans Bridge, at Saint-Pierre, links the island to Québec City. Chemin Royal goes around the island, and PLUmobile offers public transit Monday to Friday.
Le pont relie Saint-Pierre à Beauport, o: The bridge links Saint-Pierre to Beauport, where Route 368 meets Route 138 and Autoroute 40. A new cable-stayed bridge is to replace it, with service planned around 2028. PLUmobile offers public transit Monday to Friday.
Le premier convoi du Quebec &amp; Richmo: The first train of the Quebec & Richmond Railway, which links the Eastern Townships to Pointe-Lévy, ran there on November 13, 1854. A first station, a modest wooden shack, was probably built in 1855 at a spot called Chaudiere Curve. On July 17, 1879, the Intercolonial acquired the Grand Trunk section between Hadlow and Rivière-du-Loup, and Chaudiere Junction became a repair, supply and transshipment centre. The roundhouse entered service in 1880.
The first resident parish priest arrived in 1713. In 1721, Intendant Michel Bégon ordered a stone church to be built, opened for worship in 1733. The stone presbytery of 1722 is the oldest presbytery remnant on the South Shore of Québec City. The Péan seigneurial mill was built in 1744 at the foot of the Chute-à-Maillou.
Le premier curé résident arrive en 1868,: The first resident priest arrived in 1868, and the post office took the name Saint-Agapit in 1880. In 1885, as the chapel had become too small, the parish received permission to build a church, designed by architect David Ouellet. The village grew where the railway and the road met.
Le premier train de la ligne du Quebec &: The first train on the Quebec & Richmond Railway line, which passes through Charny, ran on November 13, 1854. The place, called Chaudiere Junction, became an important railway hub, and the parish of Charny was founded in 1903. Breakeyville followed in 1909, around the Breakey family’s mill. The Pont de Québec, which starts in Saint-Romuald, was inaugurated in 1919.
Le propriétaire doit en principe donner: The landlord must in principle give 24 hours’ notice to carry out work, except in an emergency[1].
Le propriétaire doit répondre par écrit,: The landlord must respond in writing, within 15 days, stating which of the three responses they choose. For the buildings we manage, every assignment notice is logged as soon as it is received and the response goes out within the deadline. See our property management.
Le propriétaire ne peut ni reprendre ni: The landlord can neither repossess nor evict when the tenant, or their spouse, meets all three of the following conditions[1][2]:
Le propriétaire peut intervenir à tout m: The landlord can step in at any time to finish the work themselves[1].
Le propriétaire peut reprendre le logeme: The landlord can repossess the dwelling to live in it, or to house their first-degree ascendants or descendants, or another relative or relation by marriage of whom they are the main support. They can also repossess it for a former spouse of whom they remain the main support[1].
Le propriétaire peut-il entrer dans mon: Can the landlord enter my unit?
Le propriétaire peut-il reprendre mon lo: Can the landlord repossess my unit?
Le propriétaire qui consent ne peut exig: A landlord who consents can only require reimbursement of the reasonable expenses related to the assignment, such as the cost of a credit check[1][2].
Le propriétaire, sans délai; à défaut, l: The landlord, without delay; failing that, the tenant does the essentials
Le propriétaire; une serrure ne se chang: The landlord; a lock cannot be changed without the agreement of both parties
Le préscolaire et le premier cycle du pr: Preschool and the first cycle of elementary are taught at the école de la Caravelle de Saint-Flavien, the 2nd cycle in Joly and the 3rd cycle in Dosquet. For secondary school, the nearest schools are École Beaurivage, in Saint-Agapit, and École secondaire Pamphile-Le May, in Sainte-Croix.
Le président est responsable de la prote: The president is responsible for the protection of personal information at LeaseLane. For any question: confidentialite@leaselane.ca. They approve our policies and ensure they are applied.
The president is responsible for personal information protection at LeaseLane. For any question, or to exercise your rights, write to confidentialite@leaselane.ca.
Le quartier actuel, Neufchâtel-Est–Lebou: The current neighbourhood, Neufchâtel-Est–Lebourgneuf, was formed in 2003. It is part of the Les Rivières borough and lies near the geographic centre of Québec City.
Le quartier compte de nombreux parcs, do: The neighbourhood has many parks, including Parc Victoria, Parc Durocher, Parc Dollard-des-Ormeaux and the linear park along the Saint-Charles and du Berger rivers, as well as the Patro Laval and the Hôtel-Dieu du Sacré-Cœur. Several former churches have made way for housing and housing cooperatives.
Le quartier compte un secteur des années: The neighbourhood has a 1950s and 1960s sector around Boulevard Pie-XII and a more recent one: compare the two before choosing.
Le quartier couvre la partie de l’arrond: The neighbourhood covers the part of the Les Rivières borough north of Autoroute Félix-Leclerc and east of the Rivière Saint-Charles; the Rivière du Berger also crosses it. Lebourgneuf occupies its east side, with recent residential areas and large commercial and business zones along the Laurentienne and Félix-Leclerc highways.
Le quartier couvre l’ancien faubourg Sai: The neighbourhood covers the former faubourg Saint-Jean, which arose under the French Regime along Chemin Saint-Jean, outside the Saint-Jean Gate. It also takes in the former faubourg Saint-Louis, south of Rue Saint-Patrick.
Le quartier de l’Aéroport est celui qui: The Aéroport neighbourhood has the most farms in Québec City, especially northwest of the airport. Its residential areas, Champigny, Jouvence and Chauveau, are in the south, between Autoroute Félix-Leclerc and Boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel, and around Boulevard Chauveau-Ouest. A big-box retail area extends to the southeast, on both sides of Autoroute Duplessis.
Le quartier des Chutes-Montmorency regro: The Chutes-Montmorency neighbourhood brings together the former sectors of Courville and Montmorency and most of Villeneuve. It extends from Rue Francheville in the west to the river and the Montmorency Falls in the east, and from the St. Lawrence in the south to Rue de la Sérénité in the north. Avenue Royale, Boulevard Sainte-Anne and Autoroute Dufferin-Montmorency run through it toward the Île d’Orléans bridge.
Le quartier des Châtels a la forme d’un: The Des Châtels neighbourhood is L-shaped: it includes the part of the borough west of Boulevard de l’Ormière, plus the part east of that boulevard and south of Rue Durand. The Saint-Charles River marks its southeastern boundary. Autoroute Henri-IV, Avenue Chauveau, Boulevard Bastien and Boulevard Saint-Claude run through it, and its western part still has farmland and woodland.
Le quartier des Jésuites occupe la parti: The Jésuites neighbourhood occupies the part of the borough between Boulevard Henri-Bourassa and Boulevard du Loiret, south of Boulevard Jean-Talon. Boulevard Louis-XIV and Autoroute Félix-Leclerc run through it. Almost entirely residential, it has a few institutional and commercial areas, including Carrefour Charlesbourg, on Boulevard Henri-Bourassa.
Le quartier dépasse 23 000 habitants en: The neighbourhood exceeded 23,000 residents in 1921. In the 1950s and 1960s, the modernization of Parliament Hill transformed the former Saint-Louis suburb completely, and thousands of residents left for the suburbs. The 1970s and 1980s saw dozens of housing and food co-operatives emerge, including the Faux-Bourg co-op, founded in 1976. Shared streets, such as Rue Sainte-Claire, now calm traffic there.
Le quartier est délimité par une zone bo: The neighbourhood is bounded by a wooded area with Saint-Émile and Loretteville to the south, a line parallel to Boulevard Valcartier to the west, Chemin de la Grande-Ligne to the east and Saint-Gabriel-de-Valcartier to the north. It is crossed north to south by Avenue du Lac-Saint-Charles and Boulevard de la Colline, and east to west by Rue Lepire and Rue Jacques-Bédard. The built-up area is concentrated in the south; the west has large wooded areas and sizeable sand pits.
Le quartier est surtout résidentiel et b: The neighbourhood is mostly residential and wooded. Check your routes to work or school before signing a lease.
Le quartier est surtout résidentiel. Vér: The neighbourhood is mainly residential. Check the Réseau de transport de la Capitale bus routes before choosing your unit.
Le quartier est très étendu : vérifiez d: The neighbourhood is very large: check which area the unit is in (Champigny, Jouvence or Chauveau) and its access to Autoroutes Félix-Leclerc and Duplessis.
Le quartier historique, entouré de forti: The historic district, surrounded by fortifications. It has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1985.
Le quartier occupe l’extrémité ouest de: The neighbourhood occupies the western end of the Québec City hill, which forms a point toward Cap-Rouge.
Le quartier partage son nom avec l’avenu: The neighbourhood shares its name with Avenue du Vieux-Moulin, which recalls a flour mill built by the Jesuits around 1695 on the banks of the ruisseau du Moulin. The mill was destroyed by fire in 1948.
Le quartier prend le nom de Lebourgneuf: The neighbourhood takes the name Lebourgneuf
Le quartier prend son essor au milieu du: The neighbourhood took off in the mid-18th century with the shipyards on the Saint-Charles River. In 1857, a market hall opened on Place Jacques-Cartier. In 1864, Guillaume Bresse’s mechanical shoemaking business launched dozens of shoe factories. Despite the fires of 1845, 1866 and 1870, Saint-Roch enjoyed unprecedented prosperity from 1880.
Le quartier s’étend du boulevard Louis-X: The neighbourhood extends from Boulevard Louis-XIV, in the south, to Lac-Beauport, in the north, and to the Montmorency River, in the east. Avenue Sainte-Thérèse crosses it from east to west, and Boulevard Raymond and Boulevard Lloyd-Welch from north to south. The terrain rises from 110 m in the south to 572 m at the montagne des Trois Sommets; the Beauport River rises here.
Le quartier s’étend du fleuve jusqu’à l’: The neighbourhood stretches from the river to Autoroute Félix-Leclerc: check the route to your work or school depending on the sector.
Le quartier tire son nom de la rivière L: The neighbourhood takes its name from the Rivière Lairet, a tributary of the Rivière Saint-Charles that rose near Charlesbourg and wound through Limoilou. On September 14, 1535, Jacques Cartier spotted this river, at whose confluence he wintered with his crew, near the Iroquoian village of Stadacona. At the start of the 19th century, all the land north of the Rivière Saint-Charles was still agricultural.
Le quartier tire son nom des Jésuites, à: The neighbourhood takes its name from the Jesuits, to whom Henri de Lévis granted the seigneury of Notre-Dame-des-Anges on March 10, 1626. The estate, enlarged in 1637 and 1652, extends north from the Saint-Charles River. The Jesuits did not begin developing it until 1652. The seigneury kept its integrity and agricultural character until 1855.
Le quartier tire son nom du chemin Saint: The neighbourhood takes its name from Chemin Saint-Louis and the Saint-Louis-de-France parish. The road, laid out in the 17th and 18th centuries under the name Chemin de Cap-Rouge, took its current name in 1929. Around 1920, a settlement called Neilsonville bordered Chemin Saint-Louis, near the Québec Bridge, completed in 1917. Until the 1950s, this road was the only route linking the bridge to the capital.
Le rapport du 15 montre où en est chaque: The report on the 15th shows where each action stands and what it changed.
Le recours au TAL</strong> pour des domm: Recourse to the TAL for actual damages, with supporting evidence.
Le recours vise le montant versé. Il ne: The remedy covers the amount paid. It does not end the lease and does not justify withholding rent.
Le retard de plus de trois semaines: The delay of more than three weeks
The patron saint is Augustine of Hippo. He is said to have been chosen to honour Augustin de Saffray de Mézy, governor of New France from 1663 to 1665, or perhaps Paul Augustin Juchereau.
Le secteur est desservi par la Société d: The area is served by the Société de transport de Lévis and by the Via Rail station on the line between Montréal and the Maritimes.
Le secteur est peuplé dès le début du XI: The area was settled from the early 19th century. Before the parish was established, part of the territory bore the name Taniata, which reportedly means “where poplars grow” in Abenaki. In 1828, the parish of Saint-Jean-Chrysostome was created. It was the fourth to break away from Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-de-Lévy, the mother parish of the seigneury of Lauzon.
Le secteur fait d’abord partie de la par: The area was first part of the parish of Saint-Flavien. In 1895, according to local history, farmer Thomas Caron convinced the superintendent of the Drummond County Railway to route the line farther north, across the lands of an area that would be called La Station. This detour became known as the “Croche à Caron.”
Le secteur fait partie de la municipalit: The area was part of the municipality of Sainte-Foy, incorporated in 1845 and reinstated in 1855. On March 10, 1949, it became a city, and on May 4, 1950, it made the name Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois official. After the Second World War, the baby boom and the growth of the road network turned its fields into suburbs: in 1971, Sainte-Foy had 21 times as many residents as in 1941.
Le secteur fait partie de l’ancienne sei: The area is part of the former seigneury of Lauzon. It was first called Village Saint-Denis, after a concession on the left bank of the Beaurivage that appears on a plan of the seigneury in 1828. The Chaudière station, on the railway now operated by Canadian National, gave its name to the post office opened in 1873, Chaudière-Station.
Le secteur se détache de Saint-Flavien e: The area separated from Saint-Flavien and became the municipality of Laurier-Station on January 1, 1951, and the new chapel held its first mass on January 28 that year. In the early 1960s, the Trans-Canada Highway, now Autoroute Jean-Lesage, drew new businesses, industries and government services. The small village became a regional crossroads.
Le secteur, d’abord appelé le Sault, est: The area, first called Le Sault, was settled around 1664 on the fief of Charleville. The territory remained agricultural, but it would never have more than about twenty farms.
Le seigneur Gabriel-Elzéar Taschereau au: The seigneur Gabriel-Elzéar Taschereau is said to have chosen this name in memory of Claire-Françoise Bissot, wife of Louis Jolliet, the first seigneur of the area. The parish also honours Saint Clare of Assisi.
Le seigneur souhaitait le nom de Saint-L: The seigneur wanted the name Saint-Laurent, but a parish on Île d’Orléans already bore it, so Saint Michael was chosen. The first church and the first presbytery were built on the current site between 1712 and 1715, then a new presbytery was built in 1740. In 1754, a village was established there to attract craftsmen.
Le sentier La Tourbière, long de 4,2 km: The La Tourbière trail, 4.2 km round trip, leads to a lookout over a 150-hectare peat bog. The Musée Isidore-Boisvert displays about 150 miniature farm implements and antique cars, and the old steam sawmill is on Rue Principale.
Le service et les rapports sont les même: The service and the reports are the same, whatever the number of doors.
Le site de l’église est fixé en 1844. Le: The church site was set in 1844. The first parish priest, Abbé André-Amable Marcoux, arrived on October 1, 1844, and the first baptisms took place on October 20. The parish was established canonically in 1849, then civilly in 1854.
Le site du patrimoine de Saint-Nicolas,: The Saint-Nicolas heritage site, on Route Marie-Victorin, groups together 18th- and 19th-century houses, including the Maison Pâquet, built around 1760, and the Chapelle Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, from 1867. It was designated a heritage site in 1987.
Le site est exploité par Solutions locat: The site is operated by Solutions locatives LeaseLane inc., which carries on business under the name LeaseLane (“LeaseLane” or “we”), a business registered in Québec under NEQ 1182479981. LeaseLane offers property management and residential rental services in the Québec City region.
Le site ne s’adresse pas aux personnes d: The site is not intended for people under 14. We do not knowingly collect their information without the consent of the person with parental authority.
Le site patrimonial de Beauport, qui lon: The Beauport heritage site, which runs along Avenue Royale, was declared in 1964 and expanded in 1985. On January 1, 1976, six neighbouring municipalities were merged with Beauport, which was in turn merged with Québec City in 2002; Vieux-Bourg then became one of the borough's five neighbourhoods. On June 22, 2022, its residents voted in favour of creating a neighbourhood council.
Le site patrimonial de Saint-Michel-de-B: The Saint-Michel-de-Bellechasse heritage site includes about fifty buildings from the 18th and 19th centuries. At its centre, the parish complex, classified in 2022, brings together the 1872 church, the cemetery, a tithe barn and the 1740 presbytery, the third oldest still standing in Québec. The Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes shrine, from 1879, stands on a promontory on the riverbank.
Le site peut contenir des liens vers des: The site may contain links to third-party sites or embed their services, such as a map or a payment tool. We do not control these sites; their own terms and policies apply.
Le sol riche et les terres en pente vers: The rich soil and the land sloping toward the river, whose stones hold the sun’s heat, allow planting earlier than elsewhere in the region. Growers cultivate more than 20 varieties of sweet corn, sold at roadside stands on Route 138, among other places.
Le stationnement dans les rues est inter: On-street parking is prohibited from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m., from November 15 to April 1. The Corporation de transport régional de Portneuf provides two park-and-ride lots for carpoolers in Cap-Santé.
Le stationnement est rare et les travaux: Parking is scarce and work on buildings is governed by heritage rules.
Le stationnement se fait souvent dans la: Parking is often on the street. Check whether the street is covered by the City’s resident parking permit.
Le surnom vient du grand nombre de conce: The nickname comes from the large number of car dealerships in the town.
Le terminus de la Cimenterie, dans le qu: The Cimenterie terminal, in the neighbourhood, is served by several Réseau de transport de la Capitale bus routes.
Le territoire change de nom plusieurs fo: The territory changed names several times. In 1814, it was called Concession Saint-Augustin, after its first grantee, Augustin Couture. In 1898, it was instead referred to as Chaudière Mills, in reference to the river and the Breakey mill. In the early 20th century, it became Saint-Omer, in honour of Abbé Omer Poirier, parish priest of Charny from 1903 to 1936.
Le territoire couvre 102,66 km², surtout: The territory covers 102.66 km², mostly farmland, where pigs and dairy cows are among the animals raised. An arena built in 1978, which also houses halls and the municipal offices, is the centre of recreation. The Monk bike path, completed in 2022, follows the former Monk subdivision railway right-of-way for 4 km.
Le territoire couvre 151,73 km², occupé: The territory covers 151.73 km², used mostly for agriculture and forest. Lacs Baxter, O’Neil and Desbarats and the Henderson, Pyke and Desbarats rivers water it. The Zoo Miller shows about a hundred animals along walking trails.
Le territoire couvre 693,6 km² et plusie: The territory covers 693.6 km² and several areas are far from the centre. A car is almost essential, especially in winter.
Le territoire couvre 85,12 km². Les deux: The territory covers 85.12 km². Two-thirds of the population live in the village, and one-third live in a farming setting. Hog farming and the dairy industry are among the foundations of the economy, along with an industrial park and about a hundred businesses.
Le territoire couvre environ 83 km², don: The territory covers about 83 km², 99% of it in an agricultural zone. Hog, dairy and poultry production dominate, along with maple production, and about twenty businesses have set up there.
Le territoire couvre une partie des anci: The territory covers part of the former Jacques-Cartier, d’Auteuil and Neuville seigneuries. Pioneers from the parishes along the river, mostly from Cap-Santé, began clearing it in the mid-19th century.
Le territoire de Beaupré est longtemps p: The territory of Beaupré was long shared between two of the oldest parishes in Québec, Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré and Saint-Joachim. In the early 20th century, timber cut in the backcountry came down to a sawmill on Île Labranche, in Beaupré. In 1927, Saint-Joachim ceded part of its territory to form the new parish.
Le territoire de Duberger, appelé à l’or: The territory of Duberger, originally called La Petite-Rivière, was part of the municipality of Saint-Roch-de-Québec in 1855, then, in 1893, of the new municipality of Saint-Malo. It was then an agricultural area, with houses lined up along the rangs of Petite-Rivière Sud and Nord, today’s Boulevards Wilfrid-Hamel and Père-Lelièvre. Les Saules, for its part, came under L’Ancienne-Lorette; its name comes from the many willows that line the Saint-Charles and Lorette rivers.
Le territoire de Honfleur appartenait d’: The territory of Honfleur first belonged to the parishes of Saint-Anselme, Saint-Gervais, Saint-Lazare and Sainte-Claire. The idea of founding a separate parish there dates back to the late 1850s. It divided the residents of Bellechasse for a long time.
Le territoire de Saint-Michel fait parti: The Saint-Michel territory is part of the seigneury of Beauport, granted on January 15, 1634 to Robert Giffard, a surgeon and apothecary from Mortagne-au-Perche. During the first decades, settlement was concentrated near the river, around the bourg du Fargy. In the 1670s, the second seigneur, Joseph Giffard, granted inland lands along new rangs, including the Saint-Michel and Saint-Joseph rangs.
Le territoire de Saint-Émile fait partie: The territory of Saint-Émile is part of a grant made to Robert Giffard in 1647. That same year, he gave these lands to the Augustinian nuns of the Hôtel-Dieu de Québec, as the dowry of his daughter Françoise, who entered as a novice. The nuns named their domain the Saint-Ignace seigneury, but at first settled no one there, for fear of the Iroquois.
Le territoire de Shannon faisait autrefo: The territory of Shannon was once part of Sainte-Catherine, where Irish immigrants settled starting in 1820 at the invitation of the seigneur Michel-Louis Juchereau Duchesnay. The town's name recalls this Irish origin. For a long time, cutting timber for the Québec City shipyards supported the population.
Le territoire de Vanier fait partie du c: Vanier's territory has been part of Québec County since 1855. Its southern part, near the Saint-Charles River and called "Petite rivière sans bruit," first attracted summer vacationers. From 1912 to 1914, speculation companies bought almost all the land in the eastern part of Petite-Rivière, a municipality that had remained agricultural. They obtained the creation of the city of Québec-Ouest, incorporated on March 9, 1916.
Le territoire est détaché de la seigneur: The territory was detached from the Sainte-Marie seigneury, long owned by the Taschereau de Linière family. The parish of Saint-Elzéar-de-Linière was established canonically in 1835. The first settlers arrived mostly around 1845, from Île d’Orléans, Beauport, Château-Richer and Sainte-Marie, and Irish families joined them.
Le territoire est vallonné et boisé, et: The territory is hilly and wooded, and distances between areas are long. A car makes it easier to get to Charlesbourg and the rest of Québec City.
Le territoire fait d’abord partie de la: The territory was first part of the Notre-Dame-des-Anges seigneury, one of the first land grants in New France. As early as 1652, settlers farmed the land there, and its tidal flats attracted fishermen and duck hunters, hence the name “Canardière.” In 1690, Admiral Phips landed there in an attempt to take Québec City; Pierre Maufils, a student of the Séminaire, was killed in the fighting. In 1705, the Séminaire de Québec acquired the lands of La Canardière.

The territory was first part of the seigneury of La Durantaye, granted to Olivier Morel de La Durantaye in 1672. The first settlers, militiamen from Île d'Orléans, settled there around 1700. A cross, a little west of the village, commemorates Prisque Bélanger, considered the first settler.

The territory was first part of the seigneury of Lauzon, granted in 1636. The route Justinienne, which links the seigneuries of Lauzon and Joliet, opened this corner of forest to settlement. In 1789, Nicolas Hamann and his family settled alongside this road and cleared the first farm.

The territory was first part of the Lauzon seigneury. Before the parish was established, Saint-Jean-Chrysostome was called Taniata, an Abenaki word said to mean “where poplars grow.” The parish was established in 1828, the fourth separated from Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-de-Lévy.

The territory was first part of the seigneury of Sillery, granted in 1651 to the Huron-Wendat under Jesuit guardianship. Settlement began in the 1660s and, in 1667, a bark chapel was built at the corner of today’s Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois and Autoroute Robert-Bourassa. Côte Saint-Michel was cleared along Chemin Sainte-Foy, around the Notre-Dame-de-Foy mission, the cradle of the village of Sainte-Foy. In 1673, the Huron-Wendat left the region for Lorette.
Le territoire fait partie de la seigneur: The territory was part of the Jolliet seigneury. Its seigneurial rights passed to the Taschereau and Fortier families, who would later give their name to the municipality of Taschereau-Fortier. Religiously, the area first came under the parish of Sainte-Claire, created in 1824.

The territory is part of the Saint-Gilles, or Beaurivage, seigneury, granted in 1738 to Gilles Rageot de Beaurivage. Alexander Fraser bought it in 1782 and, as early as 1783, had grant deeds prepared for fifteen settlers of German origin. They were the first Beaurivageois.

The territory was part of the seigneury granted to the explorer Louis Jolliet on April 30, 1697. Left undeveloped for a century, it passed to Gabriel-Elzéar Taschereau, Jolliet's great-grandson, who became its sole owner at the end of the 18th century. The first settlers arrived in the mid-1780s.

The territory was part of the Beaurivage seigneury, granted on April 1, 1738 to Gilles Rageot, a Québec City merchant. The opening of the Craig Road by the army in 1810, then of the Sainte-Marie road, passable by carriage by the summer of 1817, made the region accessible. In 1819, the surveyor Demers divided the land along the Craig Road into lots, and about fifty lots were granted as early as 1820.

The territory is part of the seigneury of Lauzon, granted in 1636 to Simon Le Maître, a front man for Jean de Lauson. The first settlers moved in near the Beaurivage and the Chaudière in the early 18th century, in the time of the seigneur Étienne Charest. Around 1780–1790, families settled the Grandes-Pointes concession, also called Longues-Pointes, and its residents asked for a chapel in 1798.

The territory is part of the seigneury of Notre-Dame-des-Anges, granted to the Jesuits in 1626, which extends north from the Saint-Charles River. Like the rest of Charlesbourg, it remained agricultural for a long time. In the first half of the 20th century, Charlesbourg also became a vacation area for Québec City residents, before urbanizing in the second half of the century.

The territory was part of the seigneury of Notre-Dame-des-Anges, granted to the Jesuits in 1626. In 1665, the village of Charlesbourg was founded on a radial plan: a square of 25 arpents, at the centre of which a square of five arpents, the trait-carré, was reserved for the church, the presbytery and the cemetery. The settlers' houses surround it, and their trapezoidal lots extend outward in a star. The first thirty lots were granted from February 22 to 28, 1665.

The territory was part of the seigneury of Notre-Dame-des-Anges, granted to the Jesuits in 1626. In 1665, Intendant Jean Talon founded a village there with a unique plan: a central square, the Trait-Carré, reserved for the church, the rectory and the cemetery, surrounded by the settlers’ houses and by lands radiating like a star.
The territory is part of the seigneury of Saint-Gabriel, occupied from 1647. It was first a private domain of Robert Giffard, then of the Jesuits, before passing to the Crown in 1800.

The territory is part of the seigneury of Rivière-du-Sud, granted to Charles Huault de Montmagny in 1646. A man named Lecolombier briefly settled there in 1696, but colonization began mainly in the early 18th century. In 1709, Pierre Blanchet donated a piece of land, and a chapel was built in 1713 north of the Rivière du Sud.

The territory is part of the seigneury of Île d’Orléans, granted on January 15, 1636, and was settled around 1660. A first wooden chapel was built there in 1675. The parish was founded in 1679 under the name Saint-Paul. In the 17th century, the place was also known as L’Arbre-Sec.

The territory was part of the seigneury of Île d'Orléans, granted on January 15, 1636. On April 2, 1656, Guillaume Baucher, known as Montmorency, received a three-arpent plot there. His descendants would take the name Morency.

The territory is part of the seigneury of Île d’Orléans, granted on January 15, 1636. The first residents settled there around 1660, and a wooden chapel was built there in 1673. The parish of Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul was founded in 1679. It then included the current territory of Sainte-Pétronille.

The territory is part of the seigneury of Île d’Orléans, granted on January 15, 1636. A wooden chapel was built there in 1675. From 1680, Saint-Jean was a mission served by the priest of Sainte-Famille, then became a parish in 1714.

The territory was part of the seigneury of Île d'Orléans, granted to Jacques Castillon on January 15, 1636. In 1651, the Jesuit Chaumonot settled refugee Wendat (Huron) there, probably near the current wharf. The following year, Éléonore de Grandmaison married Jacques Gourdeau de Beaulieu there, who gave his name to the fief.
Le territoire fait partie de la vaste se: The territory is part of the vast seigneury of Lauzon and has been inhabited since 1660. The parish was founded in 1668; in 1683, it had about fifty families. In 1690, a first mill was built at the anse aux Hirondelles and a chapel was erected. The name Saint-Nicolas was assigned in 1694, at the canonical erection, at the request of Claude de Bermen de La Martinière, administrator of the seigneury.
Le territoire fait partie des seigneurie: The territory was part of the seigneuries of Sainte-Marie and Jolliet, owned by the Taschereau family. The first settlers, from Sainte-Marie, Saint-Henri, Saint-Gervais and Sainte-Claire, settled along the route Sainte-Thérèse, which the Taschereau family had laid out to populate the hinterland.
Le territoire occupe une partie de la se: The territory occupies part of the seigneury of Lauzon known in the 18th and 19th centuries as the Hêtrière concession. Its dense forest and middling land made it poorly suited to settlement, and the first lots were granted between 1790 and 1830. The seigneur John Caldwell is said to have granted land to encourage logging near the Chaudière River.
The territory remained agricultural for a long time. The parish of Saint-Ambroise-de-la-Jeune-Lorette, founded in 1795, launched the settlement of the future Neufchâtel. Farther south, La Petite-Rivière was part of Saint-Roch-de-Québec when it was created in 1855, then became a municipality in 1902.
Le territoire se rattache d’abord à Lore: The territory is first attached to Lorette, where the Jesuit Pierre Chaumonot built a chapel in 1674 for the Huron-Wendat who had come to take refuge near Québec City. After they left for Jeune-Lorette in 1697, the place took the name Ancienne-Lorette and was settled by French colonists. The Champigny area was known as Gaudarville, and the Chauveau area as Les Grands-Déserts.
Le territoire s’appelle Concession Saint: The territory is called Concession Saint-Augustin
Le transport en commun est assuré par le: Public transit is provided by the Réseau de transport de la Capitale. The territory is large: check the route to your workplace before viewing a unit.
Le transport en commun relève du Réseau: Public transit is run by the Réseau de transport de la Capitale, as in the rest of the agglomeration. The town is small, about 7.6 km², and the airport is very close.
Le village a une école primaire, un CPE,: The village has an elementary school, a CPE (early childhood centre), a grocery store and a library. The secondary school, the hospital and the CLSC are a few minutes away by car, and Québec City about thirty minutes.
Le village compte un centre de la petite: The village has an early childhood centre, the École primaire de l’Étincelle, the École secondaire de Saint-Charles, an arena and the Jacques-Labrie library. The economy rests on dairy, hog and horticultural farms, maple syrup production and a few vineyards, including Le Ricaneux and Domaine Bel-Chas. The town hall occupies the former rectory, built in the 1740s.
Le village de Fossambault-sur-le-Lac est: The village of Fossambault-sur-le-Lac was incorporated on March 10, 1949, with Jules Gingras as its first mayor. The Notre-Dame-de-Liesse chapel was erected in 1950, and the municipality gained town status in 1974.
Le village est à 7 km de Sainte-Marie et: The village is 7 km from Sainte-Marie and 56 km from Québec City. Route 216 runs through the municipality.
Le village est à environ 15 km de Lévis: The village is about 15 km from Lévis and 30 km from Québec City. Routes 173, 218, 275 and 277 connect it to the Beauce, Bellechasse and Lévis.
Le village est à environ 20 km de Lévis,: The village is about 20 km from Lévis, by Highway 20 (exits 337 and 341). It has an early childhood centre, an elementary school and a secondary school.
Le village est à environ 26 km à vol d’o: The village is about 26 km as the crow flies northeast of Québec City. The island is reached by the Île-d’Orléans Bridge, at Saint-Pierre, and PLUmobile offers public transit Monday to Friday.
Le village est à environ 35 minutes des: The village is about 35 minutes from the Québec City bridges. Route 132 (Boulevard Blais) crosses it, and the Route verte passes through the centre of the village.
Le village est à quelque 40 km en aval d: The village is some 40 km downriver from Québec City. It is reached by the Île d’Orléans bridge, at Saint-Pierre, then by Chemin Royal, along either side of the island. PLUmobile offers public transport Monday to Friday.
Le village est à une dizaine de minutes: The village is about ten minutes from Montmagny and about 30 minutes from Lévis. Route 228 runs through it and connects to Highway 20 and Montmagny.
Le village prend le nom de Jean Lyon de: The village took the name of Jean Lyon de Saint-Ferréol, superior of the Séminaire from 1726 to 1734. A first chapel was blessed in 1767, and a stone church replaced it in 1842. The high-altitude climate made harvests difficult, but the population grew quickly between 1831 and 1851.
Le village se détache de la paroisse: The village separates from the parish
Le village se développe autour de la pet: The village developed around the small Saint-Michel-Station railway station, with the arrival of the railway in northern Bellechasse. Although it bears the name of a former seigneury, La Durantaye is one of the youngest municipalities in the region.
Le village se trouve entre Saint-Raphaël: The village lies between Saint-Raphaël to the north and Saint-Damien-de-Buckland to the southeast. The MRC de Bellechasse offers on-demand public transit to Lévis, Montmagny and Sainte-Marie.
Le village vit beaucoup du fleuve. Vers: The village lived largely off the river. Around 1830, it had about twenty boatbuilders, and the Godbout boatworks was built in 1837. The first school opened in 1842, and the Sisters of the Good Shepherd settled in the village in 1875. The current church was built in 1860 to plans by architect Raphaël Giroux.
Le véritable peuplement commence vers 18: Real settlement began around 1801, with families from Île d’Orléans, the Côte-de-Beaupré and the seigneuries of Lauzon and Bellechasse. In 1829, Bishop Bernard-Claude Panet canonically established the parish of Saint-Isidore-de-Lauzon. The name honours Saint Isidore of Seville, a Spanish bishop who died in 636.

They called Saint-Nicolas Nessawakamighe, “second place,” because the mission established there was the second along the river. From 1683 to 1700, the Jesuits ran the Saint-François-de-Sales mission at the mouth of the Chaudière.

Digs at the Marais du Nord have revealed traces of Indigenous presence dating back to the year 500.
Les Iroquoiens du Saint-Laurent fréquent: The St. Lawrence Iroquoians frequented Cap Tourmente, which they called Ajoasté. In 1626, Champlain had a farm built at the foot of the cape to feed the Québec colony. It was destroyed by the Kirke brothers in 1628.

On February 18, 1867, the Archbishop of Québec established the parish of Saint-Agapit-de-Beaurivage, and the municipality was founded on May 8 of that year.

Les premiers colons arrivent vers 1780,: The first settlers arrived around 1780, mostly from Saint-Henri and Saint-Gervais. As early as 1825, they asked for their own parish, since their church was far away. Bishop Panet established it in 1827 under the patronage of Saint Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury, and it received civil status in 1835.
Les premiers colons arrivent vers 1820,: The first settlers arrived around 1820, mostly from Beaumont. Joseph Lacasse, known as José, was the first to settle there. He cut the cedar on his land to make shingles, which he went to sell in Québec City on foot. A few Irish families also settled there before 1840.
Les premiers colons arrivent vers 1853,: The first settlers arrived around 1853, the year the area was served as a mission. A post office opened in 1866, and the municipality was created in 1872 from part of the territory of Saint-Joachim.
Les premiers efforts de colonisation dan: The first settlement efforts in the area are said to date from 1769. Les premiers habitants du territoire son: The first inhabitants of the territory were Irish who arrived around 1830. A mission was founded in 1837 and a chapel was built in 1842. A church replaced it in 1853.
Les premiers pionniers descendaient d’Ac: The first pioneers were descended from Acadians, and part of the territory long bore the name Petite-Acadie. The village is also home to the Centre de formation en entreprise et récupération de Bellechasse (CFER), which welcomes young people aged 16 to 18.

Lévis s’étend sur la rive sud du fleuve: Lévis stretches along the south shore of the St. Lawrence River, across from Québec City, between Beaumont and Saint-Antoine-de-Tilly. It is the administrative seat of Chaudière-Appalaches and the seventh most populous city in Québec. It has three boroughs and ten areas, including Saint-Romuald, Charny, Saint-Nicolas and Lauzon. L’Ancienne-Lorette est une ville de la C: L’Ancienne-Lorette is a town in the Capitale-Nationale region that is part of the Québec City agglomeration. Its 7.63 km² territory is completely enclaved within Québec City. The Lorette River, a tributary of the Saint-Charles River, runs through it from northwest to southeast.
L’Ange-Gardien fait partie de la MRC de: L’Ange-Gardien is part of the La Côte-de-Beaupré RCM, in the Capitale-Nationale region. The municipality faces the Île d’Orléans channel and extends north into a forested area, where the Ferrée and Retenue rivers flow. Its terraced hillsides long served agriculture, and its many waterways served the industry of earlier times, tied to wheat and timber.
L’Aquarium du Québec accueille ses premi: The Aquarium du Québec welcomed its first visitors in 1959. The Pierre-Laporte Bridge opened to traffic on November 7, 1970, less than 200 m west of the Québec Bridge. The Sainte-Foy city hall, today the Andrée-P.-Boucher building, was inaugurated in 1996. In 2013, the former Saint-Denys-du-Plateau church, the work of Jean-Marie Roy, became the Monique-Corriveau library; the Saint-Louis-de-France church was demolished in 2021.
L’Expo agricole, le rodéo et le Festival: The Expo agricole, the rodeo and the Festival Country Lotbinière, held since 2015, take place on the Société d’agriculture grounds. The municipality also hosts the Festival du Flocon in late February and the Festi Week-end in late June.
L’Exposition provinciale prend le nom d’: The Exposition provinciale was renamed Expo Québec in 1968. In 1988, Limoilou was divided into three neighbourhoods, and Lairet was named after the river. The site became ExpoCité in 1997, the year the Centre de foires opened; the Centre Vidéotron opened there in 2015, the year the Colisée closed its doors, and the Grand Marché de Québec moved in 2019 into the former Pavillon du commerce.
L’abbé Antonio Houde, curé de 1946 à 197: Abbé Antonio Houde, priest from 1946 to 1971, first had a crypt built, completed for Easter 1947; it served as the church for 16 years. The current church was built in 1962-1963 from plans by architect René Blanchet, in a modern Gothic style, with granite stone façades. It was blessed on December 22, 1963.

Pendant deux siècles, le secteur est par: For two centuries, the area was split between the parishes of Saint-Pierre, to the north, and Saint-Laurent, to the south. The land here is less fertile than elsewhere on the island, and was little farmed. In 1759, General Wolfe set up one of his headquarters here to conduct the siege of Québec City. Around 1820, a shipyard built two large ships there, the Colombus and the Baron Renfrew.
Pendant le siège de Québec, en 1759, les: During the siege of Québec in 1759, English troops occupied Saint-Michel. The residents’ resistance continued until 1775 and fed several oral legends. Until 1842, the territory bore the name Saint-Michel-de-la-Durantaye.
Pendant près d’un siècle, la forêt fait: For nearly a century, the forest supported the population. A railway connected Stoneham to Loretteville in 1912, and up to 20 sawmills operated in the territory. Route 175, completed in 1951, opened the region to motorists and vacationers. The golf club came into being in 1959 and the Station touristique Stoneham in 1963.

Place Sainte-Foy ouvre en 1958, puis Pla: Place Sainte-Foy opened in 1958, then Place Laurier in 1961. Riches en marne, les terres produisent s: Rich in marl, the land produced mainly wheat and buckwheat until the 1860s, then oats, potatoes and milk, sold at the Québec City and Lévis markets. In 1879, two stations served the territory, La Chaudière and Craig’s Road. The present church was built in 1904, and a bridge linked the two banks of the Beaurivage in 1917.
