Saint Damien est un médecin martyr, fêté: Saint Damian is a martyred physician, celebrated with his brother Saint Cosmas. Buckland is the name of the township created in 1806, which recalls a locality in England.
Saint Tite était un disciple de saint Pa: Saint Titus was a disciple of Saint Paul. The Caps refers to the bare rock faces of the Caps region, between Cap Tourmente and Baie-Saint-Paul.
Saint-Agapit : Vue aérienne église Saint: Saint-Agapit: Aerial view of Saint-Agapit church
Saint-Agapit est la deuxième municipalit: Saint-Agapit is the second most populous municipality in the Lotbinière MRC. Its territory of about 64 km² lies south of Saint-Apollinaire and the Bernières sector of Lévis. The Noire River crosses it from west to east, and the Route verte runs alongside Route 116 on the site of the former railway.
Saint-Anselme est une municipalité de la: Saint-Anselme is a municipality in the Bellechasse MRC, about 25 km from Lévis and 11 km west of Sainte-Claire. The Etchemin River runs through it and forms the Rouillard Falls, lined with potholes. The village is also known for its rectory with eighteen dormers, built to the plans of architect Thomas Baillairgé.
Saint-Antoine-de-Tilly s’étend sur envir: Saint-Antoine-de-Tilly covers about 60 km² along the south shore of the St. Lawrence. It is the first municipality in Lotbinière when you arrive from Lévis, and Routes 132 and 273 run through it. The village has more than 50 houses and buildings of heritage architecture, including three seigneurial manors, a former general store and two procession chapels.
Saint-Apollinaire : Vue aérienne Saint-A: Saint-Apollinaire: Aerial view of Saint-Apollinaire QC
Saint-Apollinaire est la municipalité la: Saint-Apollinaire is the most populous municipality in the Lotbinière MRC. It covers about 96 km² and borders Lévis to the east. It is about twenty kilometres from the Québec City bridges by Highway 20, and Route 273 runs through it from north to south.
Saint-Apollinaire se détache de Saint-An: Saint-Apollinaire separated from Saint-Antoine-de-Tilly in 1845. The parish was canonically established on November 23, 1853, and the abolition of the seigneurial system in 1854 made the seigneury of Gaspé disappear. The church, designed by François-Xavier and Prime Béland, was inaugurated on September 20, 1858.
Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures est l’une de: Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures is one of the three municipalities of the Québec City agglomeration, along with Québec City and L’Ancienne-Lorette. Its territory runs along the St. Lawrence for 12.3 km and extends about 10 km north, to the first slopes of the Laurentians. The population is concentrated in two areas: the centre, around the former village, and the Lac Saint-Augustin and Bocages area to the east.
Saint-Basile fait partie de la MRC de Po: Saint-Basile is part of the Portneuf MRC, in the Capitale-Nationale. It is bordered by Pont-Rouge to the east, Portneuf to the west, Saint-Raymond and Sainte-Christine-d’Auvergne to the north, and Cap-Santé to the south. Its territory of nearly 98 km² is mostly agricultural, with maple groves and the Portneuf River, joined by the Chaude River.
Saint-Bernard est située dans la plaine: Saint-Bernard is located on the St. Lawrence plain, about 35 km south of Québec City. The Chaudière River marks the southeast edge of the municipality for about twenty kilometres, and scenic Route 171 runs alongside it between Saint-Lambert-de-Lauzon and Scott. The rivière des Îles Brûlées crosses the territory from south to north, and the terrain is fairly flat.
Saint-Charles-de-Bellechasse est une mun: Saint-Charles-de-Bellechasse is a municipality in the Bellechasse MRC, about 20 km southeast of Lévis. Its name honours Saint Charles Borromeo and recalls the seigneur Charles Couillard. The Boyer River crosses the territory from southwest to northeast, and Lac Saint-Charles and Lac Beaumont are found there.
Saint-Damien compte une clinique médical: Saint-Damien has a medical clinic, two CPE facilities and a secondary school. Route 279 runs through the municipality, and the MRC offers on-demand public transport to Lévis, Montmagny and Sainte-Marie.
Saint-Damien-de-Buckland, souvent appelé: Saint-Damien-de-Buckland, often called Saint-Damien, is in the mountains of southern Bellechasse, east of Saint-Lazare-de-Bellechasse and southwest of Armagh. The rivière aux Billots runs through the village and joins the rivière des Abénaquis at the southwest boundary. The Parc des Bâtisseurs, a 1 km wooded corridor, crosses the heart of the village.
Saint-Elzéar est établie sur les bords d: Saint-Elzéar is set on the banks of the Beaurivage River, and the Nadeau and Savoie rivers also water its territory. The village crowns a hill, and the church grounds offer a view of the Chaudière valley and the Appalachians. It is 7 km from Sainte-Marie, near Saint-Bernard.
Saint-Ferréol-les-Neiges fait partie de: Saint-Ferréol-les-Neiges is part of the La Côte-de-Beaupré MRC, in the Capitale-Nationale. Its territory is watered by the Sainte-Anne River to the east and the Jean-Larose River to the west. The village neighbours Beaupré, Saint-Joachim and Saint-Tite-des-Caps.
Saint-Flavien couvre environ 66 km² au c: Saint-Flavien covers about 66 km² in the centre of the Lotbinière MRC, or about 4% of its territory. Rang Saint-Joseph (Route 271) crosses it from north to south, and Rang des Pointes from east to west. The village core is at their crossing, and Autoroute Jean-Lesage passes over a short segment to the northwest.
Saint-Flavien est électrifié en 1928. En: Saint-Flavien was electrified in 1928. In 1951, the La Station sector separated from the parish to become Laurier-Station. From 1980 to 1994, the Société québécoise d’initiatives pétrolières extracted natural gas from the subsoil, and the depleted deposit has been used since 1997 for seasonal gas storage. On December 29, 1999, the village and the parish again formed a single municipality.
Saint-François-de-la-Rivière-du-Sud est: Saint-François-de-la-Rivière-du-Sud is set on the banks of the rivière du Sud, east of Saint-Vallier and about 20 km southwest of Montmagny. The rivière du Sud crosses the territory, where it is joined by the bras Saint-Michel and the rivière Morigeau. The village is a few minutes from the river, south of Highway 20.
Saint-François-de-l’Île-d’Orléans fait p: Saint-François-de-l’Île-d’Orléans is part of the L’Île-d’Orléans MRC, in the Capitale-Nationale. Its triangle-shaped territory covers 16% of the island’s area, east of Sainte-Famille and Saint-Jean. Under the French Regime, the fief of Argentenay covered part of it.
Saint-Gabriel-de-Valcartier fait partie: Saint-Gabriel-de-Valcartier is part of the La Jacques-Cartier MRC, in the Capitale-Nationale. Its name joins that of the former seigneury of Saint-Gabriel to Valcartier, formed from val and Cartier, for the Jacques-Cartier River valley. The Sainte-Anne and Jacques-Cartier rivers cross its vast territory.
Saint-Gervais est une municipalité de la: Saint-Gervais is a municipality in the Bellechasse MRC, about 25 km southeast of Lévis. It is named after Saints Gervase and Protase, two martyrs celebrated on June 19. The bras Saint-Michel marks its northeast boundary, and the Boyer Sud River and the rivière du Moulin cross its territory.
Saint-Gervais est à environ 25 km de Lév: Saint-Gervais is about 25 km from Lévis. Route 279 connects the village to Saint-Charles-de-Bellechasse, then to Beaumont.
Saint-Henri, aussi appelée Saint-Henri-d: Saint-Henri, also called Saint-Henri-de-Lévis, is the most populous municipality in the Bellechasse MRC. It borders Lévis to the north and the La Nouvelle-Beauce MRC to the west. The Etchemin River crosses it from south to north, and the Pont Édouard-Brochu spans it in the village. The Boyer River runs through the east of the territory.
Saint-Isidore occupe l’extrémité nord-ou: Saint-Isidore occupies the northwest tip of the La Nouvelle-Beauce MRC, between the Chaudière and Etchemin rivers. It touches Saint-Henri to the north, Saint-Lambert-de-Lauzon to the west and Saint-Anselme to the east. The Chaudière River forms its western boundary, and the land rises gently to the southeast, from about 110 to 190 metres in elevation.
Saint-Jean-Baptiste se trouve du côté no: Saint-Jean-Baptiste is on the north side of the Québec City hill, at the top of the coteau Sainte-Geneviève, west of Old Québec, east of Montcalm and south of Saint-Roch. At 0.67 km², it is the smallest neighbourhood in the city, but also the densest. Rue Saint-Jean, lined with shops, bars and cafés, crosses it from east to west; Boulevard René-Lévesque brings together large hotels, office buildings and institutions.
Saint-Jean-Chrysostome est situé au sud: Saint-Jean-Chrysostome lies south of Saint-Romuald, east of Charny, north of Breakeyville and west of Pintendre. The Chaudière River borders it on the west and the Etchemin River on the east. Highways 20 and 73 run through it, as do Avenue Taniata and Route 175.
Saint-Jean-de-l’Île-d’Orléans fait parti: Saint-Jean-de-l’Île-d’Orléans is part of the MRC de L’Île-d’Orléans, in the Capitale-Nationale region. It stretches 11 km, from the Maheu River to the Dauphine River, which separates it from Saint-François. It is one of the largest municipalities on the island, and the Lafleur River also runs through it.
Saint-Joachim est une municipalité de pa: Saint-Joachim is a parish municipality in the MRC de La Côte-de-Beaupré, east of Beaupré. It forms the eastern limit of the Côte-de-Beaupré, at the foot of Cap Tourmente, and the Sainte-Anne River borders its northwest. It is one of the oldest settlement sites in Canada.
Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-De Lévy corres: Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-De Lévy corresponds to the territory of the former parish municipality, south of Lauzon and north of Pintendre. Autoroute Jean-Lesage (20) runs through it. Chemin Harlaka, Chemin Saint-Roch, Chemin des Forts and Route Monseigneur-Bourget cross it.
Saint-Lambert-de-Lauzon s’étend sur près: Saint-Lambert-de-Lauzon covers nearly 110 km², on both sides of the Chaudière River. Its population is spread between the village, the wooded Parc-Boutin area to the west, and the Domaine-des-Érables and Place-des-Îles areas, along the Chaudière. The rest of the territory, fairly flat, is given over to agriculture and forest.
Saint-Laurent-de-l’Île-d’Orléans fait pa: Saint-Laurent-de-l’Île-d’Orléans is part of the MRC de L’Île-d’Orléans, in the Capitale-Nationale region. On the south shore of the island, the village stretches along the foot of a hillside overlooking the Côte-du-Sud. Its maritime character shows in the wharf, the maritime park and the yacht club, which can host nearly 150 boats.
Saint-Lazare est à une trentaine de minu: Saint-Lazare is about thirty minutes from Lévis by Route 279. The MRC de Bellechasse offers on-demand public transit to Lévis, Montmagny and Sainte-Marie.
Saint-Lazare-de-Bellechasse occupe le ce: Saint-Lazare-de-Bellechasse occupies the centre of the MRC de Bellechasse, of which it is the seat. It is bordered by Saint-Gervais to the north, Honfleur to the northwest, Sainte-Claire to the west, Saint-Malachie to the southwest, Saint-Damien-de-Buckland to the southeast and Saint-Nérée-de-Bellechasse to the east. The Abénaquis River flows through the southeast of the territory.
Saint-Louis est l’un des sept quartiers: Saint-Louis is one of the seven neighbourhoods of the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough. The Québec and Pierre-Laporte bridges lead there, and the bridgehead area is served by Autoroutes Henri-IV and Duplessis and by Boulevards Laurier, Hochelaga and Champlain. Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois, Chemin Saint-Louis and Route de l’Église complete the network.
Saint-Malachie s’étend dans les collines: Saint-Malachie extends through the Appalachian hills, on both sides of the Etchemin River. The Desbarats, Pyke and Henderson rivers flow into the Etchemin there, and Lac des Cèdres and Lac Dion lie within the territory. Mont Kinsella and the Côte de la Crapaudière offer views over the valley.
Saint-Maxime devient le village de Scott: Saint-Maxime becomes the village of Scott
Saint-Michel occupe la partie de Beaupor: Saint-Michel occupies the part of Beauport north of its historic centre. It is bounded on the west by the Beauport River and the Charlesbourg borough, on the south by Autoroute Félix-Leclerc, on the north by Boulevard Louis-XIV and on the east by the former limestone quarries. Rue Seigneuriale, Boulevard Raymond and Avenue Saint-Michel are its main arteries; big-box stores and a 16-screen cinema line the highway.
Saint-Michel-de-Bellechasse est une muni: Saint-Michel-de-Bellechasse is a municipality in the MRC de Bellechasse, on the south shore of the St. Lawrence, between Saint-Vallier and Beaumont. The Boyer River flows almost through the centre of the territory and empties into the river opposite Île d’Orléans. The village core lines up white-painted wooden houses with coloured roofs and flowered galleries. Its many maples earned it the nickname Village of Trees.
Saint-Narcisse-de-Beaurivage couvre envi: Saint-Narcisse-de-Beaurivage covers about 61 km² in the east of the MRC de Lotbinière, 22 km from Saint-Agapit and 8 km from Saint-Bernard. The Bras d’Henri and the Petit bras d’Henri cross its territory, which is part of the Chaudière River basin. The local network includes Rue Principale and several rangs, including Rang Iberville and Rang Saint-Thomas.
Saint-Nicolas est l’un des trois secteur: Saint-Nicolas is one of the three sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough. Set on a promontory overlooking the river, it extends about 19 km along the St. Lawrence, to the Chaudière River in the east. Three residential zones can be distinguished: Bernières and the bridges in the east, the Stastny golf area in the centre and the old village in the west.
Saint-Nérée-de-Bellechasse occupe le cen: Saint-Nérée-de-Bellechasse occupies the centre of the MRC de Bellechasse, 23 km south of Saint-Vallier. It is surrounded by Saint-Raphaël to the north, Saint-Gervais to the west and Armagh to the east. Lacs Chabot, André, Pierre-Paul and à Achille are its main bodies of water, and the Abénaquis River rises in the south of the territory.
Saint-Patrice-de-Beaurivage : Vue du vil: Saint-Patrice-de-Beaurivage: Vue du village de Saint-Patrice-de-Beaurivage
Saint-Patrice-de-Beaurivage occupe envir: Saint-Patrice-de-Beaurivage covers about 86 km² in the eastern part of the MRC de Lotbinière, between Saint-Narcisse-de-Beaurivage to the north and Saint-Sylvestre to the south. Its hilly territory is crossed by the Beaurivage River and by the Filkars River, which flows into it. Route 269 passes through the village.
Saint-Pierre-de-la-Rivière-du-Sud est un: Saint-Pierre-de-la-Rivière-du-Sud is a parish municipality of the Côte-du-Sud, between Montmagny and Saint-François-de-la-Rivière-du-Sud. The Rivière du Sud runs along its northern boundary and makes the land in this area fertile. The Morigeau and des Poitras rivers and the ruisseau de la Blague complete the river network.
Saint-Pierre-de-l’Île-d’Orléans fait par: Saint-Pierre-de-l’Île-d’Orléans is part of the MRC de L’Île-d’Orléans, in the Capitale-Nationale region. The municipality lies between Sainte-Pétronille to the southwest and Sainte-Famille to the northeast, from which it is separated by the Pot au Beurre River. The Île-d’Orléans Bridge touches the island there, and its opening in 1935 made the locality more populated and less agricultural.
Saint-Raphaël est née en 1993 de la fusi: Saint-Raphaël was born in 1993 from the merger of the parish and the village of the same name. The Rivière du Sud runs through the territory, joined by the Petite rivière Sainte-Marguerite, and the Bras Saint-Michel crosses its northwest. The church, at 86 Rue Principale, forms the core of the village along with the presbytery, the cemetery and the former convent.
Saint-Raymond est à environ 10 km et Qué: Saint-Raymond is about 10 km away and Québec City about 40 km. The Vélopiste Jacques-Cartier/Portneuf runs through the town and joins the Corridor des Cheminots toward Québec City.
Saint-Raymond s’étend de part et d’autre: Saint-Raymond extends on both sides of the Sainte-Anne River, in the heart of the MRC de Portneuf. The urban core, in the hollow of the valley, has about 3,000 residents. The rest of the population lives in hamlets such as Bourg-Louis and Chute-Panet, residential neighbourhoods and vacation areas around the lakes.
Saint-Roch est l’un des plus anciens fau: Saint-Roch is one of the oldest suburbs of Québec City. In the early 17th century, Champlain envisioned a model city there named Ludovica. In 1620, the Récollets built a convent on the banks of the Saint-Charles River, the future first Hôpital général of the city. In 1692, they built a chapel dedicated to Saint Roch, which then gave its name to the street, the suburb, the parish, founded in 1829, and then the neighbourhood.
Saint-Roch se trouve dans la basse-ville: Saint-Roch is in the Lower Town, at the foot of the Québec City hill. Rue Saint-Joseph Est, reopened to the sky, is its shopping street; Boulevard Charest and Rues de la Couronne and Dorchester bring together offices and shops. The Gare du Palais is nearby.
Saint-Rodrigue occupe le sud de l’arrond: Saint-Rodrigue occupies the south of the Charlesbourg borough, alongside Autoroutes Laurentienne and Félix-Leclerc. 1re Avenue crosses it from north to south; Boulevard de l’Atrium and 55e Rue are its other main arteries. The neighbourhood is mostly apartment buildings of fewer than five storeys.
Saint-Romuald : Bibliothèque Lauréat-Val: Saint-Romuald: Lauréat-Vallière Library and Saint-Romuald City Hall
Saint-Romuald est l’un des quatre secteu: Saint-Romuald is one of the four sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough. It is bounded on the north by the river and on the south by Autoroute Jean-Lesage (Autoroute 20), and Route 132 runs through it. The mouths of the Chaudière and the Etchemin are there; the historic Chaudière-Bassin area became known for the timber trade and shipbuilding in the mid-19th century.
Saint-Romuald-d’Etchemin devient ville e: Saint-Romuald-d'Etchemin became a town in 1963 and merged with Saint-Télesphore in 1965. In 1969, an oil refinery, today the Jean-Gaulin refinery, was established on the former territory of Saint-Télesphore. The Pierre-Laporte Bridge, completed in 1970, made part of Saint-Romuald a suburb of Québec City. The town took the name Saint-Romuald in 1982, then was merged into the new city of Lévis on January 1, 2002.
Saint-Rédempteur est l’un des trois sect: Saint-Rédempteur is one of the three sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough. The smallest former municipality in the MRC des Chutes-de-la-Chaudière, it covers about 3.8 km². It lies on the west bank of the Chaudière, at the confluence of the Beaurivage, between Saint-Nicolas to the west and Charny to the east, about 17 km from Québec City.
Saint-Sacrement : Snow-covered Saint-Sac: Saint-Sacrement: Snow-covered Saint-Sacrement district in Quebec City
Saint-Sacrement occupe l’ouest de la par: Saint-Sacrement occupies the west of the part of La Cité-Limoilou located on the Québec City hill. It is bordered on the east by Avenue Joffre and Avenue Belvédère, on the south by Boulevard René-Lévesque, on the west by Avenue Painchaud and on the north by the Sainte-Geneviève hillside. Chemin Sainte-Foy, between Avenue Saint-Sacrement and Rue Eymard, is its only commercial artery; Boulevard de l'Entente and Avenue Holland complete the main routes.
Saint-Sauveur se trouve dans la basse-vi: Saint-Sauveur is in Lower Town, west of Saint-Roch. Rue Saint-Vallier Ouest, Boulevard Charest Ouest and Boulevard Langelier are its main routes; the Scott and Marie-de-l'Incarnation bridges connect it to the north, over the Saint-Charles River.
Saint-Sylvestre : Rue Principale (route: Saint-Sylvestre: Rue Principale (west route) in Saint-Sylvestre-de-Beaurivage
Saint-Sylvestre est la plus au sud des 1: Saint-Sylvestre is the southernmost of the 18 municipalities of the Lotbinière RCM. At about 148 km², it is the third largest in the RCM, and its hilly terrain rises on the first foothills of the Appalachians. Mont Sainte-Marguerite, nicknamed Mont Radar, is its highest peak.
Saint-Tite-des-Caps fait partie de la MR: Saint-Tite-des-Caps is part of the La Côte-de-Beaupré RCM, in the Capitale-Nationale region. Its terrain is rugged and largely wooded. The Sainte-Anne River borders the territory, which is also crossed by the Lombrette River.
Saint-Vallier s’étend sur la rive sud du: Saint-Vallier extends along the south shore of the St. Lawrence, 8 km east of Saint-Michel-de-Bellechasse and across from Île d'Orléans. The Boyer River marks the northwest limit of the territory before flowing into the river. The rivière des Mères runs through it and empties into the anse de Bellechasse. The village belongs to the Association des plus beaux villages du Québec.
Saint-Émile est entouré de boisés; une l: Saint-Émile is surrounded by woods; a power line and a golf course border it to the south. Avenue Lapierre runs through it from north to south and Rue de la Faune from east to west; Rue Vézina completes its main arteries. The terrain varies between 110 and 230 m, dominated by Le Rocher, and the ruisseau de la Montagne Saint-Charles runs along the east of the neighbourhood.
Saint-Étienne-de-Lauzon est l’un des tro: Saint-Étienne-de-Lauzon is one of the three sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough. Crossed by the Beaurivage River, it is bordered to the east by the Chaudière River. It touches Saint-Nicolas to the north and Saint-Rédempteur to the northeast, as well as Saint-Lambert-de-Lauzon, Saint-Gilles, Saint-Agapit and Saint-Apollinaire to the south and west.
Sainte Brigitte d’Irlande, patronne de l: Saint Brigid of Ireland, patron of the parish erected in 1863, recalls the Irish origin of the first settlers. Laval refers to François de Montmorency-Laval, the first owner of the seigneury of Beaupré.
Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré fait partie de la: Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré is part of the La Côte-de-Beaupré RCM, in the Capitale-Nationale region. The population lives mostly on a narrow strip of shoreline, less than a kilometre wide, at the foot of terraces about a hundred metres high. Farther north, the territory reaches the first peaks of the Laurentians, and the rivière aux Chiens crosses it to the river.

Sur la Rive-Sud, dans la MRC de La Nouve: On the South Shore, in the La Nouvelle-Beauce RCM in Chaudière-Appalaches, between the Chaudière and Etchemin rivers. The village neighbours Saint-Isidore and is 14 km from Saint-Anselme.
On the South Shore, in the La Nouvelle-Beauce RCM in Chaudière-Appalaches, between the Chaudière and Etchemin rivers. The village is about 10 km east of Sainte-Marie.
On the South Shore, in the La Nouvelle-Beauce RCM in Chaudière-Appalaches, 12 km north of Sainte-Marie and about 45 km from Québec City. It neighbours Sainte-Hénédine and Frampton.
On the South Shore, in the La Nouvelle-Beauce MRC in Chaudière-Appalaches, 7 km from Sainte-Marie and 56 km from Québec City. The village is built on a hill, near the Beaurivage River.
On the South Shore, in the La Nouvelle-Beauce MRC in Chaudière-Appalaches, about 35 km south of Québec City. The Chaudière River borders the southeast of the territory.

On the South Shore, in the La Nouvelle-Beauce RCM in Chaudière-Appalaches, about 35 km from Québec City. The territory extends on both banks of the Chaudière River, between Saint-Isidore, Sainte-Hénédine, Saint-Bernard and Sainte-Marie.
On the South Shore, in the La Nouvelle-Beauce MRC in Chaudière-Appalaches, about fifteen kilometres south of Lévis. The municipality extends east of the Chaudière River.
Sur la Rive-Sud, dans la MRC de Lotbiniè: On the South Shore, in the Lotbinière MRC, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The municipality is south of Saint-Apollinaire and the Bernières sector of Lévis, on the banks of the Noire River.
On the South Shore, in the Lotbinière MRC, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The municipality is about 20 minutes from Lévis and 30 minutes from Québec City.
On the South Shore, in the Lotbinière MRC, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The municipality borders Lévis to the east and is about 20 km from the Québec City bridges.
On the South Shore, in the Lotbinière RCM, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The village is 11 km south of Autoroute 20, via exit 278, on Routes 116 and 271.
On the South Shore, in the Lotbinière MRC, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The village is 7 km from Laurier-Station on Route 271 and about 40 km from the Québec bridges.
Sur la Rive-Sud, dans la MRC de Montmagn: On the South Shore, in the MRC de Montmagny in Chaudière-Appalaches, between Montmagny and Saint-François-de-la-Rivière-du-Sud. The Rivière du Sud runs along the north of its territory.
On the South Shore, in the Montmagny MRC in Chaudière-Appalaches, about 20 km southwest of Montmagny. The village borders the rivière du Sud, south of Highway 20.
Sur la Rive-Sud, dans la partie est de l: On the South Shore, in the eastern part of the MRC de Lotbinière, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The municipality lies between Saint-Narcisse-de-Beaurivage to the north and Saint-Sylvestre to the south, on Route 269.
Sur la Rive-Sud, dans l’arrondissement L: On the South Shore, in the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough of the city of Lévis, south of Saint-Romuald and east of Charny, between the Chaudière and Etchemin rivers.
Sur la Rive-Sud, dans l’est de la MRC de: On the South Shore, in the east of the MRC de Lotbinière, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The village is about 20 minutes from the Québec bridges, 22 km from Saint-Agapit and 8 km from Saint-Bernard.
Sur la Rive-Sud, le long de la rivière C: On the South Shore, along the Chaudière River, south of Charny, in the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough of the city of Lévis.
Sur la Rive-Sud, à environ 5 km au sud d: On the South Shore, about 5 km south of central Lévis, on both sides of Route 173, in the Desjardins borough of the City of Lévis.
Sur la Rive-Sud, à l’extrémité sud-est d: On the South Shore, at the southeastern end of the Lotbinière RCM, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The village is 6 km south of Saint-Patrice-de-Beaurivage, 23 km from Sainte-Marie and 37 km from Thetford Mines.
Sur la colline de Québec, à l’ouest de M: On the Québec City hill, west of Montcalm, between the Sainte-Geneviève hillside and Boulevard René-Lévesque, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough. It also borders Saint-Sauveur and the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough.

On the Québec City hill, west of Montcalm, between the Sainte-Geneviève hillside and Boulevard René-Lévesque. Chemin Sainte-Foy is its only commercial artery; the Église du Très-Saint-Sacrement and Cégep Garneau are neighbourhood landmarks.
Sur la côte nord-est de l’île d’Orléans,: On the northeast coast of Île d'Orléans, between Saint-Pierre and Saint-François, facing the Côte-de-Beaupré. It is the seat of the L'Île-d'Orléans RCM.
On the northeast coast of Île d'Orléans, facing the Île d'Orléans channel and the Côte-de-Beaupré. Chemin Royal (Route 368) runs through the municipality, between Saint-Pierre and Saint-François.
Sur la côte sud de l’île d’Orléans, entr: On the south shore of Île d’Orléans, between Saint-Laurent and Saint-François, facing the Grands Voiliers channel. Chemin Royal (Route 368) runs along the river and through the village.
On the south shore of Île d’Orléans, between Saint-Laurent and Saint-François. The village is about 26 km as the crow flies northeast of Québec City.
Sur la côte sud de l’île d’Orléans, à en: On the south shore of Île d’Orléans, about 11 km east of Sainte-Pétronille. The municipality is part of the MRC de L’Île-d’Orléans.

On the south shore of Île d’Orléans, about 11 km east of Sainte-Pétronille. The village stretches along the foot of a hillside, facing the Côte-du-Sud, and Chemin Royal (Route 368) runs along the river.
Sur la rive est de la rivière Chaudière,: On the east bank of the Chaudière River, not far from the Québec Bridge, in the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough. The Joffre rail yard and the Charny station mark the area; Parc des Chutes-de-la-Chaudière borders the river.
On the east bank of the Chaudière River, not far from the Québec Bridge, in Lévis. It is one of the four sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough.
Sur la rive nord du Saint-Laurent, à env: On the north shore of the St. Lawrence, about 30 km west of downtown Québec City, in the Portneuf MRC. The town lies between Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures and Donnacona.
On the north shore of the St. Lawrence, about 30 km west of downtown Québec City. Route 138, the Chemin du Roy, crosses the town, and Rue des Érables forms the heart of the old village.
Sur la rive nord du Saint-Laurent, à l’e: On the north shore of the St. Lawrence, at the mouth of the Jacques-Cartier River, west of Québec City. Autoroute 40 runs along the town, and the Chemin du Roy runs through it.
Sur la rive nord du Saint-Laurent, à l’o: On the north shore of the St. Lawrence, west of Québec City. Route 138 serves as the main street of the central sector, and Highway 40 crosses the city from east to west.
On the north shore of the St. Lawrence, west of Québec City. The city neighbours the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough to the east and Neuville to the west.
Sur la rive ouest de la rivière Chaudièr: On the west bank of the Chaudière River, at the confluence of the Beaurivage, in the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough. Route des Rivières crosses the area; Charny is on the other bank and the bridges to Québec City are less than 5 km away.

On the west bank of the Chaudière River, at the confluence of the Beaurivage, between Saint-Nicolas and Charny. It is one of the three sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough, in Lévis.
Sur la rive sud du Saint-Laurent, dans l: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, in the Bellechasse RCM in Chaudière-Appalaches. The village is 8 km east of Saint-Michel-de-Bellechasse, facing Île d'Orléans, and Highway 20 has an exit there (356).
On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, in the MRC de Bellechasse, between Beaumont and Saint-Vallier, facing Île d’Orléans. Route 132 runs through the village.
On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, in the Lotbinière MRC, in Chaudière-Appalaches. The village is about 25 km from Québec City by Route 132, just west of Lévis.
On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, in the Montmagny MRC in Chaudière-Appalaches, about 60 km east of Québec City. The village faces the northeastern tip of Île d’Orléans.
Sur la rive sud du Saint-Laurent, en Cha: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, in Chaudière-Appalaches. It is the seat of the Lotbinière RCM, about fifty kilometres west of Québec City, across from Portneuf, Cap-Santé and Donnacona.
Sur la rive sud du Saint-Laurent, en fac: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, across from Québec City. Boulevard Guillaume-Couture (Route 132) is its main commercial artery.
Sur la rive sud du Saint-Laurent, face à: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, facing Sillery, in the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough. Chemin du Fleuve runs along the shore and is home to Lévis city hall; the Chaudière and Etchemin rivers flow into the St. Lawrence there.
On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, facing Sillery, between the Chaudière and Etchemin rivers. It is one of the four sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Est borough, in Lévis.
Sur la rive sud du Saint-Laurent, à envi: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, about 15 km east of Lévis, at the northwest end of the Bellechasse MRC. Autoroute 20 crosses the municipality south of the village.
Sur la rive sud du Saint-Laurent, à l’ou: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, west of the Chaudière River, in the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough. Route Marie-Victorin runs along the river and Route des Rivières crosses the area; the Québec and Pierre-Laporte bridges are very close.

On the south shore of the St. Lawrence, west of the Chaudière River, in Lévis. It is one of the three sectors of the Les Chutes-de-la-Chaudière-Ouest borough, along with Saint-Rédempteur and Saint-Étienne-de-Lauzon.
Sur la rive sud du fleuve Saint-Laurent,: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence River, directly across from Québec City, in the Chaudière-Appalaches region. The city stretches between Beaumont, to the east, and Saint-Antoine-de-Tilly, to the west.
Sur le formulaire obligatoire du Tribuna: On the mandatory form of the Tribunal administratif du logement, with electronic signature.

Une église plus vaste est construite à p: A larger church was built starting in 1872, and the Redemptorists took charge of the shrine in 1877. In 1895, the Cyclorama of Jerusalem, an immense panoramic canvas, was installed in the town.

Vanier est délimité approximativement pa: Vanier is roughly bounded by Avenue Godin to the west, the Saint-Charles River to the south, Autoroute Laurentienne to the east and Autoroute Félix-Leclerc to the north. Boulevard Pierre-Bertrand and Avenue Plante run through it from north to south, and Boulevard Wilfrid-Hamel from east to west. A residential area is surrounded by the Cardinal industrial park to the north and west, and by a commercial and institutional zone to the east that includes Fleur de Lys.
Vers 1695, les Jésuites font construire: Around 1695, the Jesuits had a flour mill built on the banks of the ruisseau du Moulin; destroyed by fire in 1948, it gave its name to Avenue du Vieux-Moulin. In 1759, the Marquis de Montcalm set up his headquarters near a redoubt built on the Giffard hillside. In 1785, a new seigneurial mill was built on the west bank of the Beauport River, near its mouth.
Vers 1696, le chemin de Charlesbourg, l’: Around 1696, the Chemin de Charlesbourg, today’s 1re Avenue, was extended north as the rang Saint-Pierre, now Boulevard Henri-Bourassa. The rang links the Trait-Carré de Charlesbourg to the future neighbourhood and separates two cleared areas: Saint-Pierre, to the west, and Saint-Claude, to the east. The Élie and Joubert families were the first to settle there.
Vers 1825, la paroisse demande une églis: Around 1825, the parish asked for a larger church; architect Thomas Baillairgé drew up the plans in 1827. The current church was consecrated on May 25, 1830, and the first one was demolished in 1836 to make room for the cemetery. The current presbytery dates from 1875. In 1919, Parc du Sacré-Cœur was blessed; its central statue is a work by Alfred Laliberté.
Vers 1830, des colons s’établissent dans: Around 1830, settlers established themselves in the 5th, 6th, 7th and 9th concessions of the seigneury of Livaudière, then attached to Saint-Gervais. Too far from the church, they met at Notary Roy’s on April 24, 1831 and asked for a new parish.
Vers 1840, des Irlandais catholiques s’i: Around 1840, Irish Catholics settled in the backcountry, the Concessions, but the poor soil drove them away. French-Canadian families replaced them the following decade. The present church was built in 1866, the old convent in 1907, and Château-Richer gained town status in 1968.
Vers 1840, environ 200 familles catholiq: Around 1840, about 200 Catholic families from Ireland settled in Saint-Patrice and Saint-Sylvestre. The seigneur Arthur Ross had a French-inspired manor built, which still stands. In the spring of 1860, without agreement from the archdiocese, the settlers built a chapel themselves on land donated by the seigneur.
Vers 1845 naît Boisseauville, lotie sur: Around 1845, Boisseauville was born, subdivided from the former Bois-Bijou estate. The shipyards, the timber trade and the port attracted a large workforce, and the building rules there allowed houses that were not fireproof. After the Saint-Roch fire of 1845, many families settled there. The neighbourhood received its municipal charter in 1862 and took the name Saint-Sauveur in 1872.
Vers 1850, environ un millier de personn: Around 1850, about a thousand people lived there and asked for their own parish. Archbishop Pierre-Flavien Turgeon canonically erected it on March 20, 1852, from parts of Sainte-Marguerite, Sainte-Claire and Sainte-Marie. The name pays tribute to Catherine-Hénédine Dionne, widow of the seigneur Pierre-Elzéar Taschereau, who contributed to the building of the church. The parish municipality was created in 1855.
Vers 1850, le chemin de fer facilite l’a: Around 1850, the railway made the area easier to reach, attracting vacationers. Cottages multiplied, notably at Château-d’Eau, created in 1926 and then attached to Loretteville in 1965. The first drinking water main to Québec City, drawn from the Saint-Charles River, was laid in 1854, and the present water tower was built in 1949.
Vers 1870 à 1872, un moulin à eau est bâ: Around 1870 to 1872, a water mill was built of limestone on the banks of the Jacques-Cartier. This mill, the Marcoux mill, operated until it went bankrupt in 1910, then became a theatre and movie house in 1918. In 1911, the parish split in two: the village of Pont-Rouge and the parish of Sainte-Jeanne-de-Pont-Rouge.
Vers 1900, les frères Luc et Jean-Baptis: Around 1900, brothers Luc and Jean-Baptiste Pelletier settled in the locality. Luc Pelletier’s sawmill, powered by logs floated down from the forests of Lac-Beauport and Stoneham, gave rise to a timber industry. In 1909, the parish was established on June 15, and the parish municipality of Notre-Dame-des-Laurentides was founded; Luc Pelletier became its first mayor.
Vers 1934, Thomas Maher achète tout le p: Around 1934, Thomas Maher bought the entire perimeter of the lake’s north basin. He had a ring road built and sold the lots between the road and the shore. Within a few years, most found buyers, and cottages multiplied.

À Québec, le système de chauffage doit p: In Québec City, the heating system must be able to maintain at least 20 °C in the unit, measured in the centre of the room one metre above the floor. Adjoining spaces must stay at 15 °C or higher, and the unit must be supplied with hot and cold water[3].
À Québec, les gestionnaires facturent le: In Québec City, managers most often charge a percentage of the rent collected. Québec firms publish ranges of roughly 4% to 11% depending on the type of building and the scope of service[1][2][3], plus leasing fees that often run from 50% to 100% of one month’s rent[1][2]. These fees are deductible from rental income[4].
À comparer : baisser le loyer de 25 $ pa: For comparison: lowering the rent by $25 a month to rent 30 days sooner costs $300 over a year, versus about $1,410 for an empty month.
À environ 25 km au nord-ouest de Québec,: About 25 km northwest of Québec City, in the La Jacques-Cartier RCM, of which it is the seat. It neighbours Canadian Forces Base Valcartier and Sainte-Catherine-de-la-Jacques-Cartier.
About 25 km northwest of Québec City, on the Jacques-Cartier River, near Canadian Forces Base Valcartier. Shannon is the seat of the La Jacques-Cartier RCM.
À la fin des années 1990, la Ville lance: In the late 1990s, the City launched a revitalization program. The mall was demolished from 2000 to 2007, façades were renovated and former factories became offices, artists’ studios or housing co-operatives. IT and video game companies set up around Boulevard Charest. Between 1996 and 2017, the number of people working in the neighbourhood rose by 40%.
À la fin du XVIIe siècle, des Hurons-Wen: At the end of the 17th century, Huron-Wendat people settled on the banks of the Rivière Saint-Charles, after leaving their site at Lorette, now L’Ancienne-Lorette. Their village, founded in 1697, is present-day Wendake, enclosed within the neighbourhood. This settlement is the source of the name Jeune-Lorette, taken up by the parish of Saint-Ambroise-de-la-Jeune-Lorette.
À la pointe nord-est de l’île d’Orléans,: At the northeast tip of Île d’Orléans, facing the îles Madame and the Ruau, some 40 km downriver from Québec City. Chemin Royal (Route 368) goes around the tip of the island.
At the northeast tip of Île d’Orléans, some 40 km downriver from Québec City. The municipality borders Sainte-Famille and Saint-Jean and faces the îles Madame and the Ruau.
À la pointe sud-ouest de l’île d’Orléans: At the southwest tip of Île d'Orléans, in the L'Île-d'Orléans RCM. The village faces Old Québec and Lévis, and borders Saint-Pierre and Saint-Laurent.
At the southwest tip of Île d'Orléans, facing Old Québec and Lévis. Chemin Royal (Route 368) runs through the village, which overlooks the river and Montmorency Falls.
À la signature, le propriétaire doit ind: At signing, the landlord must state the lowest rent paid in the previous 12 months, in section G of the lease. If the new rent is higher, the tenant can ask the TAL to set it within 10 days of signing, or within 2 months of the start of the lease if the information was not given or is false[5].
À l’automne 1943, des skieurs bénévoles: In the fall of 1943, volunteer skiers from Québec City and Beaupré opened a first trail on Mont Sainte-Anne. The resort was inaugurated on January 16, 1966, then owned by the Town of Beaupré, and the Government of Québec took possession in 1970. The paper mill, which dated from 1927, closed in 2009.
À l’est de Québec, sur la rive est de la: East of Québec City, on the east bank of the Montmorency River, where it meets the St. Lawrence. Avenue Royale and Boulevard Sainte-Anne cross it from west to east.
East of the city, along the river. Avenue Royale crosses Vieux-Beauport; the Montmorency Falls mark the eastern limit.
À l’est du secteur de Limoilou, dans l’a: East of the Limoilou sector, in the La Cité-Limoilou borough, between the St. Lawrence River and Autoroute Félix-Leclerc. It borders the Beauport borough.
À l’est du secteur de Limoilou, entre le: East of the Limoilou sector, between the St. Lawrence River and Autoroute Félix-Leclerc, on the edge of the Beauport borough. Chemin de la Canardière and Boulevard Henri-Bourassa are the main routes; the Domaine de Maizerets and the Hôpital de l’Enfant-Jésus are neighbourhood landmarks.
À l’extrémité est de Beauport, à l’embou: At the eastern end of Beauport, at the mouth of the Montmorency River, in the Chutes-Montmorency neighbourhood.
À l’extrémité est de la Côte-de-Beaupré,: At the eastern end of the Côte-de-Beaupré, at the foot of Cap Tourmente. Avenue Royale, lined with old houses, runs through the village and leads to the national wildlife area.
At the eastern end of the Côte-de-Beaupré, east of Beaupré, at the foot of Cap Tourmente. It is reached by Route 138 East, then Avenue Royale.
À l’extrémité ouest de la colline de Qué: At the western tip of the Québec City hill, in the former city of Sainte-Foy, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough. The Cap-Rouge neighbourhood lies to the west.
At the western tip of the Québec City hill, in the former city of Sainte-Foy. Boulevard Pie-XII and Chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois cross it; Rue du Campanile and the Boisé de Marly are landmarks.
À l’origine, le territoire de Pintendre: Originally, Pintendre’s territory was part of Lévis territory. The place name “Pain Tendre” first appears in a notarial deed on November 28, 1757. It is found again in 1797 on a map of the village of “Pain Tendre” drawn by Jeremiah McCarthy. The name then evolved into Pin Tendre, then Pintendre.
À l’ouest de Sainte-Foy, dans la vallée: West of Sainte-Foy, in the Cap Rouge River valley, all the way to the St. Lawrence. Rue Saint-Félix and Rue de la Promenade-des-Sœurs are major routes; the Cap-Rouge viaduct spans the valley.
À l’ouest de la ville de Québec, dans l’: In the west of Québec City, in the Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge borough. The neighbourhood stretches from the St. Lawrence River in the south to Autoroute Félix-Leclerc in the north.
À l’ouest de la ville. On y trouve le ca: West of the city. It is home to the Université Laval campus and the shopping centres of Boulevard Laurier.
À l’échelle de Lévis, 34,1 % des ménages: Across Lévis, 34.1% of households were tenants at the 2021 census. The Davie shipyard, still in operation, has the largest dry dock in Canada. Parc de la Paix, a former military camp, the Guillaume Couture monument near the Saint-Joseph church, and the Guillaume-Couture secondary school mark the neighbourhood.

Across Lévis, 34.1% of households were tenants in the 2021 census. A bike path runs along the river on the mill’s former railway line and crosses an old forest of pines, ash, yellow birch and beech. The area also has a golf course, which hosted the Telus World Skins Game during Breakeyville’s centennial, and a summer equestrian competition.
À l’époque de la Nouvelle-France, le fie: In the days of New France, the fief of Bélair was granted to Guillaume Bonhomme in 1682, and the grant was ratified by Louis XIV on April 15, 1684. The fief included Mont Bélair and Lac Bonhomme. After Guillaume Bonhomme died in 1710, his children gradually sold their shares to the Jesuits; in 1800, the territory became British Crown land.
À l’étroit dans le Vieux-Québec, l’Unive: Cramped in Old Québec, Université Laval bought the Brophy sisters’ property in 1942, then more land in 1944. The architect-urban planner Édouard Fiset drew up the master plan for the university city, and work began in 1949, the year construction of Boulevard Laurier started. In the 1950s and 1960s, streets of bungalows and apartment buildings appeared around the campus.
À l’été 1759, les troupes britanniques s: In the summer of 1759, British troops settled at Pointe-Lévy. Their cannons, placed on the cliff, bombarded Québec City for 70 days. After the Battle of the Plains of Abraham, General Wolfe’s body was laid for a few hours in Église Saint-Joseph, which had been turned into a military hospital.
À partir de 1855, le territoire fait par: From 1855, the territory was part of the vast municipality of Saint-Charles-de-Charlesbourg, split up several times until 1952. In 1931, the Jardin zoologique du Québec opened its doors on the banks of the Rivière du Berger. After the river flooded in 1938, the site was redeveloped and new buildings were built there.
À partir de 1871, des familles canadienn: From 1871, French-Canadian families settled in place of the Irish and became the majority. The parish was canonically erected in 1873, and the municipality was created in 1874. An invasion of toads in 1873 is said to have given the place the nickname La Crapaudière.
À partir de 1940, les coopératives se mu: From 1940 on, cooperatives multiplied: agricultural in 1941, a bakery in 1943, a flour mill in 1949 and a garage in 1955. The village and the parish amalgamated in 1998. In 2005, Saint-Anselme celebrated its 175th anniversary, and in 2012, the former railway became a bike path.
